component_details.description: Incorporates a system of public messaging to enable the NS to share timely, accurate information before, during, and after a disaster or crisis.

component_responses.notes: По результатам самооценки компонент оценён как «1- Отсутствует». Это означает, что компонент в настоящее время отсутствует как полноценная система и требует разработки с нуля или серьёзного формирования. По индикаторам участники отметили: «да» — 2, «нет» — 8. Приоритизация: высокий приоритет. Компонент был включён в число ключевых направлений плана действий и должен рассматриваться как один из основных элементов последующего усиления готовности. В качестве доказательной базы/практических примеров участники ссылались на следующие элементы: Не закрепленны соответсвующими документами; Не закрепленны соответсвующими документами.

component_details.title: Resource Mobilisation
component_details.description: A documented strategy for raising domestic funds from the government, private sector, general public and other in-country actors to support the national society’s response. This would include allocation of responsibilities, practical mechanisms for accepting funds and for being accountable on funds.

component_responses.notes: По результатам самооценки компонент оценён как «2- Частично имеется». Это означает, что компонент частично имеется, но нуждается в существенной институционализации, документировании и практической проверке. По индикаторам участники отметили: «да» — 6, «нет» — 6. Приоритизация: низкий приоритет. В качестве доказательной базы/практических примеров участники ссылались на следующие элементы: Среди сотрудников НО точно распределены роли и ответственности между центральным офисом и региональными подразделениями; Координация деятельности по мобилизации ресурсов через профильные отделы и руководство НОКПТ.

component_details.title: RC auxiliary role, Mandate and Law
component_details.description: A constitutional reference to the role of the NS in responding to disasters and crises, which may be legislated or included/ recognized in the National Response System.

component_responses.notes: NS decided that this component is strong and missing elements will be included in the updated Strategic Plan in 2021, along with improvements in the policy review being currently conducted at a National level, in partnership with the National Disaster Office.

component_details.title: DRM Strategy
component_details.description: An outline of the overall goal that the NS seeks to achieve in its disaster and crisis response operations. The goal considers: context analysis, ongoing/regular all-hazards risk assessments: it may define the target proportion of affected population that will be reached, and a definition of the areas/sectors where a NS will usually respond during an emergency.

component_responses.notes: The DRM Strategy exists and includes references to the National Response Framework . However, the NS acknowledges that staff and volunteers do not know much about the DRM Plan. The Strategy is aligned with the National Response Framework and IFRC Disaster Management Strategic Framework for the Caribbean.

component_details.title: DRM Policy
component_details.description: Reflects the NS mission, RCRC principles and mandate. It acknowledges other relevant NS policies, and aligns with the government policy (where applicable), incorporating the general rules that the NS will obey in order to achieve something (i.e mandate, strategy, etc.)

component_responses.notes: The NS has its own DRM Policy which is aligned to the IFRC Disaster Management Strategic Framework for the Caribbean. Guiding priciples for values embedded in response approach is adopted from the IFRC's principles and NS's Mission and Vision Statements. It is inclusive and mentions the involvement of other critical sectors such as Community Disaster Response Teams, youth, first aid training & other departments. The NS agrees that for the policy to be more effective and adhered by all staff  and volunteers it has to be widely disseminated.

component_details.title: DRM Laws, Advocacy and Dissemination
component_details.description: Designed to support the NS in improving legal preparedness for disasters and crisis and to promote the use of the IDRL Guidelines in order to reduce human vulnerability.

component_responses.notes: The NS acknowledges the importance of IDRL humanitarian diplomacy, but has no active documented plan to drive related initiatives. However, the NS is actively working on building  stronger relationships with governmental partners to build visibility and operationality under national legislation. Although, the NS has no staff trained in IDRL & IHL to act as a focal point in an emergency, but has identified that it will fall under the remit of the DM Officer. The NS is currently working on advocacy for government enactment of legislation in line with the Model Act for the Facilitation and Regulation of International Disaster Relief and Initial Recovery Assistance, via National DRM Policy and Legislative consultation currently taking place by the National Disaster Office. NS is seen as a critical contributor.

component_details.title: Quality and accountability
component_details.description: Describes the essential elements of principled, accountable, and high-quality humanitarian action. The RCRC Movement provides support to the most vulnerable people in line with the Sphere and CHS standards, Code of Conduct for the RCRC Movement and NGOS in Disaster Relief and the Code for Good Partnership of the RCRC Movement, Gender & Diversity, inclusion and protection, BPI/ Do no harm, context-sensitive analysis, violence prevention, accountability to affected population and disability considerations, Community engagement and accountability (CEA).

component_responses.notes: The NS has mechanisms in place to ensure the affected populations are involved in all stages of the response. However, it does not have a CEA plan and safe and accessible feedback and complaints mechanisms in place. There are two CEA trained persons at Headquarters (HQ), but they are not established focal points and/or assigned to the role for branches, they are also volunteers and only based at HQ. The NS has developed beneficiary satisfaction surveys to allow safe and accessible feedback mechanisms for impacted communities. Creation of Hotline for impacted persons to gain feedback. The NS does not have Protection, Gender and Inclusion (PGI) policy documented to embed and streamline gender based interventions during assessment, planning and response. However, two (2) staff members have taken part in a recent PGIE training (December 2020), so that a policy can be drafted/developed. In the interim the NS follows the Minimum Standards for Protection, Gender and Inclusion in Emergencies, but no document exists to identify this in any existing response SOP.

component_details.title: Business continuity
component_details.description: A strategy to counter any potential or anticipated obstacles to effective functioning of the NS, with an eye to ensuring that personnel and assets are protected and able to function in the event of a disaster/crisis.

component_responses.notes: At present the NS donor procedures with projects to ensure business continuity. A BCP for COVID 19 exists but a multi-hazard plan is being developed and will take time

component_details.title: Emergency Response Procedures (SOPs)
component_details.description: Written guidelines that describe duties and rights of personnel, command structures, coordination with other organizations, and reporting requirements, etc. Includes detailed organogram, decision-making flow chart, and defined roles and responsibilities.

component_responses.notes: The NS has an EOC SOP which covers general operational procedures and protocols. It includes the responsibilities of staff, including both senior and operational management teams (inclusive of second in command should persons be unavailable). This SOP exists only at HQ and does not extend to the branch level. It is also not tailored to specific interventions and is not well known by staff and volunteers.

component_details.title: Response and recovery planning
component_details.description: A documented set of procedures for the disaster/crisis response and recovery process. Including use of local capacities, transition to recovery, type of activities and serivices provided during response and recovery activities and exit strategies, procedures for DREF & EA, and templates for planning, budgeting and accessing funds.

component_responses.notes: When needed, the NS develops response plans in accordance with IFRC standards and takes into consideration community and other relevant stakeholders. However, these plans are purely response based and do not incorporate risk analyisis or medium and long term recovery planning,

component_details.title: Pre-disaster meetings and agreements
component_details.description: A commitment to arrange meetings and agreements with Movement stakeholders and external actors to identify, plan for and address gaps for any upcoming disaster season (e.g. monsoon, floods or cyclones, or for any generic disaster/crisis event (e.g Epidemic, pandemic, confilict situations). Pre-disaster agreements should set out each partner's role in the event of a disaster/crisis.

component_responses.notes: This component was not seen as a priority component because it is being done under other modes of response and will be captured, so reviewing on its own will not beneficial at this time.

component_details.title: Hazard, Context and Risk Analysis, Monitoring and Early Warning
component_details.description: Describes how the NS monitors and maps past, present and potential hazards, disasters and crises (e.g. hazard, vulnerability assessments, gathering information from communities and government authorities) and systematically evaluates the damage that could be caused by a potential disaster/crisis, the frequency, severity of the impact, and the alert the relevant areas to scale the preparedness actions to reduce population vulnerability.

component_responses.notes: There is no risk monitoring focal point, but the DM Director and Coordinator are identified as Focal points, who are involved in levels of activation, which includes monitoring and early actions needed by the NS. Additionally, the NS has the capacity to collect and analyse primary and secondary hazard data /impact data in DANA and situation reports, but this is impact based and not done on a regular basis to facilitate the monitoring of trends, excluding trends collected and analysed through the analysis of the recovery assessments issued in July 2020 during the COVID-19 response. The NS has analysed its risk and barriers to its operations as proven through the identification of an alternate sites for Head Quarters due to identified hazards of the current location. TTRCS is a part of the national EWS development with national stakeholders. They do not have direct legal path to alert responders and affected population, but can activate early actions at the community level through community response teams; NS also participates in meetings held pre-impact for anticipated events (hurricanes) and receives updates from the authority of hydrometeorological hazards the Trinidad and Tobago Meteorological Office. The non-existence of a national multi-hazard risk analysis limits the updated information received and gathered through official means; therefore updated data is not shared as regular. Updates are project based and not done regularly; done in 2018 under Zika Project but not updated since then. There is intention to develop a policy to collect disaggregated data, not currently being collected.

component_details.title: Scenario planning
component_details.description: A set of practical operation plans that closely mirror the generic disaster or crisis response plan but are tailored to a specific hazard type (e.g. earthquake, dengue epidemic, floods, cyclone) and a specific scenario (i.e. number of people affected, their locations and other important factors).

component_responses.notes: The National Society decided that this is something that they will like to focus on the development of the data coming out of Hazard, Context and Risk Analysis, Monitoring and early warning so better scenario planning can be developed, also based on testing and learning experiences from Operational Capacity which was kept by the National Society.

component_details.title: Risk management
component_details.description: A mapping of the potential risks in every area, along with its related mitigation measures. Including financial, reputational, organizational risks etc.

component_responses.notes: There is a no assigned or designated focal point for risk management in the NS. However, there are assigned team leads as part of the EOC and Operations management team. Identifying, evaluating and accounting for operational risks are part of the NSs standard operations. NS regularly coordinates with the NDO and other disaster management authorities in exercising their duties to avoid duplication of efforts. There are systems in place eg procurement and mapping processes and audits, that are now built into donor proposals and agreements to safe guard against impropriety. The NS noted that there needs to be a shift from disaster response to crisis response and even the need to expand to crisis management. TTRCS has systems in place eg audits, procurement process and mapping, project audits included in proposals, finance manual. It was noted that such systems have improved from 2017 to now. TTRCS identified the need to make the shift from disaster response to crisis response, needs to be broaden to speak to crisis management.

component_details.title: Preparedness plans and budgets
component_details.description: Plans identifying organisational resources, determining roles and responsibilities, and developing policies, procedures and activities in order to reach a level of preparedness to be able to respond effectively to a disaster or crisis. Budgets ensure that the necessary financial support is secured to allow capacities to be built and readiness maintained.

component_responses.notes: The NS has a designated focal point for disaster preparedness. Gaps are identified through a post-mortem analysis of response strategies, but risk assessments are not carried out prior (as previously noted). Simulation exercises to test capability and identifying gaps do not take place annually or as often as the NS would like. In an effort to ensure operational preparedness, mitigation activities are conducted at HQ and branches. A recognised area of weakness for the NS is in financial preparedness. The NS is aware of emergency funding avenues through the Federation (eg DREF), but there are currently no emergency cash funds within the NS, though it is an aspiration.

The NS ensures participation of community representatives to reflect the needs and strengths of local population in the assessment, design, and planning of community-based preparedness activities. NS conducts regular awareness raising and public education on disasters or crises as a part of their CERT training sessions. Not all community based early warning and early action systems are in place. In 2019, the NS brought together multi-agencies for flood EWS. However, it is a work in progress to be multi-hazard. EWS Toolkits do exist in some vulnerable communities and there is a partnership with local government, who is responsible for checks on stock. Community Disaster Response Team (CDRTs) are trained and equipped to handle local response in partnership with relevant local actors and have contingency plans, again through CERT trainings with Ministry of Local Government. CDRTs are trained and equipped to handle local response in partnership with relevant local actors based on municipal plans. NS ensures no groups are excluded when conducting community assessment, with atleast one of the religious groups and women’s groups involved in a conflict sensitive way, when needed.

component_details.title: Mapping of NS capacities
component_details.description: A list of the NS capacities including HR (staff, response teams and volunteers) and equipment that are available for disaster/crisis response. Teams could include branch and national response teams. This should be defined by technical speciality where relevant.

component_responses.notes: The NS has a focal point identified and available for each specific area of intervention and services to provide technical guidance and support covered in National Disaster Plan and EOC SOPs. The staff and volunteers are trained and kept up to date, but the platform is not always used. Response materials and equipment database is up to date, excel sheet is kept and some items need to be updated on a broader basis and at branch level. The NS does not believe resources (HR and equipment) are available and sufficient to cover the initial response needs. However, NS has mapped levels of response according to National Response Framework and levels of Emergency Operation Centre activation. At level 3 of response, coordination with IFRC and NSs within the region and then mechanisms are in place to share resources amongst branches/regions, as needed.

component_details.title: Early Action Mechanisms
component_details.description: Designed to translate warnings into anticipatory actions to help reduce the impact of specific disaster or crisis events. They focus on consolidating available forecasting information and putting procedures in place to ensure that a NS can act ahead of any disaster/crisis. Forecast-based financing is included within the scope of this area.

component_responses.notes: This component is not apart of the NSs mandate, but they feel confident that with past responses they have done well. Work needs to be done to improve methodology, triggers etc to improve this component. The NS has early warning early action systems accepted as part of the national Early Warning Early Action strategies and preparedness system for hydro-met hazards, other hazards have to be worked on. The NS addresses any issues related to vulnerability, exposure and triggers  in the established Disaster Management Committee meetings before and after the disaster. NS has procedures and personnel permanently available, to communicate alerts and initiate early action to all levels of the NS by establishing alternative point of contacts(pocs), if first pocs become unavailable.

component_details.title: Cash Based Intervention (CBI)
component_details.description: An effective and flexible way, including all forms of cash and voucher-based assistance, to support people affected by emergencies, maintaining their dignity and choice, while fostering local economies. Cash should also be mainstreamed into other sectors (including Relief, shelter, livelihoods) and services (Logistics, Finance, etc.)

component_responses.notes: The NS does not have a CBI preparedness plan, but agreed this will be included in their Emergency SOPs. Noting that the CBI preparedness plan would address NS opportunities and barriers to be ready to provide scalable emergency CBI, this also will be considered in the NS Emergency SOPs and response plan. CBI Training was conducted for 12 staff and volunteers and records have been kept of persons as part of volunteer profiles for further support to CBI services for the NS. NS has to develop pre-disaster feasibility cash analysis and baseline about market systems, prices and seasonality, mapping of other actors and coordination structures.	It is hoped that this will be developed after train staff is engaged, then this can be achieved. The NS has regularly revised CBI SOPs with clear roles and responsibilities outlined at each stage of the response process, based on lessons learned from previous responses. Other elements of CBI are a work in progress and to be developed. NS understands they will lead this activity and coordinate with local agencies to provide CBI.

component_details.title: Emergency Needs Assessment
component_details.description: Assess the extent and impact of the damage caused by the disaster/crisis and the degree of vulnerability of the affected population. The first step in any emergency response, such an assessment will identify the needs that require external intervention and the gaps to be filled. It is a vital component of the programme-planning process.

component_responses.notes: The NS has standardised templates and trained multi-sectorial emergency assessment team available to deploy in a timely manner to collect and report on primary and secondary disaggregated data. It builds emergency plans on the needs assessment results. The needs assessment analyses secondary risk and specific needs of vulnerable people. NS never been placed in this situation to look at emergency needs assessments and take into consideration existing capacities and analyses the national and international capacities, responses and gaps. Also, the NS has never had to analyse secondary risk, specific needs/concerns of vulnerable people/coping mechanisms/early and self-recovery from emergency needs assessment. However, the NS is currently,  conducting this analysis for migrant population  by online and in person surveys done , focus groups also in pockets.

component_details.title: Affected population selection
component_details.description: Identification and selection of target Affected population for interventions, using a pre-defined set of criteria based on need and vulnerability. This includes consideration of specific vulnerabilities such as disability, age and gender.

component_responses.notes: The NS communicates selection criteria to the affected population using appropriate and established communication channels and involves community leaders/representatives. The selection criteria is made very clear and is printed, as well as distributed to make sure it is clearly identified to impacted persons. It identifies appropriate selection criteria based on existing vulnerability and taking into consideration gender, diversity, age and disabilities. Responders have been trained in data collection by using standardised templates, there is a mechanism to cross-check that data, and the NS protects data collected from affected population.

component_details.title: Emergency Operations Centre (EOC)
component_details.description: A central command and control facility responsible for carrying out disaster/crisis management functions at a strategic level in an emergency situation. The common functions are to collect and analyze data; facilitate decision making that protects life and livelihoods; and disseminate those decisions to all concerned agencies and individuals. Generally located at the headquarter level of an organization.

component_responses.notes: The NS has a formally appointed focal point for EOC and SOPs are being developed. EOC protocols are activated as needed and in coordination with the National Disaster Office’s (NDO’s) National Emergency Operations Centre (NEOC). The NS makes decisions based on situational analysis and there is clarity on authority at all levels. There is no designated EOC as it is not seen as needed since it works with the NDO and has a space at the NEOC.

component_details.title: Information Management (IM)
component_details.description: Ability to manage information including requesting, receiving, analyzing and disseminating as per its procedures and partner requirements (IFRC and public authorities in particular). There should be a clear digital/paper trail that documents what, when and how the NS has acted and provides key information for the development of Emergency Plan of Actions. Includes IM between levels, between departments and Situational Reports, mapping, visualisation of data, GO platform (IFRC).

component_responses.notes: The NS has key staff at HQ and branch level are familiar with IM templates, methodology and procedures, and have access to equipment to compile, visualise and share information. It has a system at HQ to store and share files with emergency personnel and recently purchased and set up a server for this purpose; branches will be given access once the intranet is set up. NS has collaborative relationship with Ministry of Social Development to access vulnerability data. However, information is not as forthcoming from Ministry of Health and disability information is difficult to access. Information and specific decisions are recorded in minutes at Board Meeting minutes, NS is also purchasing a server to systematically record decisions. Additionally, the NS documents has key information and decisions in the form of minutes which are used for information sharing across levels and sectors. It has a standardised Situation Report format and these reports are analysed to adapt response plans.

component_details.title: Testing and Learning
component_details.description: Drills and Simulations allow the organization to test, identify and learn from the results of these type of exercises and incorporate learning into future preparedness and response planning.

component_responses.notes: The NS includes branches in drills, but it is not hazard specific as featured in the current response plan. Lessons are drawn from drills, simulations and responses inform revisions in the emergency procedures, but mainly through After Action Review sessions. TTRCS does include access, acceptance, security and the practical application of the Fundamental Principles in their simulations and drills. NS conducts cross-border simulations in relevant contexts and simulations are conducted in partnership with national authorities and other organisations.

component_details.title: Activation of regional and international support
component_details.description: Procedures for requesting and accepting regional and international support in operations, including triggering coordination mechanisms for funding, materials and human resources deployments.

component_responses.notes: The NS key staff are familiar with the available IFRC support (technical, financial, material and HR). The mechanism to coordinate response with respective IFRC offices is widely understood (with a familiarity with IFRC emergency funding mechanisms) but is not available in the form of formal documented SOPs. NS procedures (not documented SOPs) include procedures to request and incorporate regional and global support/teams into their response system, including prior to imminent crisis/disaster, and assigns a focal point to act as counterpart to regional/international responders. NS informs IFRC within 24 hours for which assistance may be required. In this regard, a focal person is identified. EOC SOPs under orders of succession Senior individual based on chain of command.  TTRCS SOPs include procedures to request and incorporate regional and global support/teams into their response system, including prior to imminent crisis/disaster, this is based on TTRCS president requesting and initiating the procedure. NS informs IFRC within 24 hours for which assistance may be required (Go). NS is familiar with the IFRC emergency funding mechanisms  and can request bilateral assistance in accordance with established coordination frameworks. TTRCS liaises with the CCST to interact and coordinate initially with regional/international responders.

component_details.title: CHEMICAL, BIOLOGICAL, RADIOLOGICAL AND NUCLEAR (CBRN) EMERGENCY PREPAREDNESS

component_responses.notes: Livelihoods is currently being  incorporated into NS DRM strategy, plans, systems and procedures. TTRCS has identified a focal point specific to Livelihoods to champion such activities and NS staff, as well as volunteers are trained in livelihoods data collection through previous NS responses.

While this component is not part of the NS's Mandate, but they have done some work in the area. There are prepositioned shelter bins in 8 high risk communities which conform to IFRC standards. The NS also has an SOP for obtaining NFIs from the IFRC and are working on MOUs that will allow priority access to the NSs for shelter items from suppliers. Staff and volunteers do not have shelter kit training.

component_details.title: MANAGEMENT OF DEAD BODIES TO FACILITATE THEIR IDENTIFICATION

component_responses.notes: The NS is part of the regional RFL network and actively takes part in meetings with other NSs and stakeholders,
This is not part of the NSs mandate but they acknowledge that recovery is a aspect of DM that is important and should be incorporated.

component_details.title: NS-specific areas of intervention
component_details.description: Sector-specific or services provided by the NS in case of emergencies, it is in line with the NS mandate and legislation in country. It includes Community Based DP/DRR, Evacuation, Health in Emergencies, Epidemic and Pandemic, First aid, WASH, Food security and Livelihoods, Search and rRescue, Shelter, Management of dead bodies, RFL, Transition to recovery, and CBRN preparedness.

component_responses.notes: There is no specific CBDRR plan that includes First Aid, but it is the main income generator and a substantial amount of work has been put in place at the NS HQ to render this service. However, the NS has identified First Aid Services at branch levels is not as fully developed.

component_details.title: Coordination with local community level responders
component_details.description: Engagement with Community Disaster Response Teams (CDRTs), through training, coordination, and the development of community disaster preparedness and response plans.

component_responses.notes: At the HQ the component is well functioning. However, there is are major gaps to the filled at branch level. Branch development must take precedent before migrating or fully integrating this component at branch level. Communication between Branches and HQ can be improved. HQ is currently the lead for implementation and response planning and it does not happen at branch level only at HQ. TTRCS aims to get branches to be implementers and establish HQ as overall oversight. Additionally, CDRT coordination happens from HQ; CERTS/CDRTS are part of the volunteers system who are then assigned to the branch; will be called out as a Branch intervention team not as CDRTs

component_details.title: Cooperation with private sector
component_details.description: Mechanism that allows cooperation with private sector that often plays a strong role in response, particularly if there is impact on their staff and businesses. There is often a willingness to donate goods and services. Advance agreements help to expedite response actions.

component_responses.notes: NS ensures due diligence when selecting partners and accepting donations to mitigate image or reputational risk and donations are forthcoming from reputable sources. TTRCS ensures appropriate use of emblem and protect the organization's visual identity. However, NS recognises veterinarians, doctors offices, advertisements, drug stores use the red cross against a white background with no modifications; awareness of the symbol is needed; not readily associated with red cross but symbol exists in general medical services. Volunteer policy speaks to corporate volunteers; updated in 2020; met impact volunteer database that is populated and updated regularly to train and use volunteers from corporate partners.

component_details.title: Coordination with External Agencies and NGOs
component_details.description: Mechanism that facilitates coordination and collaboration with Non-Governmental Organization (NGO), both local and international NGOs, civil society organizations (CSOs) and United Nations agencies in country.

component_responses.notes: The NS is part of the regional humanitarian network and actively participates in knowledge sharing best practices. TTRCS is an active member of the humanitarian community (UN, NGO) for coordination and efficiency of response. However, TTRCS has not defined its role as a cluster member  and agreed formally on information sharing to the humanitarian coordination system.	Instead, the NS operates within the context of the IFRC framework; not a part of the national system but TTRCS is able to assist if called upon.  NS is aware of IFRC's role in the shelter cluster coordination and UN-led appeal and strategic processes. In this case UN would come to the cluster office and CCST will liaise with NS. TTRCS  has an agreement with UN for response but there are no established Memorandums Of Understanding (MOU).

component_details.title: Civil Military Relations
component_details.description: Dialogue and interaction with military actors, essential to protect and promote humanitarian principles, avoid competition, minimize inconsistency and, when appropriate, pursue common goals.

component_details.title: Coordination with Movement
component_details.description: Mechanisms that facilitate the coordination with ICRC, IFRC, and PNS in-country.

component_responses.notes: IFRC is present in Trinidad  and there is strong coordination with movement partners to share information on needs assessment, plan of actions, progress against operations and operational capacities and emerging gaps in resources. TTRCS utilises different communication channels to share information with neighbouring NSs to coordinate response actions. The NS also ensures that there are systems in place to liaise with the IFRC to accept international assistance. They did identify these procedures are not documented in SOPs and have happened only in times of emergency, thus far. In country coordination mechanisms are IFRC Framework provides information on this. Best practice as sharing is encouraged with neighbouring NSs when requested.

component_details.title: Coordination with authorities
component_details.description: Mechanism that facilitates coordination and cooperation with local and national authorities. It is connected to the NS auxiliary role for humanitarian assistance.

component_responses.notes: The NS knows their role in the national response framework and keeps regular communication with the RCRC and other national agencies to ensure assistance can be effectively given in times of emergency. The NS knows the capacities of national authorities and identifies areas within a response to fulfil their auxiliary role. It has control over its resources, assets and emblem when responding. TTRCS is part of the national response framework and is in communication with the relevant authorities should their services be needed, through some areas of intervention are not fully established.

component_details.title: Staff and volunteer management
component_details.description: Well-functioning staff and volunteer management systems and practices allow for effective recruitment, supervision, support and encouragement of staff and volunteers.

component_responses.notes: The TTRCS deploys and equips responders who are Branch Intervention Teams (BITs) and National Intervention Teams (NITs); no formalised ToRs exist but situation and safety briefings have been institutionalised out of practice. Learning paths for responders are in place through the learning platform and responders are trained in quality and accountability standards (Sphere, Code of Conduct, etc...) around the protection, sexual abuse, exploitation, child protection, gender-based violence and other forms of abuse; only the migration team will undertake this training by the end of 2020 and rest of staff can will be done next year 2021. TTRCS has learning paths for responders to obtain required qualifications and skills according to competencies and roles which id logged in the volunteer database. Not all responders have official updated ID recognised by authorities and appropriate visibility items. TTRCS has changed the process of how IDs are issued and are now issued for the duration of the operation, also Staff IDs expire every 2 years and the Code of Conduct is signed by all NS staff and volunteers. TTRCS has safety briefs and IFRC basic insurance for volunteers; staff have insurance. Procedures do exist to activate, deploy and manage branch and national response teams such as for BITs which is communicated through a structured protocol with Disaster Officer North Branch, where reports go back to Disaster Management Unit.  NS has an accessible, up-to-date database of responders’ contacts and capacities at all branches, except for the South Branch. At HQ level there is gap analysis and competency mapping i.e. if specific volunteers for shelters needed, as well as a list of who can be contacted. Obtaining a sectoral response categorisation to maintain a diverse workforce is in progress, as there are gaps in transitioning all volunteers to the better impact database from the hardcopy system and many persons have not created their profiles. The digital divide for some volunteers must be resolved and worked onto capture all sectors.  Further the NS does not have expedited procedures to incorporate spontaneous volunteers during emergencies which meet minimum screening procedures and comply with its volunteer in emergency policy. TTRCS also does not have HR procedures to scale-up and down (recruitment, retention), and procedures for appreciation of volunteers during emergencies. There is a formal personnel rotation for response, but not retention at the NS. For scenarios that entail safety and/or security concerns for staff and volunteers, a specific Safer Access analysis is conducted. Additionally, training on self-care, violence and harassment in the workplace is completed regularly, and psychosocial support is available for staff and volunteers during and after emergencies and crises. Lastly, part of finance procedures covers responders' expenses once they are incurred during emergencies and can be justified.

component_details.title: Safety and security management
component_details.description: Addresses policy and procedures to ensure the safety of staff and volunteers. This include awareness, effective recruitment, training and management processes in place to ensure that personnel are capable of undertaking the roles demanded of them (from NS operational, management and leaders) according to the Stay Safe (IFRC) and Safer Access (ICRC). Based on safer access framework, including concepts of access, perception, identification and acceptance, and protection and violence prevention.

component_responses.notes: NS implements Safer Access and has appropriate security systems in place to protect staff and volunteers, as a part of mandatory volunteer and staff training prior to appointment. There is no designated staff trained at headquarter and branch appointed and accountable for safety and security but others with experience are called upon to assist if needed as apart of their current portfolio. TTRCS team recognised there needs to be more accountability here. Context and risk analysis information are divulged to teams before they are deployed, before any emergency a proper briefing is done. A safety and security policy and a compliance system exist to monitor staff and volunteers, as persons directed to safer access and TTRCS has adopted IFRC’s safety policies. Further, responders have been trained in Safer Access, Stay Safe and managers have completed security management training; and all staff and volunteers know the NS safety and security rules and procedures and follow them. TTRCS has worked on this (as identified in the OCAC findings) as part of mandatory volunteer and staff training prior to appointment. Staff and volunteers are held accountable based on the certification given prior to employment. However, no document that legally assigns responsibility. TTRCS  has communication mechanisms for staff and volunteers to report safety and security risks and incidents through the volunteer director if needed.

component_details.title: Communication in emergencies
component_details.description: Incorporates a system of public messaging to enable the NS to share timely, accurate information before, during, and after a disaster or crisis.

component_responses.notes: The NS has identified a trained focal point for communications only at HQ. TTRCS’s designated official spokesperson in an emergency is the president. The NS uses public and social media to draw attention to the unmet needs of affected people, and key public awareness messages are developed and shared with staff regularly. No standard templates for communication and any plan for external communication during an emergency exist, nor does TTRCS have a social networking policy or guidelines to ensure appropriate conduct of staff and volunteers. To provide information to public on an emergency within 24 hours is not within the NSs mandate, but will reshare from national agencies as needed. Key messages and public awareness messages in an emergency are developed and shared with staff regularly, via WhatsApp, email. The NS tracks negative media and social media to react accordingly via the hotline, social media monitoring; TTRCS has done training with Communications Delegate assisting CCSD on how to handle such situations. TTRCS also featured content on Tik Tok. NS does have a social networking policy and guidelines to ensure appropriate conduct of staff and volunteers. Also, NS has capacity to generate evidence-based results/messages to advocate to targeted audiences, i.e. decision makers and communities.

component_details.title: Operations Monitoring, Evaluation, Reporting and Learning
component_details.description: The PMERL is designed to implement a results-based planning, monitoring and evaluation system that provides an evidence base of NS performance, including relevance, efficiency, effectiveness, sustainability and impact. A reliable and trusted organization is accountable, providing transparent and timely information and building systems to strengthen data collection and reporting. It is data-driven, analytical and results-based.

component_responses.notes: TTRCS does not have a dedicated PMER function for emergency operations with adequate human and financial resources. NS refers to and uses lessons from previous operations in response planning (e.g. from evaluation, review and operational reports) from the lessons learnt Workshops/After Action Review conducted for the 2019 Floods. TTRCS has a standardised framework or plan of action for emergency operations which identifies specific results and the indicators to measure them. NS does not have revised and updated operational plans based on intended and unintended outcomes of operations, but staff is aware of the mechanism to change the operation if needed. TTRCS has identified that this situation has never occurred, where it was required to do so. TTRCS only conducts evaluations and/or reviews of the operation to identify and integrate key lessons and recommendations for ongoing projects and the First Aid Department. TTRCS revises operational plans based on intended and unintended outcomes in collaboration with the IFRC Country Cluster Delegation (CCSD). The NS also reports to partners in line with agreement, using appropriate templates. For Movement-wide contributions, NS cooperates with IFRC CCSD on PMER activities.

component_details.title: Finance and Admin policy and emergency procedures
component_details.description: Overall budgeting, accounting, treasury, assets, financial reporting and financial services operations. it also includes the efficient delivery , cost effective and timely services to the NS. Pre-approved, auditable, expedited procedures that allow for flexibility during a disaster/crisis. These must meet transparency, oversight and accountability standards. Procedures may include faster approval processes, fewer signatures, different authority levels. The Emergency Procedures are activated for a specific period of time.

component_responses.notes: The NS has an automated accounting and financial system and procedures to account for and report regularly on funds and expenditures. NS has trained personnel in Finance and Admin emergency support procedures (IFRC). TTRCS has the activation of its Finance and Admin emergency procedures is linked to the EOC SOPs. procedures is not linked to the EOC SOPs as SOPs are non-existent. NS has procedures in place to facilitate transparency, financial reporting mechanism in place, but the mechanism needs to be further strengthened in order to prevent acts of fraud and/or corruption during an emergency, there will always be unforseen gaps but procedures are in place. All MoUs or agreements for compliance are documented, but staff and/or relevant volunteers need to be sensitized on existing MoUs. TTRCS idenitfied that all donor MOUs are signed and copies kept with finance. Further, invoices must be signed by finance and president.

component_details.title: Information and Communication Technology (ICT)
component_details.description: Refers to technologies that provide access to information through telecommunications. This includes the Internet, wireless networks, mobile phones, radios and other communication mediums.

component_responses.notes: Not all TTRCS Staff has office issued phones paid by the NS. Radios will be used for emergencies when required, as there is no system to ensure recharging is in place while in the field. NS operations personnel always carry contact lists with critical numbers saved on their mobile phones. However, the contact emergency call tree has to updated with new positions. NS has approved Emergency Notification SOPs followed by all staff and volunteers. It has an agreed social media platform such as Whatsapp, Facebook, Instagram, Twitter and Tik Tok for emergency communications and public information sharing of messages. Key headquarter and branch staff in high-risk areas do not have a functioning radio system (two-way VHF and HF). The NS has radio systems at branches but they are not linked together and operate on different ranges and frequency. A new radio system purchased but not yet operational to be assigned to key staff and placed in NS vehicles. All personnel have received radio training and call signs are assigned accordingly in collaboration with the National Disaster Office (ODPM). TTRCS is working on updated SOPs for mobile and radio communications.	As a more economic alternative to satellite phones the NS Staff is utilising the commercial radio system through a local communications service provider (Massy) and will be able to have access to the national radio network. TTRCS is following up on the procurement of portable generators to ensure continuity of operations at HQ. TTRCS also has an internet capable router to provide data connectivity for operational staff and pocket WiFi devices are available for field personnel. The NS has trained IT support focal points able to support technical issues and equipment (e.g. computers, software, phones, cameras, GPS) and provide maintenance, from identified skilled volunteers who are capable; as well as contacts with suppliers to provide these services.

component_details.title: Resource Mobilisation
component_details.description: A documented strategy for raising domestic funds from the government, private sector, general public and other in-country actors to support the national society’s response. This would include allocation of responsibilities, practical mechanisms for accepting funds and for being accountable on funds.

component_responses.notes: The NS key staff are familiar with the resource mobilisation options for humanitarian operations and preparedness activities.  TTRCS and its branches do not have a resource mobilisation strategy, SOPs or focal point in place at HQ, but they are working on this as identified through the need of COVID-19 Impact. NS has agreements and mechanisms for collaboration and fundraising with the private sector; in fact every partner brought on board has a Memorandums Of Understanding (MOUs). NS has not established a national emergency fund with criteria for proper use, but is aiming toward this and working toward setting up a dedicated account that can be used in the event it is needed for both overseas and local needs. For resource mobilisation there is a focal point at the NS but they are not involved in emergency operations coordination. Additionally, the NS resource mobilisation has not yet established pre-disaster agreements with partners and donors, it is in progress. TTRCS has a platform (phone number, bank account, online, etc.) able to accept national and/or international donations within 48 hours of an emergency .However, NS does not have a pre-defined list of acceptable in-kind donations and makes decision on an ad hoc basis to mitigate image or reputational risks. TTRCS does have a  donation tracking system, and works with the IFRC on joint operational shared services platform, as the NS’s Finance tracks money using the Table platform used for credit cards and cheques, and reporting is done to IFRC and government of Trinidad and Tobago due to subvention. NS does not have agreed procedures across departments (technical teams and support services) to communicate changes and report on outcomes of resources provided but saw this to not be applicable to their context.

The NS has separate focal points for procurement, stock and warehouse management, transport and fleet management. There is prepositioned stock at TTRCS branches but not in strategic areas. The NS has prepositioned stock and procurement has a database of suppliers accordingly to needs but there are no existing MOUs formalised at this time. The NFIs meet standards and reflect the needs of populations at risk, specifically in the case of hygiene kits. The NS has volunteers trained in logistics training but are not equipped to fill surge capacity gaps during an emergency response.//The NS has an agreement with the government for import duty and tax exemptions and benefits from the CCST agreement with government. However, in times of emergency it is a timely process and not as effective. TTRCS coordinates its stock and equipment with local authorities for the sake of response planning and coordination, in relation to supporting the state in distribution of items and replenishment agreements. No document exists to expedite procedures for branches to request additional relief items and equipment for early action and immediate response, but it exists at headquarters. The NS has both SOPs for accepting and rejecting goods under finance regulations, as well as procedures to import goods.//The NS has trained personnel for procurement, which is managed by Headquarters. The NS has a database of suppliers to immediately access supplies but are not in compliance with IFRC standards and is a work in progress. NS has to work on an up-to-date database of suppliers and formalised agreements (who are in compliance with IFRC Code of Conduct) for key items and services. On the other hand, relevant staff is aware of emergency procurement procedure, including authorisation levels, standard forms, templates. TTRCS maintains a blacklist of suppliers for immediate access to supplies and/or services necessary for humanitarian response.//The NS does not have a fleet manual. The existing vehicles are insured, but their use is not fully documented using logbooks, maintenance records, fuel checks etc. There are working seatbelts in all vehicles, first aid kits in some vehicles, and fire extinguishers only in ambulances. The NS uses licensed mechanics/workshops for the maintenance of its vehicle. There are documented procedures for reporting of accidents and insurance claims. The NS has mapped 2 main companies in Trinidad and 1 in Tobago to rent vehicles during a response. The NS has informal procedures to induct and test new drivers. The drivers have valid licenses for the types of vehicles they are driving but are not regularly tested. However, drivers for the ambulances are tested. TTRCS does not have emergency procedures to guide the hours for drivers including non-standard hours and compensation.//The NS does not have an approved warehouse and stock management manual with standard forms and templates, or relevant staff trained in such. NS has a minimum stock for 200 families in a dedicated and appropriate space with 24/7 access to receive, store and dispatch relief supplies and response equipment, enough to cover target number of households as per its response plan. In addition, the NS has 2 storage places at strategic locations owned by the NS, in Port of Spain and Point Fortin.

component_details.title: RC auxiliary role, Mandate and Law
component_details.description: A constitutional reference to the role of the NS in responding to disasters and crises, which may be legislated or included/ recognized in the National Response System.

component_responses.notes: TRCS have the tool but not yet disseminated

component_details.title: DRM Strategy
component_details.description: An outline of the overall goal that the NS seeks to achieve in its disaster and crisis response operations. The goal considers: context analysis, ongoing/regular all-hazards risk assessments: it may define the target proportion of affected population that will be reached, and a definition of the areas/sectors where a NS will usually respond during an emergency.

component_responses.notes: The documents should be familiar to all the staffs and volunteers at all levels.

component_details.title: DRM Policy
component_details.description: Reflects the NS mission, RCRC principles and mandate. It acknowledges other relevant NS policies, and aligns with the government policy (where applicable), incorporating the general rules that the NS will obey in order to achieve something (i.e mandate, strategy, etc.)

component_responses.notes: TRCS have all the documents the area which needs improvements is dissemination

component_details.title: DRM Laws, Advocacy and Dissemination
component_details.description: Designed to support the NS in improving legal preparedness for disasters and crisis and to promote the use of the IDRL Guidelines in order to reduce human vulnerability.

component_responses.notes: IFRC to provide technical support to TRCS in documents developed and strengthen the  Capacity of IDRL humanitarian and DRM policy to staffs and volunteers to be able to disseminate them. TRCS to initiate Legal Unit which will  support with legislative advocacy

component_details.title: Quality and accountability
component_details.description: Describes the essential elements of principled, accountable, and high-quality humanitarian action. The RCRC Movement provides support to the most vulnerable people in line with the Sphere and CHS standards, Code of Conduct for the RCRC Movement and NGOS in Disaster Relief and the Code for Good Partnership of the RCRC Movement, Gender & Diversity, inclusion and protection, BPI/ Do no harm, context-sensitive analysis, violence prevention, accountability to affected population and disability considerations, Community engagement and accountability (CEA).

component_responses.notes: More trainings  to volunteers in every aspect such as PSEA, PGI,CEA etc, should be scheduled for all branches to be trained and not taking place in places with on going projects.The development of CEA SOPs should be given priority.

component_details.title: Emergency Response Procedures (SOPs)
component_details.description: Written guidelines that describe duties and rights of personnel, command structures, coordination with other organizations, and reporting requirements, etc. Includes detailed organogram, decision-making flow chart, and defined roles and responsibilities.

component_responses.notes:
NS needs to Update and review the presence SoP. 
Although there is need to map unpresence SoP for the development.
Print, share and disseminate all the SoP to staff and volunteers

component_details.title: Response and recovery planning
component_details.description: A documented set of procedures for the disaster/crisis response and recovery process. Including use of local capacities, transition to recovery, type of activities and serivices provided during response and recovery activities and exit strategies, procedures for DREF & EA, and templates for planning, budgeting and accessing funds.

component_responses.notes: NS has to Develop Multi-sectoral response plan, Review SDP (2020-2025) and icorporate IFRC's inputs,principle and rule, DRM policy, PGI and fundamental. Conduct a regular dissemination on DRM policy to accommodate the staff and volunteers who are newly  employed and/or registered. The NS need have safer access trainining for staff and volunteers. The NS need to develop a formal procedures for Donation protocals.

component_details.title: Pre-disaster meetings and agreements
component_details.description: A commitment to arrange meetings and agreements with Movement stakeholders and external actors to identify, plan for and address gaps for any upcoming disaster season (e.g. monsoon, floods or cyclones, or for any generic disaster/crisis event (e.g Epidemic, pandemic, confilict situations). Pre-disaster agreements should set out each partner's role in the event of a disaster/crisis.

component_responses.notes: NS has to develop response strategies, reviewed and updates SOPs in order to have more stakeholders. NS need have MoU with relevant local and national key actors, the procedures and code of conduct that NS has with some contractors has to be signed before the collaboration with them. Development and signing of MoUs/agreements with public authorities has to be done to facilitate expedited import of humanitarian aid and visas for incoming personnel. All necessary agreements has to be taken into account for smooth operations and implementation.

component_details.title: Hazard, Context and Risk Analysis, Monitoring and Early Warning
component_details.description: Describes how the NS monitors and maps past, present and potential hazards, disasters and crises (e.g. hazard, vulnerability assessments, gathering information from communities and government authorities) and systematically evaluates the damage that could be caused by a potential disaster/crisis, the frequency, severity of the impact, and the alert the relevant areas to scale the preparedness actions to reduce population vulnerability.

component_responses.notes: On the area of developing and dissemination on the Multi -hazard risk analysis map, eVCA, improvement and strentherned on the early action, Reviewing SoP on the EWEA, Strenthern cross-border relation, support on the Risk management training and the development of the risk management policy, strategies and framework.

component_details.title: Scenario planning
component_details.description: A set of practical operation plans that closely mirror the generic disaster or crisis response plan but are tailored to a specific hazard type (e.g. earthquake, dengue epidemic, floods, cyclone) and a specific scenario (i.e. number of people affected, their locations and other important factors).

component_responses.notes: NS has no response strategy which create different scenarior with clear definition of key role and responsibilities in multi sectoral to ensure complementality of the onorgram. So  NS its require to develop and disseminate the strategy. However much can be done on the development of NS contigency plan and dissemination with accountability. NS should develop simulation exercise on different scenarior testing and ensure its acceptance, Also should consider hiring security focal point, equip vehicles with VHF radio for reporting movement and volunteer staff and link with EOC .Ns needs also to intergrate cross border coordination mechanism for epidemic and pandemic criss.

component_details.title: Risk management
component_details.description: A mapping of the potential risks in every area, along with its related mitigation measures. Including financial, reputational, organizational risks etc.

component_responses.notes: Strengthen Risk management into practices, develop risk management frame work, Training and Dissemination of Risk register, guidelines and policy.

component_details.title: Preparedness plans and budgets
component_details.description: Plans identifying organisational resources, determining roles and responsibilities, and developing policies, procedures and activities in order to reach a level of preparedness to be able to respond effectively to a disaster or crisis. Budgets ensure that the necessary financial support is secured to allow capacities to be built and readiness maintained.

component_responses.notes: NS needs to develop reponse strategy that catch up preperedness gap and develop the strategic plan to adress the gaps to support Capacity building on different knowledge on how to prepere for effective response (Evca, BDRT, NDRT, DRR, Livelihood, EWEA and other Climate related project.training), Simulation of different scenarior, financial resources and Manpower, Preposition of different stock,etc. Requires to update and review different preparedness SoPs

component_details.title: Business continuity
component_details.description: A strategy to counter any potential or anticipated obstacles to effective functioning of the NS, with an eye to ensuring that personnel and assets are protected and able to function in the event of a disaster/crisis.

component_responses.notes: NS need to build awareness  on EWEA concept to its staff and volunteers, Developing more projects on EWEA to cascade to as many regions as possible. NS need to introduce a CDRT to those regions which has not yet been introduced and update it to that one region which has conducted a CDRT. The review and development of tools to ensure assessment, planning and response is done in an inclusive of Gender and Diversity and conflict sensitive way.

The NS need to have a response strategy which identifies  multiple scenarios. Conduct a refresher training on evacuation, search and rescure, Drivers training to cover coastal and lake zones areas to support the initiatives and the procurement of evacuation gears as well.

NS develop a pre - disaster agreements for mult-country outbreaks, strengthen the EOC to link with National health emergency response team, having a proper mechanism for responding to rumours, NS should put in place the necessary mechanism adhered by Staff and volunteers for safety and insurance. The NS need to clearly identify its role incase of isolation and quarantine. Need to procure more equipments for safe and dignified management of dead bodies.
NS needs more CBDRR trinings wich includes FA to cover all 189 districts. Need to procure more eguipment for FA and provides for rules and regulations for its sustainability.
Need for development of response strategy which comprises of WASH scenarious, conducting more WASH training to staff and volunteers all over the NS coverage. Development of WASH SOPs.

NS needs to review and harmonise guidelines concernig Food Security to strengthen coordination with partners on this sector, need to have Food Security Focal Person. Build awareness on the Intergrated Phase Classification IPC, provides for Food Security Training ToT Level to cascade the knowledge at the branch level. The NS should develop FS SOPs relys with the government policy and standards

NS need to develop SOPs on Livelihood Security and Safety Nets, Identify a Focal Person and other technical staff and build their capacity. NS has to Map and identify market systems and baselines. Make the Identification of high risk areas. Needs for training and equipments.
NS need to develop response strategy and make updates on the SOPs for rearch and rescure

NS needs more shelter supplies and NFIs for effective response during disasters. Needs for pre disaster and framework agreement in place. Provision of more training and preposition of shelter kit to some regions.

component_details.title: MANAGEMENT OF DEAD BODIES TO FACILITATE THEIR IDENTIFICATION

component_responses.notes: More training and equipments required in place across the regions. Training on antemortem and postmotem for identification of dead bodies data base.NS should include the management of dead bodies within the response strategy.

Due to financial constraints, TRCS is unable to provide RFL services to people in need. However, there is a need to build more capacity to staff and volunteers, and TRCS must seek additional resources to support RFL services.

NS has to set a long term Early Recovery System for food security and other climate issues, Strengthen the coordination with partners for more support to reach more people in communities. NS need to develop a livelihood recovery plan of action and also need to have a food and livelihood focal point at HQ and region branches to influence on the resources mobilization. More training on response intervention is needed to cascade to more regions and prepositioning of cleaning items.

component_details.title: CHEMICAL, BIOLOGICAL, RADIOLOGICAL AND NUCLEAR (CBRN) EMERGENCY PREPAREDNESS

component_responses.notes: NS needs to train and conduct a refresher course as well on CBHFA and BFA to its staffs and volunteers all over the country.

component_details.title: Mapping of NS capacities
component_details.description: A list of the NS capacities including HR (staff, response teams and volunteers) and equipment that are available for disaster/crisis response. Teams could include branch and national response teams. This should be defined by technical speciality where relevant.

component_responses.notes: NS need to conduct training and refresher courses for staff and volunteers in the specific areas of intervention. The need for resources mobilization (Crisis modifier) to pre position DP stocks. NS has to develop a storage data base which will easen the issue of mapping and gaps identification.

component_details.title: Early Action Mechanisms
component_details.description: Designed to translate warnings into anticipatory actions to help reduce the impact of specific disaster or crisis events. They focus on consolidating available forecasting information and putting procedures in place to ensure that a NS can act ahead of any disaster/crisis. Forecast-based financing is included within the scope of this area.

component_responses.notes: On the area of Early Warning System, NS needs to strengthen coordination with stakeholders and partners for resource mobilization and strengthening EW communication system as well.

component_details.title: Cash Based Intervention (CBI)
component_details.description: An effective and flexible way, including all forms of cash and voucher-based assistance, to support people affected by emergencies, maintaining their dignity and choice, while fostering local economies. Cash should also be mainstreamed into other sectors (including Relief, shelter, livelihoods) and services (Logistics, Finance, etc.)

component_responses.notes: More training, dissemination and simulations are needed to all levels  to strengthen the capacity of NS on conducting CTP. For a better practices/operations on CTP NS need to abide with the PMO-DMD HCT SOPs and to strengthen communication with the government (to review the NS CTP SOPs together with that one of the government). NS regional branches needs to have a Disaster Management Monetary Donation Busket that may be used for CT during an emergency.

component_details.title: Emergency Needs Assessment
component_details.description: Assess the extent and impact of the damage caused by the disaster/crisis and the degree of vulnerability of the affected population. The first step in any emergency response, such an assessment will identify the needs that require external intervention and the gaps to be filled. It is a vital component of the programme-planning process.

component_responses.notes: The templete for ENA needs to be improved and customized to NS context and regularly updated. NS need to train more Staff and Volunteers on mult - sectorial emergency assessment.

component_details.title: Affected population selection
component_details.description: Identification and selection of target Affected population for interventions, using a pre-defined set of criteria based on need and vulnerability. This includes consideration of specific vulnerabilities such as disability, age and gender.

component_responses.notes: We have a gap on beneficiary selection criteria. NS should develop a criteria guidline

component_details.title: Emergency Operations Centre (EOC)
component_details.description: A central command and control facility responsible for carrying out disaster/crisis management functions at a strategic level in an emergency situation. The common functions are to collect and analyze data; facilitate decision making that protects life and livelihoods; and disseminate those decisions to all concerned agencies and individuals. Generally located at the headquarter level of an organization.

component_responses.notes: The NS EOC need the following issues to be taken care of so that will be working properly and accordingly: The SOPs has to be developed and disseminated to both staff and vonteers, needs for Focal Person, activation has to be done according to procedures with mechanism in place.

component_details.title: Information Management (IM)
component_details.description: Ability to manage information including requesting, receiving, analyzing and disseminating as per its procedures and partner requirements (IFRC and public authorities in particular). There should be a clear digital/paper trail that documents what, when and how the NS has acted and provides key information for the development of Emergency Plan of Actions. Includes IM between levels, between departments and Situational Reports, mapping, visualisation of data, GO platform (IFRC).

component_responses.notes: NS has to conduct a dissemination on IM templetes methodology and procedures, introducing the IM focal point, NS has to develop a system that can share report. NS should also initiate a base line support rather that that one done on projects and should develop a standardised situation report format.

component_details.title: Testing and Learning
component_details.description: Drills and Simulations allow the organization to test, identify and learn from the results of these type of exercises and incorporate learning into future preparedness and response planning.

component_responses.notes: Develop SOP for simulations, develop different scenarios and to have MOU and relationships with fellow cross-borders NS

component_details.title: Activation of regional and international support
component_details.description: Procedures for requesting and accepting regional and international support in operations, including triggering coordination mechanisms for funding, materials and human resources deployments.

component_responses.notes: NS has to develop SOPs to coordinate response with respective IFRC offices, SOPs which includes procedures to request and incorporate regional and global support/teams into the response system, Dissemination to staff and volunteers on the EPoA procedures, DREF criteria and EA proceess. NS need to have an assigned Focal point act as counterpart to regional/inernational responders. NS should have a legal frame work documented to facilitates timely access of RCRC goods and personnel into the country

component_details.title: Coordination with Movement
component_details.description: Mechanisms that facilitate the coordination with ICRC, IFRC, and PNS in-country.

component_responses.notes: For NS to exchanges information with neighboring NS and coordinates its response activities with them need to have document to support this process.

component_details.title: Coordination with authorities
component_details.description: Mechanism that facilitates coordination and cooperation with local and national authorities. It is connected to the NS auxiliary role for humanitarian assistance.

component_responses.notes: NS needs to work more and make disseminaton on the use of emblem to its staff, volunteers, government authorities and other stakeholders.

component_details.title: Coordination with External Agencies and NGOs
component_details.description: Mechanism that facilitates coordination and collaboration with Non-Governmental Organization (NGO), both local and international NGOs, civil society organizations (CSOs) and United Nations agencies in country.

component_responses.notes: NS is not an active member of the humanitarian community (UN, NGO) for coordination and efficiency of response, so NS needs to build trust with other agencies and making more disseminations and coordinations with other actors.

component_details.title: Civil Military Relations
component_details.description: Dialogue and interaction with military actors, essential to protect and promote humanitarian principles, avoid competition, minimize inconsistency and, when appropriate, pursue common goals.

component_responses.notes: The NS work under the umbrella of ICRC on the issue of Coordination arrangements with military and  adhere to Fundamental Principles, International humanitarian law (IHL), Council of Delegates (CoD) resolutions.NS need awareness and dissemination of the Geneva convention regarding the IHL.

component_details.title: Coordination with local community level responders
component_details.description: Engagement with Community Disaster Response Teams (CDRTs), through training, coordination, and the development of community disaster preparedness and response plans.

component_responses.notes: NS has to make sure that Information from communities is well taken into consideration for decision-making at branches and shared with headquarters by strengthening its system and mechanism of collecting such informations and communicating them.

component_details.title: Cooperation with private sector
component_details.description: Mechanism that allows cooperation with private sector that often plays a strong role in response, particularly if there is impact on their staff and businesses. There is often a willingness to donate goods and services. Advance agreements help to expedite response actions.

component_responses.notes: NS needs to develop a policy for accepting donations to mitigate reputational risks. The NS will also need to document the mechanism to have a clear system in place to train and use volunteers from corporate partners

component_details.title: Safety and security management
component_details.description: Addresses policy and procedures to ensure the safety of staff and volunteers. This include awareness, effective recruitment, training and management processes in place to ensure that personnel are capable of undertaking the roles demanded of them (from NS operational, management and leaders) according to the Stay Safe (IFRC) and Safer Access (ICRC). Based on safer access framework, including concepts of access, perception, identification and acceptance, and protection and violence prevention.

component_responses.notes: NS should have Safer Access training to protect staff and volunteers.A safety and security policy need to be developed to monitor staff and volunteers and the policy should be disseminated to all levels.

component_details.title: Operations Monitoring, Evaluation, Reporting and Learning
component_details.description: The PMERL is designed to implement a results-based planning, monitoring and evaluation system that provides an evidence base of NS performance, including relevance, efficiency, effectiveness, sustainability and impact. A reliable and trusted organization is accountable, providing transparent and timely information and building systems to strengthen data collection and reporting. It is data-driven, analytical and results-based.

component_responses.notes: NS has to invest more on human and financial report for a well functionable PME, NS needs a standardised framework or plan of action which icludes references from IFRC PoA guidelines, Sphere Standards, the CHS and Grand Bargain. The NS has has to develop a standardised M&E templetes and the tracking system for timely monitoring of reports.

component_details.title: Finance and Admin policy and emergency procedures
component_details.description: Overall budgeting, accounting, treasury, assets, financial reporting and financial services operations. it also includes the efficient delivery , cost effective and timely services to the NS. Pre-approved, auditable, expedited procedures that allow for flexibility during a disaster/crisis. These must meet transparency, oversight and accountability standards. Procedures may include faster approval processes, fewer signatures, different authority levels. The Emergency Procedures are activated for a specific period of time.

component_responses.notes: NS has to conduct training and dissemination for NAVISION, train its personnel in Finance and Admin emergence support procedures, develop the Finance and Admin emergency procedures that comply with national laws and IFRC practice to rapidly support operations. NS has to be familiar and complies with MoUs drafted during an emergency.

component_details.title: Information and Communication Technology (ICT)
component_details.description: Refers to technologies that provide access to information through telecommunications. This includes the Internet, wireless networks, mobile phones, radios and other communication mediums.

component_responses.notes: NS need to have an up to date and approved Emergency Notification Protocal SOPs followed by both staff and volunteers, develop an agreed social media platform for emergency communications and messaging, develop a functioning radio system and disseminate the system to all staff and volunteers. NS need to develop SOPs for mobile and radio communications.

LOGISTICS MANAGEMENT: Need to recruit more personnel on Logistic Unit and train them on humanitarian and emmergency context. NS has to train key staff on IFRC logistics services in emergency operations. The NS needs to have pre disaster agreements with suppliers in terms of cost, speed and reliability. NS should have a pre-positioned relief items strategically located. NS also need to train volunteers who can act as surge.
SUPPLY CHAIN MANAGEMENT: Need to activate NAVISION for logistic unit. NS needs to have a documented expedited procedure for branches to  request additional relief items and/or equipment for early action and immediate response from  HQ or from local, pre-agreed suppliers. NS has to develop SOPs for accepting/rejecting, storing, disposing and reporting on in-kind donations.
PROCUREMENT: There is a need for disseminations of the procurement manual to staff and volunteers. NS should develop SOPs on import of goods. NS need to have a documented and approved expedited logistics procedures for emergency situations  and all relevant staff should be familiar with the content and procedures.
FLEET AND TRANSPORTATION MANAGEMENT: There is a need for dissemination of the Fleet manual, the NS also need to review its procedures of Insuring its vehicles. NS has to develop/review its mechanism of mapping iin country resources to rent/borrow vehicles and or drivers. NS has to develop emergency procedures to guide the hours for drivers including non-standard hours and compensation.
