component_responses.notes: •	A dedicated PMER focal point has been in place for two years which have greatly benefitted PMER processes and reporting.  •	BRCS refers to and uses lessons from previous operations in response planning but does not systematically allocate resources for evaluations.  •	BRCS monitors Facebook/social media and addresses comments that may have a risk to the NS; it monitors newspapers for mentions of NS.  •	The hotline is no longer functioning but a new one is planned.  •	NS follows partners' agreements, formats, and deadlines for reporting. SADDD is incorporated to NS reports. •	BRCS affectively cooperates with IFRC on relevant PMER processes. PMER Officer submits annual report with key indicators to IFRC e.g., FDRS (Federation-wide databank and reporting system), COVID-19 reports. •	More systematic processes need to be in place for the PMER cycle, especially evaluation.

component_details.title: Finance and Admin policy and emergency procedures
component_details.description: Overall budgeting, accounting, treasury, assets, financial reporting and financial services operations. it also includes the efficient delivery , cost effective and timely services to the NS. Pre-approved, auditable, expedited procedures that allow for flexibility during a disaster/crisis. These must meet transparency, oversight and accountability standards. Procedures may include faster approval processes, fewer signatures, different authority levels. The Emergency Procedures are activated for a specific period of time.

component_responses.notes: •	BRCS has existing Finance and Administration procedures for NS normal operations and service delivery which are relevant for emergency response programming.  •	BRCS national EOC and related SOPs including finance and administration procedures have yet to be drafted and finalized.  •	Joint IFRC and BRCS support to Hurricane Dorian response operations provide an opportunity to transition relevant IFRC processes and templates directly into BRCS procedures in an updated Finance and Administration Manual. •	Development of specific emergency finance procedures including those related to epidemic risks is pending with the development of the EOC and coordination with the DM unit.

component_details.title: Information and Communication Technology (ICT)
component_details.description: Refers to technologies that provide access to information through telecommunications. This includes the Internet, wireless networks, mobile phones, radios and other communication mediums.

component_responses.notes: •	The ICT component at BRCS is met and functioning well.  •	NS has recently acquired tablets for the activities in the field. NS volunteers are deployed with the cell phone that has data plan. •	Satellite phones have been procured for HQ and Branches. Radios and satellite phones cleared by national authorities for frequencies. •	BRCS has access to radio Public Service Announcements (PSAs) for the dissemination of information to the public. •	Standardized usage of this equipment needs be improved by the development of SOPs for mobile communications.  •	NS has 2 drones and trained 3 drone pilots: PMER, Communications and DM focal points. •	ICT responsibility in BRCS is with Communications department. There is an IT volunteer available to support with technical issues.  •	If staff cannot come into the office due to epidemic outbreak (e.g. lockdown) or other reasons, there are processes for staff to operate from home (in terms of ICT connectivity) to allow the business continuity.

component_details.title: Resource Mobilisation
component_details.description: A documented strategy for raising domestic funds from the government, private sector, general public and other in-country actors to support the national society’s response. This would include allocation of responsibilities, practical mechanisms for accepting funds and for being accountable on funds.

component_responses.notes: •	BRCS is emerging from its largest response operation for Hurricane Dorian with significant resources and support from IFRC and PNS. It presents BRCS an opportunity to strengthen Resource Mobilization capacity based on its profile and role in emergency preparedness, response and recovery with Government of Bahamas, the private sector and other key stakeholders, both at national and international level.  •	BRCS lacks an overall Resource Mobilisation (RM) strategy and plan. •	BRCS has a fundraising strategy, committee and an RM policy approved by the Board which, to be verified (if draft or final), provides a basis for the development of a RM strategy/plan.  •	COVID-19 seriously impacted regular fundraising events which could not be organized due to public health restrictions. •	Current lack of integration of program data with a CRM (database of contacts, funding target) makes it difficult to 'position' the NS with larger donors due to limited capacity for compliance with donations (accountability). •	Need to link the RM strategy with financial and program performance targets, reporting and accountability across BRCS Departments (donor compliance).

•	BRCS has a Warehouse Manager, which is a dedicated staff  responsible for warehouse, fleet and logistics (procurement is with finance/ 1 officer). BRCS Warehouse staff reports directly to DG and Welfare/DM Manager. •	There is a need to develop a comprehensive guidance for the logistics function (fleet, warehouse, procurement, logistics) within BRCS for emergencies. Currently, drafting SOPs for logistics linked the EOC is in process. •	Additional actions under consideration by BRCS include the revision of the Warehouse Manager JD to a logistics position  which has a functional comprehensive role and responsibility within BRCS.   •	Annual planning for the hurricane season (June 1 - Nov 30) includes a review of current stocks and pre-positioning of relief supplies for distribution.   •	Internal coordination between the DM Manager (preparedness and response plans), Finance Manager (procurement) and Warehouse (logistics and fleet) facilitates planning and accountability across BRCS but may also limit timeliness, consistency and quality given that key functions are not managed by a single unit.//•	Supply Chain Management (SCM) is shared across multiple BRCS units (DM, Warehouse, Resource Mobilization, Finance) and lacks specific SOPs for emergency response to provide guidance for both procedures and decision making.  •	Hurricane Dorian response operations lead by IFRC for impacted areas are not documented in the form of a manual or specific handover plan for the SCM function to BRCS.//•	Procurement is a function within Finance and requires coordination with both the DM unit and logistics at HQ level for shipment of equipment and supplies to branches.  •	SOPs for emergency need to be developed linked to the EOC. •	Procurement within response operations need to be updated with specific SOPs for processes that are shared by different BRCS units. These SOPs can be based on the current IFRC procurement manual used by BRCS.   •	No blacklist exists but this information is managed informally by BRCS as there are a limited number of suppliers available in-country.  •	Additional risk to BRCS emergency response is the lack of a formal pre-agreement for procurement //•	Fleet management and logistics functions are the responsibility of the Warehouse Manager but need to be formalized within the JD.  •	Fleet management manual and related SOPs during an emergency need to be finalized/formalized based on the Hurricane Dorian response.  •	Maintenance and repair, insurance and registration of vehicles is managed by Warehouse Manager in coordination with Finance.  •	Current fleet management procedures require that all vehicles are parked at a central HQ location, drivers, or staff complete logbooks daily and vehicle requests are managed 24 hours in advance.  •	One BRCS vehicle is a Toyota LC 4x4, but other vehicles are not appropriate for disaster response.// •	BRCS strengthened its warehouse capacity through the Dorian Hurricane Response with a dedicated 2 storey container facility at HQ level which functions as the central warehouse for all BRCS services/programs. These are 8 (eight) 40-foot containers welded together as a single warehouse with a walkway is designed to lift to the 2nd level. •	Rental companies are available locally for larger loads and BRCS has 2 forklifts for pallet jacks. There are limitations with the design, but it complies with the standard IFRC requirements for basic warehouse facilities (lack of climate control is a significant limitation for proper storage of some materials). •	Warehouse system with labelling and shelving allocated to each container in currently under development.//•	Overall functioning staff and volunteer management systems and practices allow for effective recruitment, supervision, support and encouragement of staff and volunteers. •	Initial volunteer orientation includes CoC, PSEA with subsequent additional training identified by each manager. Regular First Aid and recertification trainings are available as well.  •	BRCS responders/volunteers do not have official IDs, RC vests and T-shirts are used for visibility. •	BRCS is actively working on renewing the existing volunteer database (Excel) with IFRC to have all volunteers’ profiles, certificates, trainings etc. in one place •	BRCS Volunteers are insured through IFRC (covers up to 500 volunteers) but does not include COVID-19 coverage.  •	BRCS maintains diverse background/skills of responders and Volunteer Recruitment and Retention Strategy (approved February 2022) reinforces it. Plan for appreciation of volunteers is included in Volunteer Recruitment and Retention Strategy. •	NS does not have formal expedited procedures to incorporate spontaneous volunteers during emergencies however, there is a plan to reflect that in SOPs (currently under development).  •	There appears to be a challenge with the HR scale down after Hurricane Dorian response. Number of staff is reducing with the loss of IFRC and ARC support. Pandemic has also impacted resource mobilization to retain staff into 2022. •	EPC training has been conducted but not systematically.  •	NS takes measures for protecting its staff and volunteers during epidemics by following government mandates and protocols, and provision of PPEs. Vaccination is not mandatory but is encouraged.  •	CoC for Volunteers needs to be reviewed to include Zero Tolerance for Violence, PSEA, feedback mechanisms and whistle-blower policies. •	Systematic training and signing of HR Policy/Employee Handbook, CoC/PSEA and confidential reporting mechanisms need strengthening.

component_details.title: RC auxiliary role, Mandate and Law
component_details.description: A constitutional reference to the role of the NS in responding to disasters and crises, which may be legislated or included/ recognized in the National Response System.

component_details.title: DRM Strategy
component_details.description: An outline of the overall goal that the NS seeks to achieve in its disaster and crisis response operations. The goal considers: context analysis, ongoing/regular all-hazards risk assessments: it may define the target proportion of affected population that will be reached, and a definition of the areas/sectors where a NS will usually respond during an emergency.

component_details.title: DRM Policy
component_details.description: Reflects the NS mission, RCRC principles and mandate. It acknowledges other relevant NS policies, and aligns with the government policy (where applicable), incorporating the general rules that the NS will obey in order to achieve something (i.e mandate, strategy, etc.)

component_details.title: DRM Laws, Advocacy and Dissemination
component_details.description: Designed to support the NS in improving legal preparedness for disasters and crisis and to promote the use of the IDRL Guidelines in order to reduce human vulnerability.

component_details.title: Quality and accountability
component_details.description: Describes the essential elements of principled, accountable, and high-quality humanitarian action. The RCRC Movement provides support to the most vulnerable people in line with the Sphere and CHS standards, Code of Conduct for the RCRC Movement and NGOS in Disaster Relief and the Code for Good Partnership of the RCRC Movement, Gender & Diversity, inclusion and protection, BPI/ Do no harm, context-sensitive analysis, violence prevention, accountability to affected population and disability considerations, Community engagement and accountability (CEA).

component_details.title: Hazard, Context and Risk Analysis, Monitoring and Early Warning
component_details.description: Describes how the NS monitors and maps past, present and potential hazards, disasters and crises (e.g. hazard, vulnerability assessments, gathering information from communities and government authorities) and systematically evaluates the damage that could be caused by a potential disaster/crisis, the frequency, severity of the impact, and the alert the relevant areas to scale the preparedness actions to reduce population vulnerability.

component_details.title: Scenario planning
component_details.description: A set of practical operation plans that closely mirror the generic disaster or crisis response plan but are tailored to a specific hazard type (e.g. earthquake, dengue epidemic, floods, cyclone) and a specific scenario (i.e. number of people affected, their locations and other important factors).

component_details.title: Risk management
component_details.description: A mapping of the potential risks in every area, along with its related mitigation measures. Including financial, reputational, organizational risks etc.

component_details.title: Preparedness plans and budgets
component_details.description: Plans identifying organisational resources, determining roles and responsibilities, and developing policies, procedures and activities in order to reach a level of preparedness to be able to respond effectively to a disaster or crisis. Budgets ensure that the necessary financial support is secured to allow capacities to be built and readiness maintained.

component_details.title: Business continuity
component_details.description: A strategy to counter any potential or anticipated obstacles to effective functioning of the NS, with an eye to ensuring that personnel and assets are protected and able to function in the event of a disaster/crisis.

component_details.title: Emergency Response Procedures (SOPs)
component_details.description: Written guidelines that describe duties and rights of personnel, command structures, coordination with other organizations, and reporting requirements, etc. Includes detailed organogram, decision-making flow chart, and defined roles and responsibilities.

component_details.title: Response and recovery planning
component_details.description: A documented set of procedures for the disaster/crisis response and recovery process. Including use of local capacities, transition to recovery, type of activities and serivices provided during response and recovery activities and exit strategies, procedures for DREF & EA, and templates for planning, budgeting and accessing funds.

component_details.title: Pre-disaster meetings and agreements
component_details.description: A commitment to arrange meetings and agreements with Movement stakeholders and external actors to identify, plan for and address gaps for any upcoming disaster season (e.g. monsoon, floods or cyclones, or for any generic disaster/crisis event (e.g Epidemic, pandemic, confilict situations). Pre-disaster agreements should set out each partner's role in the event of a disaster/crisis.

component_details.title: Activation of regional and international support
component_details.description: Procedures for requesting and accepting regional and international support in operations, including triggering coordination mechanisms for funding, materials and human resources deployments.

component_details.title: CHEMICAL, BIOLOGICAL, RADIOLOGICAL AND NUCLEAR (CBRN) EMERGENCY PREPAREDNESS
MANAGEMENT OF DEAD BODIES TO FACILITATE THEIR IDENTIFICATION
NS-specific areas of intervention
component_details.description: Sector-specific or services provided by the NS in case of emergencies, it is in line with the NS mandate and legislation in country. It includes Community Based DP/DRR, Evacuation, Health in Emergencies, Epidemic and Pandemic, First aid, WASH, Food security and Livelihoods, Search and rRescue, Shelter, Management of dead bodies, RFL, Transition to recovery, and CBRN preparedness.

component_responses.notes: According to COVID-19 Preparedness Profile, CBHFA is active within BRCS with volunteers trained in Health in Emergencies, Communicable Disease Prevention, Beahviour Change

There is some basic coverage of operational components but overall, this area will require extensive development.  Care needs to be taken, though, to ensure the development of this capacity is right sized.  IFRC resources will need to be adjusted to the context and flat structure of the NS.  NS Specific Areas of Intervention are under discussion based on the national context, under served needs, opportunities and where BRCS aspires to build capacity.  Specific sectors that are part of the response and existing capacities are noted in the PER Assessment Tool October 2019. It is important to ensure that any capacity development and investments in sectors are comprehensive, using the benchmarks of best practice for that sector’s interventions. (From PER Surge Report, p.3)

component_details.title: Mapping of NS capacities
component_details.description: A list of the NS capacities including HR (staff, response teams and volunteers) and equipment that are available for disaster/crisis response. Teams could include branch and national response teams. This should be defined by technical speciality where relevant.

component_details.title: Early Action Mechanisms
component_details.description: Designed to translate warnings into anticipatory actions to help reduce the impact of specific disaster or crisis events. They focus on consolidating available forecasting information and putting procedures in place to ensure that a NS can act ahead of any disaster/crisis. Forecast-based financing is included within the scope of this area.

component_details.title: Cash Based Intervention (CBI)
component_details.description: An effective and flexible way, including all forms of cash and voucher-based assistance, to support people affected by emergencies, maintaining their dignity and choice, while fostering local economies. Cash should also be mainstreamed into other sectors (including Relief, shelter, livelihoods) and services (Logistics, Finance, etc.)

component_responses.notes: "The NS had previous experience in Cash Based Interventions but due to volunteer turnover, this capacity was no longer available in-house.  As this is a key modality for the Hurricane Dorian operation, additional capacity is being re-built. This modality could reduce the heavy workload of relief and food parcels by replacing stocks with cash."   This retains capacity built for any future responses." (From PER Surge Report, p.3)

component_details.title: Emergency Needs Assessment
component_details.description: Assess the extent and impact of the damage caused by the disaster/crisis and the degree of vulnerability of the affected population. The first step in any emergency response, such an assessment will identify the needs that require external intervention and the gaps to be filled. It is a vital component of the programme-planning process.

component_details.title: Affected population selection
component_details.description: Identification and selection of target Affected population for interventions, using a pre-defined set of criteria based on need and vulnerability. This includes consideration of specific vulnerabilities such as disability, age and gender.

component_details.title: Emergency Operations Centre (EOC)
component_details.description: A central command and control facility responsible for carrying out disaster/crisis management functions at a strategic level in an emergency situation. The common functions are to collect and analyze data; facilitate decision making that protects life and livelihoods; and disseminate those decisions to all concerned agencies and individuals. Generally located at the headquarter level of an organization.

component_details.title: Information Management (IM)
component_details.description: Ability to manage information including requesting, receiving, analyzing and disseminating as per its procedures and partner requirements (IFRC and public authorities in particular). There should be a clear digital/paper trail that documents what, when and how the NS has acted and provides key information for the development of Emergency Plan of Actions. Includes IM between levels, between departments and Situational Reports, mapping, visualisation of data, GO platform (IFRC).

component_details.title: Testing and Learning
component_details.description: Drills and Simulations allow the organization to test, identify and learn from the results of these type of exercises and incorporate learning into future preparedness and response planning.

component_details.title: Coordination with local community level responders
component_details.description: Engagement with Community Disaster Response Teams (CDRTs), through training, coordination, and the development of community disaster preparedness and response plans.

component_details.title: Cooperation with private sector
component_details.description: Mechanism that allows cooperation with private sector that often plays a strong role in response, particularly if there is impact on their staff and businesses. There is often a willingness to donate goods and services. Advance agreements help to expedite response actions.

component_details.title: Coordination with External Agencies and NGOs
component_details.description: Mechanism that facilitates coordination and collaboration with Non-Governmental Organization (NGO), both local and international NGOs, civil society organizations (CSOs) and United Nations agencies in country.

component_details.title: Civil Military Relations
component_details.description: Dialogue and interaction with military actors, essential to protect and promote humanitarian principles, avoid competition, minimize inconsistency and, when appropriate, pursue common goals.

component_details.title: Coordination with Movement
component_details.description: Mechanisms that facilitate the coordination with ICRC, IFRC, and PNS in-country.

component_responses.notes: "This area is a strength for BRCS.  The NS Movement Coordination   is through the IFRC Caribbean Country Cluster, under the American Regional Office. There are strong relationships between sister National Societies that were called upon and supported during this response either individually, through the RIT or with surge delegates. " (PER Surge Report, p. 4)

component_details.title: Coordination with authorities
component_details.description: Mechanism that facilitates coordination and cooperation with local and national authorities. It is connected to the NS auxiliary role for humanitarian assistance.

component_details.title: Staff and volunteer management
component_details.description: Well-functioning staff and volunteer management systems and practices allow for effective recruitment, supervision, support and encouragement of staff and volunteers.

component_details.title: Safety and security management
component_details.description: Addresses policy and procedures to ensure the safety of staff and volunteers. This include awareness, effective recruitment, training and management processes in place to ensure that personnel are capable of undertaking the roles demanded of them (from NS operational, management and leaders) according to the Stay Safe (IFRC) and Safer Access (ICRC). Based on safer access framework, including concepts of access, perception, identification and acceptance, and protection and violence prevention.

component_responses.notes: "Support areas  overall need to be enhanced as already identified by the BRCS OCAC' (PER Surge Presentation)

component_details.title: Communication in emergencies
component_details.description: Incorporates a system of public messaging to enable the NS to share timely, accurate information before, during, and after a disaster or crisis.

component_details.title: Operations Monitoring, Evaluation, Reporting and Learning
component_details.description: The PMERL is designed to implement a results-based planning, monitoring and evaluation system that provides an evidence base of NS performance, including relevance, efficiency, effectiveness, sustainability and impact. A reliable and trusted organization is accountable, providing transparent and timely information and building systems to strengthen data collection and reporting. It is data-driven, analytical and results-based.

component_details.title: Finance and Admin policy and emergency procedures
component_details.description: Overall budgeting, accounting, treasury, assets, financial reporting and financial services operations. it also includes the efficient delivery , cost effective and timely services to the NS. Pre-approved, auditable, expedited procedures that allow for flexibility during a disaster/crisis. These must meet transparency, oversight and accountability standards. Procedures may include faster approval processes, fewer signatures, different authority levels. The Emergency Procedures are activated for a specific period of time.

component_details.title: Information and Communication Technology (ICT)
component_details.description: Refers to technologies that provide access to information through telecommunications. This includes the Internet, wireless networks, mobile phones, radios and other communication mediums.

component_responses.notes: "Internal and external communications are uneven in the Society" (OCAC Findings Report) Need to "formalize the communications framework and develop monitoring and evaluation measures" (OCAC Findings Report)

component_details.title: Resource Mobilisation
component_details.description: A documented strategy for raising domestic funds from the government, private sector, general public and other in-country actors to support the national society’s response. This would include allocation of responsibilities, practical mechanisms for accepting funds and for being accountable on funds.

component_details.title: RC auxiliary role, Mandate and Law
component_details.description: A constitutional reference to the role of the NS in responding to disasters and crises, which may be legislated or included/ recognized in the National Response System.

component_responses.epi_considerations: Needs improvement. Through COVID 19, the NS gained exposure to epidemic risk management. However, plans only exists in relation to COVID-19. These plans therefore need to be updated to reflect more generalised epidemic best practices before the NS can move towards full recognition by local and public authorities.
component_responses.notes: Not everyone was aware of the mandate. Policies and legislation are in place but not eveyone is aware of them; Participants agree that while there are laws and policies that are of high quality that exists, some persons may not be aware of them; EPI- BRC now considered essential workers but the BRC needs to be incorporated into laws or proceedures; need to reach out to local authorites for the role of the BRC eg MOH

component_details.title: DRM Strategy
component_details.description: An outline of the overall goal that the NS seeks to achieve in its disaster and crisis response operations. The goal considers: context analysis, ongoing/regular all-hazards risk assessments: it may define the target proportion of affected population that will be reached, and a definition of the areas/sectors where a NS will usually respond during an emergency.

component_responses.epi_considerations: Exists, could be strengthened. The annex to the NDRP contained a Hazard Impact Analysis within which epidemics of varying scales were considered.
component_responses.notes: The DRM Strategy (National Disaster Response Plan (NDRP)) exists and provides the framework for a response to disasters within the jurisdiction of the Belize Red Cross (BRC). The NDRP is also in line with the IFRC’s Disaster Management stratify in the Caribbean. However, the NS acknowledges that staff and volunteers do not know much about the DRM Plan

component_details.title: DRM Policy
component_details.description: Reflects the NS mission, RCRC principles and mandate. It acknowledges other relevant NS policies, and aligns with the government policy (where applicable), incorporating the general rules that the NS will obey in order to achieve something (i.e mandate, strategy, etc.)

component_responses.epi_considerations: Exists, could be strengthened. The NDRP is a generalised document that outlines the steps to the taken in any emergency and so does not specifically clarify the roles and responsibilities of DM and health staff in epidemics to ensure technical leadership. However, within its annex, epidemics are considered as part of the risk assessment, Additionally, through the COVID-19 response, the NS has gained experience in mapping this component.
component_responses.notes: The NS has its own DRM Policy which is aligned to the IFRC Disaster Management Strategic Framework for the Caribbean and they also draw on IFRC policies when needed. It is inclusive and mentions the involvement of other critical sectors such as NEMO, District Emergency Managers, National Intervention Teams, branches and other teams within the BRC. Further dissemination of this document will improve the internal adherence by all staff and volunteers

component_details.title: DRM Laws, Advocacy and Dissemination
component_details.description: Designed to support the NS in improving legal preparedness for disasters and crisis and to promote the use of the IDRL Guidelines in order to reduce human vulnerability.

component_responses.epi_considerations: Exists, could be strengthened. As above
component_responses.notes: The NS is aware of and acknowledges the importance of IDRL humanitarian diplomacy. However, they need to provide supporting documents and/or examples to illustrate the command of this component. The NS acknowledged that while persons may be aware of IDRL, they may have not been trained and no focal point exists.

component_details.title: Quality and accountability
component_details.description: Describes the essential elements of principled, accountable, and high-quality humanitarian action. The RCRC Movement provides support to the most vulnerable people in line with the Sphere and CHS standards, Code of Conduct for the RCRC Movement and NGOS in Disaster Relief and the Code for Good Partnership of the RCRC Movement, Gender & Diversity, inclusion and protection, BPI/ Do no harm, context-sensitive analysis, violence prevention, accountability to affected population and disability considerations, Community engagement and accountability (CEA).

component_responses.epi_considerations: Throughout the COVID-19 pandemic, the NS has played a key role in national communication campaigns encouraging best health and safety practices.
component_responses.notes: The NS has mechanisms in place to ensure the affected populations are involved in all stages of the response. CEA engagement plans are considered based on the event but a singular CEA plan for the NS does not exist. The NS has persons trained in CEA in the headquarters and across some of the branches but there is no designated focal point. The NS has developed beneficiary satisfaction surveys to allow safe and accessible feedback mechanisms for impacted communities ad part of the operational and programmatic activities. The NS is placing focus on gender and inclusion across their activities. Improvement can be made through the development of policies to accompany many things being done in practice.

component_details.title: Scenario planning
component_details.description: A set of practical operation plans that closely mirror the generic disaster or crisis response plan but are tailored to a specific hazard type (e.g. earthquake, dengue epidemic, floods, cyclone) and a specific scenario (i.e. number of people affected, their locations and other important factors).

component_responses.epi_considerations: Exists, could be strengthened. Epidemic scenarios were taken into considered in the NDRP. The NS uses thresholds as provided by the government and response strategies are aligned with same.
component_responses.notes: As part of the NDRP, scenario planning formed part of the hazard analysis annex and included various levels of response. These also took into consideration the tole of public authorities such as the NDO. However, not all the branches were/are involved in the development of their plans in their area. As part of the planning process, the NS recognised their challenges and hazard impact sheets identify their ability to cope in various scenarios. While is so, contingency planning within the NS could be strengthened. Basis/broad scenario planning takes place but tends to lack the specificity required in contingency planning. Contingency plans are developed as needed based on the particular event. When developed, plans take into consideration coordination mechanisms

component_details.title: Risk management
component_details.description: A mapping of the potential risks in every area, along with its related mitigation measures. Including financial, reputational, organizational risks etc.

component_responses.epi_considerations: Exists, could be strengthened. NS ensures protection of first responders including contractors (capacities, inputs), taking into account the impact of fear, stigma and diseases-specific precautions. NS has identified trusted sources of communication to ensure community engagement and public health messaging. NS has policies and procedures to manage infected staff and volunteers through security briefings. Systems and procedures are in place to prevent fraud and corruption and reinforce acceptance, security and access.
component_responses.notes: While the NS does not have a dedicated focal point for risk management, the responsibility for this portfolio lies with HQ and/or branch managers who a liable for the safety of staff and volunteers. The NSs policies and practices do not allow persons to go into situations for which they are not trained. Identifying, evaluating and accounting for operational risks are part of the NSs standard operations. Improvement is needed in assessing and managing risks systematically and proactively. The NS has adopted and follows IFRC to prevent fraud and corruption and reinforce acceptance, security and access. The BRCS so follows requirements set out by donors to ensure their reputation is upheld. The NS acknowledged that they do not engage in crisis management.

component_details.title: Preparedness plans and budgets
component_details.description: Plans identifying organisational resources, determining roles and responsibilities, and developing policies, procedures and activities in order to reach a level of preparedness to be able to respond effectively to a disaster or crisis. Budgets ensure that the necessary financial support is secured to allow capacities to be built and readiness maintained.

component_responses.epi_considerations: Exists, could be strengthened. Disaster Preparedness for Epidemics is well coordinated between DM and Health teams. Epidemic preparedness gaps are identified based on risk analysis, response strategy and take into account the strengthening of support units. Financial gaps for epidemic preparedness or early actions are identified and the NS actively seeks resources and support
component_responses.notes: The BRCS has a nominated, trained focal point for disaster preparedness. Gaps in preparedness are identified and analysed through lessons learnt activities that are built into all operations and programmes and efforts are made to incorporate feedback and make improvements where possible. A recognised area of weakness for the NS is in financial preparedness as preparedness and early action are dependent on projects to support same. As such, the NS has a resource mobilisation strategy that actively seeks funding to ensure support community programmes that include preparedness activities. The NS is aware of emergency funding avenues through the Federation (eg DREF)

component_details.title: Business continuity
component_details.description: A strategy to counter any potential or anticipated obstacles to effective functioning of the NS, with an eye to ensuring that personnel and assets are protected and able to function in the event of a disaster/crisis.

component_responses.epi_considerations: Exists, could be strengthened. NS Business Continuity plan includes epidemics among major risks, but NS does not yet have agreements with donors to repurpose funds for epidemic control and management including early action.
component_responses.notes: COVID-19 has forced business continuity to the forefront. While there plan exist for COVID-19, no formal Continuity of Operations Plan exists. However, the Director General has the authority to make the decision to return to normal business and under what conditions. The NS follows donor procedures should funds need to be reallocated or repurposed for unexpected or emerging needs.

component_details.title: Emergency Response Procedures (SOPs)
component_details.description: Written guidelines that describe duties and rights of personnel, command structures, coordination with other organizations, and reporting requirements, etc. Includes detailed organogram, decision-making flow chart, and defined roles and responsibilities.

component_responses.epi_considerations: Partially exists. Roles and responsibilities for epidemic response strategy at the NS level take into consideration NS support to the MOH. While the NS does not have active participation in the MOH EOC, the NS has developed elements of support to the MoH including active participation in the MoH committees. Further, NS does not have specific SOPs for epidemic response are available, include all response phases (early warning, early action, emergency assessment, response planning, etc.) and standardized templates. Branches also do not have epidemic response SOPs agreed with local authorities and partners. Contact details exists to support DM and will be mirrored and integrated for epidemic response as tested through the COVID -19 response.
component_responses.notes: The NS has an EOC SOP which covers general operational procedures and protocols. It includes the responsibilities of staff, including both senior and operational management teams. While these SOPs exist at HQ, they do not exist across all branches as some branches are at different stages of development (only 2 of 7 branches have up to date branch SOPs in alignment with the NDRP). It is also not tailored to specific interventions and is not well known by staff and volunteers.

component_details.title: Response and recovery planning
component_details.description: A documented set of procedures for the disaster/crisis response and recovery process. Including use of local capacities, transition to recovery, type of activities and serivices provided during response and recovery activities and exit strategies, procedures for DREF & EA, and templates for planning, budgeting and accessing funds.

component_responses.epi_considerations: Exists, could be strengthened. Community response plans for epidemics are not available. The NS also has work to do adapting its epidemic response plan to changing contexts and emerging needs.  The NS does not have a policy for donation of medical items as this is not applicable but follows approved global guidance and protocols as it relates to PPE (eg donation of face masks).
component_responses.notes: When needed, the NS develops response plans in accordance with IFRC standards and takes into consideration community and other relevant stakeholders. The NS makes an effort to incorporate medium term planning initiatives (eg WATSAN interventions, backyard gardens, training of CDRTS for longer term community based interventions) into response plans that can transition to recovery.

component_details.title: Pre-disaster meetings and agreements
component_details.description: A commitment to arrange meetings and agreements with Movement stakeholders and external actors to identify, plan for and address gaps for any upcoming disaster season (e.g. monsoon, floods or cyclones, or for any generic disaster/crisis event (e.g Epidemic, pandemic, confilict situations). Pre-disaster agreements should set out each partner's role in the event of a disaster/crisis.

component_responses.epi_considerations: Partially exists. Coordination and management arrangements with MOH at national, district and local levels are formalised and regular community discussions on epidemics include health officials and other public sector officials in charge of the community. However, the NS does not engage in the importation of medicinal products as part of its mandate. Agreements regarding the supply of PPE are not pre-defined.
component_responses.notes: The NS has pre-disaster meetings with key stakeholders at least once per year (typically before hurricane season) and key staff are familiar with pre-disaster/crisis agreements and how to operationalize them in a response. While agreements are in line with NS policies and procedures and the NS adheres to the tenets of due diligence, they tend to be adhoc and not pre-determined or agreed. This is not limited to agreements with private entities, but also characterises interactions with public agencies as agreements do not exist with public authorities to facilitate expedited import of humanitarian aid and visas for incoming personnel.

component_details.title: Hazard, Context and Risk Analysis, Monitoring and Early Warning
component_details.description: Describes how the NS monitors and maps past, present and potential hazards, disasters and crises (e.g. hazard, vulnerability assessments, gathering information from communities and government authorities) and systematically evaluates the damage that could be caused by a potential disaster/crisis, the frequency, severity of the impact, and the alert the relevant areas to scale the preparedness actions to reduce population vulnerability.

component_responses.epi_considerations: Exists, could be strengthened. Zoonoses were not taken into consideration as part of this response. However, the NS has done work in CBHFA through Zika and Dengue projects and as part of the COVID response. As a key actor in National COVID response, coordination with MoH exists, and the NS has the capacity and regularly tracks the status of outbreaks/cases of infectious diseases. Improvements needs to made in understanding gender and diversity specific needs and issues of acceptance and security during epidemics.
component_responses.notes: The focal point for risk monitoring within the NS is the Disaster Management Coordinator. The NS has the capacity to collect and analyse primary and secondary hazard data /impact data and does so during emergencies which assists in beneficiary selection and as a support for programmatic activities/project proposals. As an annex to their disaster response plan, a hazard impact analysis is included. The hazard and impact analysis identifies the hazards that threaten the National Society, determines the risks that the hazards pose and assesses the impacts on the community and the Red Cross. While the NS has the capacity for risk mapping, concerns surround the regularity with which these exercises are conducted and the inclusion of communities in assessments as these tend to be project funded or only done through DANA. When collected, data is disaggregated.

component_responses.epi_considerations: The NS does not have early warning system for food contamination in epidemics and has SOPs for food distribution in quarantine nor technical staff for food assistance trained to identify needs and analyse market situation.
component_responses.notes: The NS decided to review this component as it recognised its importance and engages in some of the benchmarks outlined. The BRCS is engaged and coordinates with other organizations and networks (clusters) active in food aid distribution and has integrated food distribution in its response strategies.

component_responses.epi_considerations: Exists, could be strengthened.  The NS has the capacity and safety materials to inform at-risk communities about the causes and consequences of epidemics (Dengue, Zika, COVID-19). The NS has embedded measures to avoid fear and stigma in the assessment, planning and response phases. CDRTs are familiar with the NS epidemic response strategy and its complementarity with the national strategy and are trained and equipped to respond through partnership with local authorities.
component_responses.notes: The NS ensures participation of community representatives to reflect the needs and strengths of local population in the assessment, design, and planning of community-based preparedness activities. NS conducts regular awareness raising and public education on disasters or crises as a part of their CERT training sessions. Community based early warning and early action systems are in place. Community Disaster Response Team (CDRTs) are trained and equipped to handle local response in partnership with relevant local actors and have contingency plans. CDRTs are trained and equipped to handle local response in partnership with relevant local actors based on municipal plans. NS ensures that community assessments are inclusive, with appropriate representation done in an inclusive, gender, diversity and conflict sensitive way.

component_details.title: Mapping of NS capacities
component_details.description: A list of the NS capacities including HR (staff, response teams and volunteers) and equipment that are available for disaster/crisis response. Teams could include branch and national response teams. This should be defined by technical speciality where relevant.

component_responses.epi_considerations: Exists, could be strengthened. Capacities at NS level have been mapped in line with types of epidemic prone diseases and epidemic risks along with current capacity in terms of response teams and Community Engagement and Accountability (CEA). Available and needed PPE has been identified.
component_responses.notes: The NS has a focal point identified and available for each specific area of intervention and services to provide technical guidance and support covered in National Disaster Plan and EOC SOPs. The staff and volunteers are trained and kept up to date, along with response materials and equipment database (some items need to be updated at branch level). The NS does not believe resources (HR and equipment) are available and sufficient to cover the initial response needs. However, NS has mapped levels of response as described in the NDRP (single family, local, regional etc). Mechanisms are in place to share resources amongst branches/regions and to trigger international assistance as needed.

component_responses.epi_considerations: Partially exists. While some of these indicators do not apply to the NS (management of dead bodies, disposal of PPE), the BRCS ensures that staff and volunteers supporting NS health care services have appropriate training and regular refresher trainings on communicable diseases and epidemic control. The NS also supports the government during outbreaks.
component_responses.notes: There is no specific Health Plan in place that set guidance surrounding the NS role in emergencies outside of its national mandate for the provision of First Aid. First Aid distribution is contained within the BRCS National Disaster Response Plan. As part of its mandate, the BRCS does not align itself with the management of dead bodies or medical equipment. However, the NS has procedures, data collection and feedback mechanisms in place to ensure community engagement in prevention and response interventions and safety protocols in place for paid staff and volunteers, for infection prevention and control within epidemics. While the NS is currently involved with the response to the COVID-19 Pandemic, there have been substantial progress towards the development a Health Response Plan.

component_details.title: Early Action Mechanisms
component_details.description: Designed to translate warnings into anticipatory actions to help reduce the impact of specific disaster or crisis events. They focus on consolidating available forecasting information and putting procedures in place to ensure that a NS can act ahead of any disaster/crisis. Forecast-based financing is included within the scope of this area.

component_responses.epi_considerations: Needs improvement. Early Action mechanism in case of epidemics is not formalized with MoH, including triggers. However, the NS has appropriate mechanisms to communicate key messages and protection actions for contamination mitigation to the branches, which have functioning local networks to inform communities of potential risks
component_responses.notes: The NS does not have early warning early action system - inclusive of Forecast-based Financing and disease surveillance as part of the national Early Warning Early Action strategies and preparedness system. However, the NS has mechanisms to anticipate and respond to major hazards in coordination with the national system. NS has procedures and personnel permanently available, to communicate alerts and initiate early action to all levels of the NS by establishing alternative point of contacts if primary contacts are unavailable. The NS makes use of new technologies appropriate for the context and audiences for sending alert messages related to early action (e.g: text, twitter, email, SMS).

component_details.title: Cash Based Intervention (CBI)
component_details.description: An effective and flexible way, including all forms of cash and voucher-based assistance, to support people affected by emergencies, maintaining their dignity and choice, while fostering local economies. Cash should also be mainstreamed into other sectors (including Relief, shelter, livelihoods) and services (Logistics, Finance, etc.)

component_responses.epi_considerations: Partially Exists. Cash transfer programme is not tailored to face the challenges of infectious disease outbreaks.
component_responses.notes: The NS has experience with CBI through previous emergency response (Flood response in 2020). As part of the emergency response CBI Training was conducted for staff and volunteers and records have been kept of persons as part of volunteer profiles for further support to CBI services for the NS. However, the NS does not have a CBI plan and the requisite SOPs.

component_details.title: Emergency Needs Assessment
component_details.description: Assess the extent and impact of the damage caused by the disaster/crisis and the degree of vulnerability of the affected population. The first step in any emergency response, such an assessment will identify the needs that require external intervention and the gaps to be filled. It is a vital component of the programme-planning process.

component_responses.epi_considerations: Partially Exists. Data collection templates for epidemics needs assessment are available to include CBS, health services etc. Emergency multi-sectoral assessment team is trained on Infection prevention and control but is not reflective of all epidemics at this time.
component_responses.notes: The NS has standardised templates and trained multi-sectorial emergency assessment team available to deploy in a timely manner to collect and report on primary and secondary disaggregated data. Emergency plans of action are based on the needs assessment results, which takes into consideration existing capacities and analyses the national and international capacities, responses and gaps. Emergency needs assessments also analyse secondary risk, specific needs/concerns of vulnerable people.

component_details.title: Affected population selection
component_details.description: Identification and selection of target Affected population for interventions, using a pre-defined set of criteria based on need and vulnerability. This includes consideration of specific vulnerabilities such as disability, age and gender.

component_responses.epi_considerations: Needs Improvement. The BRCS has a policy to share personal data with operational actors (i.e. contact tracing) via their confidentiality and disclosure agreement.
component_responses.notes: The BRCS prides itself on its ability to reach the most vulnerable within impacted populations. The NS communicates selection criteria to the affected population using appropriate and established communication channels and involves community leaders/representatives. The selection criteria is made very clear and is printed, as well as distributed to make sure it is clearly identified to impacted persons. It identifies appropriate selection criteria based on existing vulnerability and taking into consideration gender, diversity, age and disabilities. Responders have been trained in data collection by using standardised templates, there is a mechanism to cross-check that data, and the NS protects data collected from affected population.

component_details.title: Emergency Operations Centre (EOC)
component_details.description: A central command and control facility responsible for carrying out disaster/crisis management functions at a strategic level in an emergency situation. The common functions are to collect and analyze data; facilitate decision making that protects life and livelihoods; and disseminate those decisions to all concerned agencies and individuals. Generally located at the headquarter level of an organization.

component_responses.epi_considerations: Needs Improvement. Health EOCs are established on a case by case basis. When needed, the EOC structure includes decision-making responsibilities for health staff, and how NS EOC supports the national EOC. The roles of health managers within the EOC are clear.
component_responses.notes: The NS has a formally appointed focal point for EOC and SOPs detailed in the NDRP and the EOC SOP. EOC protocols are activated as needed and contains activation and call out, a concept of operations, response levels and deactivation protocols. EOC does not have intended space with sufficient equipment to manage information and coordination without affecting other NS activities, nor are its facilities are self-sufficient with at least power, water and telecommunications with functioning back-up. The alternate EOC is mobile and allows for key functions to continue. The EOC is not operated on a 24/7 basis and so does note require rotational staff.

component_details.title: Information Management (IM)
component_details.description: Ability to manage information including requesting, receiving, analyzing and disseminating as per its procedures and partner requirements (IFRC and public authorities in particular). There should be a clear digital/paper trail that documents what, when and how the NS has acted and provides key information for the development of Emergency Plan of Actions. Includes IM between levels, between departments and Situational Reports, mapping, visualisation of data, GO platform (IFRC).

component_responses.epi_considerations: Needs improvement.  Key staff at headquarters and branch level are familiar with IM templates (these may be the NS or IFRC), methodology and procedures specific to epidemics. However, there are no specific SOPs for data sharing in epidemics are not available. Ongoing scenario plans and response options are documented and filed and Go reports are shared.
component_responses.notes: The NS has key staff at HQ and branch level are familiar with IM templates, methodology and procedures, and have access to equipment to compile, visualise and share information. The NS has a system at HQ to store and share files with emergency personnel. The NS has access to updated data on high-risk areas (demographic, socio-economic) disaggregated by age, gender and disability via the Statistical Institute of Belize. There is a standardised Situation Report format that is utilized at all levels and these reports are analysed to adapt response plans. NS has mechanisms to share information across levels, sectors and support services.

component_details.title: Testing and Learning
component_details.description: Drills and Simulations allow the organization to test, identify and learn from the results of these type of exercises and incorporate learning into future preparedness and response planning.

component_responses.epi_considerations: Does not exists. Epidemic considerations are not considered for this component.
component_responses.notes: The NS does not regularly test its early action and response system through simulation and drills and as such, do not draw lessons from same. However, when simulations and drills are conducted, they are done in conjunction with national authorities and other organisations. They also include access, acceptance, security and the practical application of the Fundamental Principles in their simulations and drills when conducted.

component_details.title: Activation of regional and international support
component_details.description: Procedures for requesting and accepting regional and international support in operations, including triggering coordination mechanisms for funding, materials and human resources deployments.

component_responses.epi_considerations: This component was not reviewed as the National Society does not deal with medical personnel or supplies as part of its mandate
component_responses.notes: The NS key staff are familiar with the available IFRC support (technical, financial, material and HR). The mechanism to coordinate response with respective IFRC offices is widely understood and IFRC protocols are followed. NS procedures include instructions to request and incorporate regional and global support/teams into their response system, including prior to imminent crisis/disaster, and assigns a focal point to act as counterpart to regional/international responders. NS informs IFRC within 24 hours for which assistance may be required. NS is familiar with the IFRC emergency funding mechanisms and can request bilateral assistance in accordance with established coordination frameworks. BRCS liaises with the CCD to interact and coordinate initially with regional/international responders.

component_details.title: CHEMICAL, BIOLOGICAL, RADIOLOGICAL AND NUCLEAR (CBRN) EMERGENCY PREPAREDNESS

component_responses.epi_considerations: Does not exist. Markets as potential sources of transmission have not been mapped by the NS. Additionally, epidemic-prone areas are not identified, whereby risks to community and household productive assets are outlined in a plan for protecting assets at the NS. NS is not in the position to support business continuity planning for private sector actors (especially Small and Medium Enterprises) at this time.
component_responses.notes: Livelihoods is not currently incorporated into NS DRM strategy, plans, systems and procedures. However, the NS has volunteers who are trained in livelihoods data collection through previous emergency responses. While there is no set standardized primary plan in place, the NS uses this component to fulfil its response modalities.

component_details.title: MANAGEMENT OF DEAD BODIES TO FACILITATE THEIR IDENTIFICATION

component_responses.epi_considerations: The NS does  not carry out RFL in epidemics due to separation in isolation.
component_responses.notes: This component was reviewed as the NS recognises its importance. While the NS staff and volunteers are capable of provide quality RFL services and procedures and agreements with IFRC and ICRC on RFL are in place, the NS has not engaged in this activity. The NS is part of the regional RFL network and actively takes part in meetings with other NSs and stakeholders.

component_details.title: NS-specific areas of intervention
component_details.description: Sector-specific or services provided by the NS in case of emergencies, it is in line with the NS mandate and legislation in country. It includes Community Based DP/DRR, Evacuation, Health in Emergencies, Epidemic and Pandemic, First aid, WASH, Food security and Livelihoods, Search and rRescue, Shelter, Management of dead bodies, RFL, Transition to recovery, and CBRN preparedness.

component_responses.epi_considerations: Exists, could be strengthened. NS has Infection Prevention and Control policies and procedures to accompany first aid responders in an infectious disease outbreak.
component_responses.notes: As part of its NDRP, the BRCS outlines the provision of First Aid. As such, first aid training is part of the NSs CBDRR strategy and is a key income generating activity for the NS.

component_responses.epi_considerations: Exists, could be strengthened. NS includes WASH measures in its response strategies in case of epidemics, and response teams are familiar with WASH in infectious settings including environmental sanitation.
component_responses.notes: Water and Sanitation initiatives formed part of the BRCS’ response for many years at the community level. As such, the NS has trained technical personnel to support in emergency WASH interventions. The NS has the required equipment to provide quality WASH services or clear SOPs on how to obtain this equipment (in-country or via IFRC) and  coordinates with other organizations and networks active in WASH in the country.

component_responses.epi_considerations: Does not exist. The NS does not have the capacity for CBHFA in epidemics.
component_responses.notes: While there are trained CBHFA focal points, the NS was unable to deploy this methodology across the NS (including branches) as there are inadequate human resources to effectively do so. most in part due to the limitations associated with the current pandemic. Notwithstanding, the NS is able to use elements of CBHFA in their community engagement while supporting the National Response to COVID 19 and the recent flooding responses.

component_details.title: Civil Military Relations
component_details.description: Dialogue and interaction with military actors, essential to protect and promote humanitarian principles, avoid competition, minimize inconsistency and, when appropriate, pursue common goals.

component_responses.epi_considerations: Partially exists. The NS does not have coordination mechanisms specific to epidemic risk management. However, if an epidemic situation escalates and takes a national security angle, resulting in restrictions impacting the ability of responders to move, NS is prepared to ensure the protection of humanitarian space.
component_responses.notes: The NS does not have direct contact with the military. However, the NS is exposed to engagement with the Military via the NDO who coordinates on their behalf. The NS ensures that all security protocols (eg no weapons) are followed when utilising military resources. This is only done on an as needed basics and is typically limited to accessing transport to and from impacted areas.

component_details.title: Coordination with Movement
component_details.description: Mechanisms that facilitate the coordination with ICRC, IFRC, and PNS in-country.

component_responses.epi_considerations: This component was not reviewed as the National Society does not deal with medical personnel or supplies as part of its mandate
component_responses.notes: The BRCS is part of the IFRC’s Port of Spain Country Cluster Delegation and are in constant coordination with movement partners to share information on needs assessments, plans of action, progress against operations and operational capacities and emerging gaps in resources. The BRCS has a positive working relationship with its neighbouring NSs and utilises different communication channels to share information and coordinate response actions when required. The NS is guided by and utilises IFRC policies and procedures to ensure that there are systems in place to liaise with the IFRC and Movement Partners to accept international assistance.

component_details.title: Coordination with authorities
component_details.description: Mechanism that facilitates coordination and cooperation with local and national authorities. It is connected to the NS auxiliary role for humanitarian assistance.

component_responses.epi_considerations: Exists, could be strengthened. The NS is aware of national authorities' capacities for epidemic prevention and control and identifies areas within a response to fulfil their auxiliary role. The also play and active role in risk communication and engagement at the community and National level. The NS ensures that their emblem is respected and appropriately utilised.
component_responses.notes: The NS knows their role in the national response framework and keeps regular communication with the RCRC and other national agencies to ensure assistance can be effectively given in times of emergency. The NS knows the capacities of national authorities and identifies areas within a response to fulfil their auxiliary role. It has control over its resources, assets and emblem when responding. The NS is part of the national response framework and is in communication with the relevant authorities should their services be needed, through some areas of intervention are not fully established.

component_details.title: Coordination with local community level responders
component_details.description: Engagement with Community Disaster Response Teams (CDRTs), through training, coordination, and the development of community disaster preparedness and response plans.

component_responses.epi_considerations: Exists, could be strengthened. The staff and volunteers of the BRCS have been classified and first responders through COVID-19 response. This is allowed them to be able to establish coordination of mechanisms specific to epidemic risk management (e.g. with limited number of key available staff and volunteers, security/access limitations). These are however guided by National protocols and restrictions to ensure safety and security for all involved.
component_responses.notes: Coordination with CDRTs is one the stronger areas for the BRCS. Hazard impact data are articulated by the branches to the headquarters when needed in an emergency. CDRTs and branches also have a positive working relationship with key actors and stakeholders within their communities.  However, there are communication gaps within the NS. Branches development must take precedent and communication between Branches and HQ can be improved. HQ is currently the lead for implementation and response planning, and it does not happen at branch level. BRCS aims to get branches to be implementers and establish HQ as overall oversight. Information from communities should more strongly inform decision-making at branches and headquarters.

component_details.title: Cooperation with private sector
component_details.description: Mechanism that allows cooperation with private sector that often plays a strong role in response, particularly if there is impact on their staff and businesses. There is often a willingness to donate goods and services. Advance agreements help to expedite response actions.

component_responses.epi_considerations: Exists, could be strengthened. Coordination mechanisms specific to epidemic risk management (e.g. partnership with communication or PPE providers, protection of corporate partner volunteers) partially exists as it is done on an as needed basis.
component_responses.notes: NS ensures due diligence when selecting partners and accepting donations to mitigate image or reputational risk and donations are forthcoming from reputable sources. BRCS ensures appropriate use of emblem and protect the organization's visual identity.  Volunteer policy speaks to corporate volunteers and was updated. The NS has a volunteer database that is populated and updated regularly to train and use volunteers from corporate partners.

component_details.title: Coordination with External Agencies and NGOs
component_details.description: Mechanism that facilitates coordination and collaboration with Non-Governmental Organization (NGO), both local and international NGOs, civil society organizations (CSOs) and United Nations agencies in country.

component_responses.epi_considerations: Exists, could be strengthened. While the BRCS does not have coordination mechanisms specific to epidemic risk management, the NS is actively engaged in the country’s health security agenda, adopting a OneHealth approach and has identified partners it works closely with and discussed coordination mechanisms for epidemic risk management
component_responses.notes: The NS is part of the regional humanitarian network and actively participates in knowledge sharing best practices. BRCS is an active member of the humanitarian community (UN, NGO) for coordination and efficiency of response. NS is aware of IFRC's role in the shelter cluster coordination and UN-led appeal and strategic processes. In this case UN would come to the cluster office and CCD will liaise with NS. The NS does not have partnership agreements with key emergency response UN/NGO partners in country are formalized and shared between branches and headquarters.

component_details.title: Staff and volunteer management
component_details.description: Well-functioning staff and volunteer management systems and practices allow for effective recruitment, supervision, support and encouragement of staff and volunteers.

component_responses.epi_considerations: Exists, could be strengthened. The NS does not conduct regular training of key staff on epidemic prevention and control at all levels (HQ, high-risk branches, volunteers). However, they do ensure that measures are taken to protect staff and volunteers, by limiting their risk exposure or enhancing safety and protection measures. While labour laws may not be consulted, the NS ensures that the competences and permissions required for the task are followed. Insurance (Federation) and PSS are provided for volunteers.
component_responses.notes:
The BRCS deploys and equips responders according to needs of the situation (may not be an official TOR) and safety and security briefings have been institutionalised in accordance with the volunteer policy.  Through trainings offered by the IFRC and/or partnerships, the NS has learning paths for responders to obtain required qualifications and skills according to competencies and role profiles. However, not all volunteers are trained in quality and accountability standards (Sphere, Code of Conduct, etc...) around the protection, sexual abuse, exploitation, child protection, gender-based violence and other forms of abuse and the NS is working to ensure that all volunteers are trained in same. Responders have official updated ID recognised by authorities and appropriate visibility items. 

Through their branches and in collaboration with HQ, the NS is able to activate, deploy and manage branch and national response teams. Levels of response are also outlined in the NDRP. The NS has expedited procedures to incorporate spontaneous volunteers during emergencies which meet minimum screening procedures and comply with its volunteer in emergency policy and provides insurance to all volunteers (Federation insurance) and requires that all volunteers sign the code of conduct. While the NS does not typically operate on a 24/7 basis, when required, personnel are rotated to ensure continuity.  

For scenarios that entail safety and/or security concerns for staff and volunteers, a specific Safer Access analysis is conducted. Additionally, training on self-care, violence and harassment in the workplace is completed regularly, and psychosocial support is available for staff and volunteers during and after emergencies and crises. As part of the BRCS volunteer policy, it is the responsibility to cover expenses incurred by responders in an emergency.

component_details.title: Safety and security management
component_details.description: Addresses policy and procedures to ensure the safety of staff and volunteers. This include awareness, effective recruitment, training and management processes in place to ensure that personnel are capable of undertaking the roles demanded of them (from NS operational, management and leaders) according to the Stay Safe (IFRC) and Safer Access (ICRC). Based on safer access framework, including concepts of access, perception, identification and acceptance, and protection and violence prevention.

component_responses.epi_considerations: Needs improvement. NS has conducted a protection, gender and inclusion (PGI) analysis to put a gender and culturally appropriate security system in place to protect all staff and volunteers from the risk of epidemics. However, all responders are not trained in PGI and are aware of gender specific safety and security requirements during epidemics.
component_responses.notes: NS implements Safer Access and has appropriate security systems in place to protect staff and volunteers, as a part of mandatory volunteer and staff training prior to appointment. The NS has trained staff at headquarters and branches who are appointed and accountable for safety and security. Context and risk analysis information are divulged to teams before they are deployed, before any emergency a proper briefing is done. A safety and security policy and a compliance system exist to monitor staff and volunteers and all staff and volunteers know the NS safety and security rules and procedures and follow them. NS has communication mechanisms for staff and volunteers to report safety and security risks and incidents. However, responders have not been trained in Safer Access, Stay Safe and managers have completed security management training.

component_details.title: Communication in emergencies
component_details.description: Incorporates a system of public messaging to enable the NS to share timely, accurate information before, during, and after a disaster or crisis.

component_responses.epi_considerations: Exists, could be strengthened. Key messages and public awareness messages for specific epidemics are available and shared with staff regularly. NS also has as a rumour management system (hotline, social media) for epidemics
component_responses.notes: The NS has a communication policy dated 2016 that provides guidelines for communication at the NS, including the use of social media. The NS acknowledges that this needs to be updated. The NS has a communication focal point at HQ but not at not branch level. The DG speaks on behalf of the NS during an emergency. Standard templates for communication also exist. While the NS does not operate on a 24/7 basis, information from national agencies are reshared as needed. Key messages and public awareness messages in an emergency are developed and shared with staff regularly, via WhatsApp, email. The NS tracks negative media and social media to react accordingly via the hotline, social media monitoring. The BRCS is also supported by the POS CCD when needed in emergencies

component_details.title: Operations Monitoring, Evaluation, Reporting and Learning
component_details.description: The PMERL is designed to implement a results-based planning, monitoring and evaluation system that provides an evidence base of NS performance, including relevance, efficiency, effectiveness, sustainability and impact. A reliable and trusted organization is accountable, providing transparent and timely information and building systems to strengthen data collection and reporting. It is data-driven, analytical and results-based.

component_responses.epi_considerations: Exists, could be strengthened. The NS recognises as caters for the gaps created in PMER by an outbreak (eg. with limited number of key staff and volunteers available). The BRCS also has a system to monitor community feedback and rumours during epidemics in place.
component_responses.notes: There is no designated M&E focal point in the NS; M&E is done as part of the NSs work but there is not data system in place; M&E related to field work captured through DANA forms. There were discussions with respect to the difference between operations, projects and programmes as terms were being used by the NS which were not necessarily in line with the components. BRCS does not have a dedicated PMER function for emergency operations with adequate human and financial resources. NS refers to and uses lessons from previous operations in response planning (e.g. from evaluation, review and operational reports) from the lessons learnt Workshops and when needed, operational plans are revised based on intended and unintended outcomes in collaboration with the IFRC POS CCD. The NS also reports to partners in line with agreement, using appropriate templates. While there is no separate M&E Plan, M&E is built into programmes and projects and is included in budgets (including lessons learnt activities). When in the field, volunteers and staff have a standardised DANA template that is accompanied by a briefing and debriefing

component_details.title: Finance and Admin policy and emergency procedures
component_details.description: Overall budgeting, accounting, treasury, assets, financial reporting and financial services operations. it also includes the efficient delivery , cost effective and timely services to the NS. Pre-approved, auditable, expedited procedures that allow for flexibility during a disaster/crisis. These must meet transparency, oversight and accountability standards. Procedures may include faster approval processes, fewer signatures, different authority levels. The Emergency Procedures are activated for a specific period of time.

component_responses.epi_considerations: Needs improvement. While there is no set plan or procedure in place, finance and administration processes are not particularly affected during epidemics as the NS staff and volunteers have are classed as first responders and so typically have access to the resources needed for work to continue.
component_responses.notes:
There is a gap bet HQ and the branches when to comes to reporting; Component needs improvement overall; standarisation, coordination with braches. While proceedures are followed but there are not set SOPs or guildelines for the NS to follow or if the NS has it the policy is it done in practice. 
The NS has an automated accounting and financial system and procedures to account for and report on funds and expenditures on a regular basis. NS has trained personnel in Finance and Admin emergency support procedures and works closely with the IFRC to ensure that reports are to standard. The NS has adopted IFRC protocols to ensure transparency and has in place systems and procedures for control and oversight to prevent acts of fraud and/or corruption during an emergency.
