Cash should also be mainstreamed into other sectors (including Relief, shelter, livelihoods) and services (Logistics, Finance, etc.)

component_responses.epi_considerations: Non
component_responses.notes:
Le plan de préparation des IBAC (Interventions Basées sur l'Analyse des Catastrophes) n'existe pas au sein de la SN.
Quelque volontaire a été formé sur les IBAC.
La Société Nationale (SN) ne dispose pas d'une analyse de faisabilité financière pré-catastrophe ni de références concernant les systèmes de marché, les prix et la saisonnalité. 
Toutefois, elle possède une idée générale de la cartographie des autres acteurs et structures de coordination, bien que cette information ne soit pas formellement documentée.
Aucun processus de révision des SOP (Standard Operating Procedures) n'a été effectué depuis 2018.
La SN ne dispose pas d'une boîte à outils dédiée aux IBAC.
Implications: 
L'absence d'un plan de préparation des IBAC et d'une analyse des risques limite la capacité de la SN à répondre de manière proactive et adaptée aux catastrophes.
Le manque de formation des volontaires sur les IBAC et l'absence de révision des SOP depuis 2018 nuisent à l'efficacité et à la réactivité des interventions en cas de crise.
L'absence d'une analyse financière pré-catastrophe et d'une boîte à outils dédiée complique la gestion optimale des ressources et la mise en œuvre rapide des interventions humanitaires

component_details.title: Emergency Needs Assessment
component_details.description: Assess the extent and impact of the damage caused by the disaster/crisis and the degree of vulnerability of the affected population. The first step in any emergency response, such an assessment will identify the needs that require external intervention and the gaps to be filled. It is a vital component of the programme-planning process.

component_responses.notes:
Il n’existe pas un département de PMER au niveau de la SN
Les outils sont élaborés en fonctions des situations 
Peu de volontaires disposent d’une capacite pour la collecte 
Pendant les opérations précédant c’est le PMER du cluster Addis Ababa qui appuie la SN 
Implication: 
lorsque les équipes ne  connaissent les modèles, la collecte de données démarre tardivement car il faut toujours un briefing. 
Lorsque les modèles sont les mêmes, les données collectées sont analysées de façon systématique et efficace.

component_details.title: Affected population selection
component_details.description: Identification and selection of target Affected population for interventions, using a pre-defined set of criteria based on need and vulnerability. This includes consideration of specific vulnerabilities such as disability, age and gender.

component_responses.notes:
Absence de bases claires pour les critères d’identification des bénéficiaires.
Manque d’un mécanisme de sélection communautaire. 
Non-communication des critères par les branches. 
Absence de mesures spécifiques pour la protection des données des populations affectées, en particulier en période d’épidémie. 
Implications: 
1. L'absence de critères de sélection clairs peut générer des incompréhensions.  
2. Une communication insuffisante des critères risque de frustrer la population.  
3. Une mauvaise compréhension des choix peut exposer les équipes à des risques.

component_details.title: Emergency Operations Centre (EOC)
component_details.description: A central command and control facility responsible for carrying out disaster/crisis management functions at a strategic level in an emergency situation. The common functions are to collect and analyze data; facilitate decision making that protects life and livelihoods; and disseminate those decisions to all concerned agencies and individuals. Generally located at the headquarter level of an organization.

component_responses.notes:
Inexistence du COU
Un point focal  n'est nommé de manière formelle pour le COU 
Le mécanisme n'exite pas au sein de la SN 
Implications: 
1. L'absence de point focal et de mécanisme structuré entraîne une désorganisation dans la gestion des urgences.  
2. L'inexistence du COU limite l'efficacité et la crédibilité de la SN, compromettant l'aide aux populations vulnérables.

component_details.title: Information Management (IM)
component_details.description: Ability to manage information including requesting, receiving, analyzing and disseminating as per its procedures and partner requirements (IFRC and public authorities in particular). There should be a clear digital/paper trail that documents what, when and how the NS has acted and provides key information for the development of Emergency Plan of Actions. Includes IM between levels, between departments and Situational Reports, mapping, visualisation of data, GO platform (IFRC).

component_responses.epi_considerations: La SN ne dispose pas de procédures opérationnelles standard (SOP) spécifiques pour les épidémies, notamment en ce qui concerne la protection des données personnelles.
component_responses.notes:
Aucune documentation, méthodologie ni procédure formelle pour la Gestion de l'Information (GI).
Équipements disponibles pour la gestion de l'information (imprimantes, scanners, projecteurs), mais un accompagnement est nécessaire pour une utilisation optimale.
Système de mail professionnel en place et possibilité de créer une banque de stockage. Un serveur est nécessaire pour améliorer la gestion et l’accès aux données.
Les informations et décisions sont archivées au niveau national et régional. Des rapports existants, bien que non standardisés, documentent la situation et les actions, notamment lors des opérations avec la FICR.
Absence de procédures opérationnelles standard (SOP) spécifiques pour les épidémies, notamment en matière de protection des données personnelles.
Implications:
Sans procédures de gestion de l’information, les données cruciales provenant du terrain risquent de ne pas parvenir aux personnes clés.
Les données personnelles non protégées exposent les individus à des risques, notamment en période d’épidémie.
Les décisions importantes peuvent être perdues en cours de route et ne pas être institutionnalisées pour l’avenir.

component_details.title: Testing and Learning
component_details.description: Drills and Simulations allow the organization to test, identify and learn from the results of these type of exercises and incorporate learning into future preparedness and response planning.

component_responses.notes:
Les exercices de simulation ne sont pas organisés de manière régulière par la SN
Il n'y a pas de révision régulière de la procédure.
Implications:
1. Sans évaluer les problèmes d'accès et de sécurité, les équipes risquent d'être bloquées sur le terrain.
2. De mauvaises perceptions de la Société Nationale, alimentées par des rumeurs (notamment en période d’épidémie), pourraient mettre les équipes en danger, voire les exposer à des attaques.

component_details.title: Activation of regional and international support
component_details.description: Procedures for requesting and accepting regional and international support in operations, including triggering coordination mechanisms for funding, materials and human resources deployments.

component_responses.notes:
Collaboration directe avec la FICR à Addis-Abeba, mais aucun appui du CICR depuis mai 2023.  
Appels fréquents aux équipes régionales et internes, avec un délai d'intervention dépassant 24 heures.  
Maîtrise des procédures du DREF et de l’appel d’urgence, incluant la préparation de l’EPoA.  
Le Secrétaire Général est le principal coordonnateur pour les interventions internationales
implication 
1. L’absence d’appui du CICR depuis Mai 2023 limite les capacités opérationnelles de la SN.  
2. Les délais d’intervention prolongés affectent l’efficacité des réponses d’urgence.  
3. Sans soutien rapide, l’exploitation des mécanismes d’urgence comme le DREF est compromise.

component_details.title: Coordination with Movement
component_details.description: Mechanisms that facilitate the coordination with ICRC, IFRC, and PNS in-country.

component_responses.notes:
La coordination respecte les principes du Mouvement, mais un renforcement est nécessaire, notamment avec le CICR.  
Les échanges entre le siège et les branches se font principalement par appels et rapports.  
Un cadre formel est requis pour améliorer la collaboration et l’efficacité des interventions avec les partenaires. 
Implications: 
Une coordination régulière permettrait de mieux identifier les capacités et les besoins des interventions.
Informer les partenaires sur les progrès favoriserait une meilleure implication. 
Une telle coordination encouragerait les partenaires à apporter un soutien technique et autre à divers stades de la réponse.

component_details.title: Coordination with authorities
component_details.description: Mechanism that facilitates coordination and cooperation with local and national authorities. It is connected to the NS auxiliary role for humanitarian assistance.

component_responses.notes:
La SN est intégrée au système de coordination humanitaire national et y contribue activement.  
Elle informe sur les capacités du Mouvement CRCR pour mobiliser un appui international en cas de besoin. 
Un plaidoyer est nécessaire pour renforcer son rôle et ses capacités dans ce système. 
Implications: 
Une analyse et une planification solides permettent à la SN de clarifier son rôle et ses capacités dans la réponse.
L'ignorance des autorités nationales et locales sur le rôle de la CRD peut retarder ou entraver l'intervention.
L'utilisation incorrecte de l'emblème peut compromettre la sécurité des équipes et affecter l'image de la SN.

component_details.title: Coordination with External Agencies and NGOs
component_details.description: Mechanism that facilitates coordination and collaboration with Non-Governmental Organization (NGO), both local and international NGOs, civil society organizations (CSOs) and United Nations agencies in country.

component_responses.notes:
La SN collabore avec l'UNICEF pour la gestion du risque épidémique.  
Il n'y a pas d'activités coordonnées avec d'autres ONG impliquant des acteurs spécifiques.  
Le siège participe activement aux réunions avec les agences et ONG.
Implications: 
Une coordination efficace avec d'autres agences favorise l'échange d'informations et de ressources (espaces, matériel, etc.). En l'absence de coordination, le risque de duplication des efforts augmente.

component_details.title: Civil Military Relations
component_details.description: Dialogue and interaction with military actors, essential to protect and promote humanitarian principles, avoid competition, minimize inconsistency and, when appropriate, pursue common goals.

component_responses.notes:
La SN n'a pas un cadre formel  de relations civile-militaires.
La SN accompagne parfais le CICR dans certaines activités auprès des militaires  
Implications: 
Il est important que les militaires connaissent le rôle de la SN, tant au niveau national qu’à la capitale.  
Cette sensibilisation serait bénéfique pour les interventions risquées, tout en respectant les directives du Mouvement et des organes militaires (2005).

component_details.title: Coordination with local community level responders
component_details.description: Engagement with Community Disaster Response Teams (CDRTs), through training, coordination, and the development of community disaster preparedness and response plans.

component_details.title: Cooperation with private sector
component_details.description: Mechanism that allows cooperation with private sector that often plays a strong role in response, particularly if there is impact on their staff and businesses. There is often a willingness to donate goods and services. Advance agreements help to expedite response actions.

component_responses.notes: Pas d’information

component_details.title: Safety and security management
component_details.description: Addresses policy and procedures to ensure the safety of staff and volunteers. This include awareness, effective recruitment, training and management processes in place to ensure that personnel are capable of undertaking the roles demanded of them (from NS operational, management and leaders) according to the Stay Safe (IFRC) and Safer Access (ICRC). Based on safer access framework, including concepts of access, perception, identification and acceptance, and protection and violence prevention.

component_responses.notes:
Il n'y a pas de personnel de référence au siège et dans les branches pour informer régulièrement les intervenants sur les risques et les procédures, ni pour élaborer ou mettre à jour un plan d'atténuation pendant les épidémies.  
Les formations de base telles que « Accès plus sûr » et « Stay Safe » ne sont pas proposées.
Aucun mécanisme n'est en place pour permettre au personnel et aux volontaires de signaler les risques et problèmes liés à la sécurité et à la sûreté.
Implications: 
L'absence de protocole de sécurité et de personnel dédié expose les intervenants à des risques non gérés, en particulier lors d'épidémies.  
Le manque de formations de sécurité compromet la préparation du personnel aux risques potentiels, réduisant leur capacité à réagir de manière appropriée.  
L'absence de mécanismes pour signaler les risques empêche une gestion proactive des problèmes de sécurité, mettant en danger la sûreté des volontaires et du personnel.

component_details.title: Operations Monitoring, Evaluation, Reporting and Learning
component_details.description: The PMERL is designed to implement a results-based planning, monitoring and evaluation system that provides an evidence base of NS performance, including relevance, efficiency, effectiveness, sustainability and impact. A reliable and trusted organization is accountable, providing transparent and timely information and building systems to strengthen data collection and reporting. It is data-driven, analytical and results-based.

component_responses.notes:
Il n'existe pas de service pour assurer le suivi et le rapportage en urgence, mais le rapportage se fait quand même. 
La SN conduit des évaluations et utilise les enseignements tirés de précédentes opérations dans sa planification de l’intervention. 
Implications: 
L'absence d'un service dédié au suivi et au rapportage en urgence ralentit la formalisation des processus, bien que la SN réalise des évaluations et intègre les leçons des opérations passées dans la planification des interventions.

component_details.title: Finance and Admin policy and emergency procedures
component_details.description: Overall budgeting, accounting, treasury, assets, financial reporting and financial services operations. it also includes the efficient delivery , cost effective and timely services to the NS. Pre-approved, auditable, expedited procedures that allow for flexibility during a disaster/crisis. These must meet transparency, oversight and accountability standards. Procedures may include faster approval processes, fewer signatures, different authority levels. The Emergency Procedures are activated for a specific period of time.

component_responses.notes:
Pas de procédures financières d’urgence.
Implication 
L'absence de procédures ralentit la réponse aux situation de catastrophes .
Les équipes peinent à intervenir rapidement.

component_details.title: Information and Communication Technology (ICT)
component_details.description: Refers to technologies that provide access to information through telecommunications. This includes the Internet, wireless networks, mobile phones, radios and other communication mediums.

component_responses.notes: Implications : La SN ne peut pas compter sur les médias et les moyens de communication pour améliorer sa communication en urgence.

LOGISTICS MANAGEMENT: Exitance d’un service logisque, Manque de resources humaine, Absent de document de document.
SUPPLY CHAIN MANAGEMENT: Absence d’accord pour avec les perstataires, Stock d’urgence disponible au siège.
PROCUREMENT: "Local  avec des TVA, Magasin régional de la IFRC sans la TVA. 
FLEET AND TRANSPORTATION MANAGEMENT: Pas de Prévention & Contrôle des infections.
WAREHOUSE AND STOCK MANAGEMENT: 2 entrepôts au siege, Petit magasin au niveau des branches.

component_details.title: Staff and volunteer management
component_details.description: Well-functioning staff and volunteer management systems and practices allow for effective recruitment, supervision, support and encouragement of staff and volunteers.

component_responses.notes:
Il n’existe pas la politique des volontaires 
Il existe un manuel du personnel
Implications:
Sans une politique des volontaires, il serait difficile d'attirer et de retenir des volontaires pour les activités et opérations, compromettant ainsi l'efficacité des interventions.

component_details.title: Communication in emergencies
component_details.description: Incorporates a system of public messaging to enable the NS to share timely, accurate information before, during, and after a disaster or crisis.

component_responses.notes:
Des personnes
Il faut la documentation de la ligne de communication

component_details.title: Resource Mobilisation
component_details.description: A documented strategy for raising domestic funds from the government, private sector, general public and other in-country actors to support the national society’s response. This would include allocation of responsibilities, practical mechanisms for accepting funds and for being accountable on funds.

component_responses.epi_considerations: non
component_responses.notes:
Il existe une politique de mobilisation de ressources globales pour la SN jusqu’en 2025 
Lors de la revue a mi parcoure il faudra ajouter le volet

component_details.title: RC auxiliary role, Mandate and Law
component_details.description: A constitutional reference to the role of the NS in responding to disasters and crises, which may be legislated or included/ recognized in the National Response System.

component_responses.notes: DRCS establishes an auxiliary role to the public authorities through a clear mandate which is aligned with RCRC Fundamental Principles. The NS mandate is reflected in its Strategic Plan as well as Disaster Response & Contingency Plan. The mandate is understood by most staff but only some volunteers so further dissemination is needed. DRCS is putting a lot of effort into promoting IHL, through the recent desk review of humanitarian law and case study on IDRL in Dominica.

component_details.title: DRM Strategy
component_details.description: An outline of the overall goal that the NS seeks to achieve in its disaster and crisis response operations. The goal considers: context analysis, ongoing/regular all-hazards risk assessments: it may define the target proportion of affected population that will be reached, and a definition of the areas/sectors where a NS will usually respond during an emergency.

component_responses.notes: The NS’s Strategic Plan has incorporated elements of the DRM Strategy including clear engagement with technical sectors and support services for a comprehensive response, but no separate DRM Strategy exists. Strategic plan has been reviewed in 2019 however, dissemination among staff and key volunteers needs to be done yet.

component_details.title: DRM Policy
component_details.description: Reflects the NS mission, RCRC principles and mandate. It acknowledges other relevant NS policies, and aligns with the government policy (where applicable), incorporating the general rules that the NS will obey in order to achieve something (i.e mandate, strategy, etc.)

component_responses.notes: The NS has a draft DRM Policy adapted from the IFRC DRM Policy but this has to be further adapted by the NS. For the NS, the Disaster Response & Contingency Plan guides the decision making, and includes other relevant sectors and services. The Plan and the finalized DRM Policy needs to be disseminated among staff and key volunteers for the adherence of the document.

component_details.title: DRM Laws, Advocacy and Dissemination
component_details.description: Designed to support the NS in improving legal preparedness for disasters and crisis and to promote the use of the IDRL Guidelines in order to reduce human vulnerability.

component_details.title: Quality and accountability
component_details.description: Describes the essential elements of principled, accountable, and high-quality humanitarian action. The RCRC Movement provides support to the most vulnerable people in line with the Sphere and CHS standards, Code of Conduct for the RCRC Movement and NGOS in Disaster Relief and the Code for Good Partnership of the RCRC Movement, Gender & Diversity, inclusion and protection, BPI/ Do no harm, context-sensitive analysis, violence prevention, accountability to affected population and disability considerations, Community engagement and accountability (CEA).

component_responses.notes: The NS has mechanisms in place to ensure the affected populations are involved in all stages of the response. However, it does not have a CEA plan and safe and accessible feedback and complaints mechanisms in place. There is one CEA focal point at Headquarters (HQ) who has not been trained but such presence needs to be extended to the branches. The NS does not have Protection, Gender and Inclusion (PGI) policies in place, and Minimum Standards for PGI in Emergencies are not followed. Sphere standards are considered for WASH trainings and the persons with disabilities are generally integrated in sectoral activities. The NS conducts PSS and RFL activities.

component_details.title: Business continuity
component_details.description: A strategy to counter any potential or anticipated obstacles to effective functioning of the NS, with an eye to ensuring that personnel and assets are protected and able to function in the event of a disaster/crisis.

component_responses.notes: The NS identifies this is a weak component. A business continuity plan does not exist, and the NS needs to work on SOPs to direct the interaction with donors to repurpose available funds or arrange additional funds in case of anticipated/eminent disaster. However, the NS identifies that this is important and is willing to work toward improving this component.

component_details.title: Emergency Response Procedures (SOPs)
component_details.description: Written guidelines that describe duties and rights of personnel, command structures, coordination with other organizations, and reporting requirements, etc. Includes detailed organogram, decision-making flow chart, and defined roles and responsibilities.

component_details.title: Response and recovery planning
component_details.description: A documented set of procedures for the disaster/crisis response and recovery process. Including use of local capacities, transition to recovery, type of activities and serivices provided during response and recovery activities and exit strategies, procedures for DREF & EA, and templates for planning, budgeting and accessing funds.

component_responses.notes: NS has an up-to-date, approved multi-sectoral response plan for rapid deployment and efficient use of human and material resources. The plan adheres to the Principles and Rules, Fundamental principles and DRM strategy. The plan has been developed with the participation of community, staff, volunteers, management and governance. The plan aligns with IFRC standards and templates, considers reduction of secondary risks and is disseminated to relevant stakeholders. The NS has a process to adapt the plan to changing context and emergency needs.  The plan neither specifically takes into consideration gender, age, disability and diversity complexities and community capacities nor considers the self-recovery options for the affected population. Lessons learned from real time and simulated exercises have not been used to update the plan in recent past.

component_details.title: Pre-disaster meetings and agreements
component_details.description: A commitment to arrange meetings and agreements with Movement stakeholders and external actors to identify, plan for and address gaps for any upcoming disaster season (e.g. monsoon, floods or cyclones, or for any generic disaster/crisis event (e.g Epidemic, pandemic, confilict situations). Pre-disaster agreements should set out each partner's role in the event of a disaster/crisis.

component_responses.notes: At the moment, there is no Movement partner present physically in Dominica. Pre-disaster meetings with key stakeholders take place (at least once a year) and key staff are familiar with pre-disaster/crisis agreements and how to operationalize them in a response. The NS does not have formalized coordination and management arrangements with relevant local and national key actors.  All pre-disaster agreements (mostly undocumented) are in line with NS and RCRC Movement policies and procedures. There is no agreement in place with public authorities to facilitate expedited import of humanitarian aid and visas for incoming personnel; in case of emergencies, authorities provide generic support to all actors. In the same, there is no pre-agreement with key suppliers of goods and services with an agreed mechanism for activation. There is not agreement in place with Social Protection systems to facilitate access to pre-existing databases of vulnerable populations. Agreements with money transfer providers are formalised with an agreed mechanism for activation e.g. was done for CTP during Hurricane Maria emergency operation.  Contractors signed the Code of Conduct only for IFRC supported activities during Hurricane Maria emergency operation.

component_details.title: Hazard, Context and Risk Analysis, Monitoring and Early Warning
component_details.description: Describes how the NS monitors and maps past, present and potential hazards, disasters and crises (e.g. hazard, vulnerability assessments, gathering information from communities and government authorities) and systematically evaluates the damage that could be caused by a potential disaster/crisis, the frequency, severity of the impact, and the alert the relevant areas to scale the preparedness actions to reduce population vulnerability.

component_responses.notes: The NS continues to build its capacity to collect and record risk information, but they lack the expertise of analysis and trending to inform their delivery of services to vulnerable communities. However, the SWOT analysis conducted in their Strategic Plan has allowed them to evaluate their weakness and challenges in this area. Communities and local volunteers contribute to the regular update of risk mapping and VCAs. Risk assessments at community level include the analysis of the potential connectors and dividers within a community. For areas at risk, the collected/available primary and secondary data is mostly disaggregated by age, gender, disability, income etc.

component_details.title: Scenario planning
component_details.description: A set of practical operation plans that closely mirror the generic disaster or crisis response plan but are tailored to a specific hazard type (e.g. earthquake, dengue epidemic, floods, cyclone) and a specific scenario (i.e. number of people affected, their locations and other important factors).

component_responses.notes: The NS Disaster Response & Contingency Plan include scenarios and the analysis/response options include multi-sectors for the identified hazards, and identification of drivers and the potential impact. However, this does not have scenarios for each high-risk area in the country and the NS contingency plans are aligned with those of the public authorities. The NS Disaster Response & Contingency Plan includes procedures for activation of EOC and contingency/response plan. The NS has updated their Response and Contingency plans in 2019 but has not conducted testing based on scenarios. In their draft contingency plan, there are relevant triggers for hazards and scenarios. The NS never had the need to develop a regional contingency strategy within their context.

component_details.title: Risk management
component_details.description: A mapping of the potential risks in every area, along with its related mitigation measures. Including financial, reputational, organizational risks etc.

component_details.title: Preparedness plans and budgets
component_details.description: Plans identifying organisational resources, determining roles and responsibilities, and developing policies, procedures and activities in order to reach a level of preparedness to be able to respond effectively to a disaster or crisis. Budgets ensure that the necessary financial support is secured to allow capacities to be built and readiness maintained.

component_responses.notes: NS has a designated person for disaster preparedness and due to past disaster impacts. Further, staff and volunteers have a strong understanding of their roles and responsibilities, policies, procedures and activities to improve their capacity to response effectively. Though the NS has been identifying remedial actions for preparedness gaps, due to financial constraints not all actions have taken place.

The NS ensures participation of community representatives to reflect the needs and strengths of local population in the assessment, design, and planning of community-based preparedness activities. Awareness raising is limited to some public education activities. Community based early warning and early action is in place and is linked to the local early warning systems. Community based early warning and early action is in place and is linked to the local early warning systems. Community Disaster Response Team (CDRTs) are trained and equipped to handle local response in partnership with relevant local actors and have contingency plans. NS ensures community assessment, planning and response are inclusive conflict sensitive.

component_details.title: Mapping of NS capacities
component_details.description: A list of the NS capacities including HR (staff, response teams and volunteers) and equipment that are available for disaster/crisis response. Teams could include branch and national response teams. This should be defined by technical speciality where relevant.

component_responses.notes: The NS has a focal point identified and available for each specific area of intervention and services to provide technical guidance and support. The staff and volunteers are trained and kept up to date, even though NS does not follow a structured approach. Response materials and equipment database is up to date and gaps are noted and being addressed however material is not enough due to capacity gaps. The NS has a mechanism to share resources amongst branches. However, it has not mapped capacities in line with different levels of response.

The NS identifies multi-sectoral response needs for different epidemics. It has procedures, data collection and feedback mechanisms in place (limited to project areas) to ensure community engagement in prevention and response interventions. It has a procedure in place to manage and respond to rumours however its effectiveness needs to be tested. The NS does not have safety protocols in place for staff and volunteers for infection prevention and control within epidemics; some equipment is available, and staff is sensitised to risks but no formal training has been provided.  The NS is not engaged in the management of dead bodies and has not identified its role in case of isolation and declared quarantine. It has identified its role within epidemics and have established relevant technical support to ensure best practice (we may need some evidences here).

component_details.title: Early Action Mechanisms
component_details.description: Designed to translate warnings into anticipatory actions to help reduce the impact of specific disaster or crisis events. They focus on consolidating available forecasting information and putting procedures in place to ensure that a NS can act ahead of any disaster/crisis. Forecast-based financing is included within the scope of this area.

component_responses.notes: The NS has a clear methodology to take early actions (when, where) based on vulnerability, exposure and triggers, and there is a mechanism to anticipate and respond to major hazards in coordination with the national system. However, the NS's early warning early action system is not part of the national strategies and preparedness system. The NS is making use of new technologies (e.g. WhatsApp) for sending alerts to volunteers/responders who further disseminate the information using local networks and initiate early action.

component_details.title: Cash Based Intervention (CBI)
component_details.description: An effective and flexible way, including all forms of cash and voucher-based assistance, to support people affected by emergencies, maintaining their dignity and choice, while fostering local economies. Cash should also be mainstreamed into other sectors (including Relief, shelter, livelihoods) and services (Logistics, Finance, etc.)

component_responses.notes: This is another weak component of the DRCS. The NS neither has a CBI plan with accompanying SOPs nor pre-disaster feasibility cash analysis, baseline information and mapping of other actors and coordination structures in place. NS has a list of staff and volunteers trained and experienced in CBI at HQ and branch levels, across sectors and support services, to implement CBI within the response cycle. It has also mapped CBI delivery mechanisms and service providers. The NS does not have an up-to-date, approved CBI toolkit and is not active around CBI coordination, even though engaged in CBI with support IFRC after the Hurricane Maria.

component_details.title: Emergency Needs Assessment
component_details.description: Assess the extent and impact of the damage caused by the disaster/crisis and the degree of vulnerability of the affected population. The first step in any emergency response, such an assessment will identify the needs that require external intervention and the gaps to be filled. It is a vital component of the programme-planning process.

component_responses.notes: The NS has standardised templates and trained multi-sectorial emergency assessment team available to deploy in a timely manner to collect and report on primary and secondary disaggregated data. It builds emergency plans on the needs assessment results. The needs assessment analyses secondary risk and specific needs of vulnerable people.

component_details.title: Affected population selection
component_details.description: Identification and selection of target Affected population for interventions, using a pre-defined set of criteria based on need and vulnerability. This includes consideration of specific vulnerabilities such as disability, age and gender.

component_responses.notes: The NS communicates selection criteria to the affected population using feasible channels and involves community representatives. It identifies appropriate selection criteria based on existing vulnerability and taking into consideration gender, diversity, age and disabilities. Responders have been trained in data collection by using standardised templates, there is a mechanism to cross-check that data, and the NS protects data collected from affected population.

component_details.title: Emergency Operations Centre (EOC)
component_details.description: A central command and control facility responsible for carrying out disaster/crisis management functions at a strategic level in an emergency situation. The common functions are to collect and analyze data; facilitate decision making that protects life and livelihoods; and disseminate those decisions to all concerned agencies and individuals. Generally located at the headquarter level of an organization.

component_responses.notes: The NS has a formally appointed focal point for EOC however, EOC SOPs do not exit. EOC is activated as per the situation and activation is communicated. The relevant staff and volunteers know their roles and responsibilities in connection with the EOC. As there are no SOPs, technical sectors and support services are not systematically integrated with the EOC. The NS makes decisions based on situational analysis and there is clarity on authority at all levels.  EOC has intended space with enough equipment (including legal access to radio frequencies) and facilities to manage information and coordination that does not affect other NS activities. There is no equipped alternative space for the EOC. The NS has full and updated contact details for relevant personnel. EOC staff manages and displays regular updated information however no maps are readily available/displayed in the EOC room

component_details.title: Information Management (IM)
component_details.description: Ability to manage information including requesting, receiving, analyzing and disseminating as per its procedures and partner requirements (IFRC and public authorities in particular). There should be a clear digital/paper trail that documents what, when and how the NS has acted and provides key information for the development of Emergency Plan of Actions. Includes IM between levels, between departments and Situational Reports, mapping, visualisation of data, GO platform (IFRC).

component_responses.notes: The NS key staff at HQ and branch level are familiar with IM templates, methodology and procedures, and have access to equipment to compile, visualise and share information. It has a system at HQ to store and share files with emergency personnel; branches will be given access once they have power system installed. The NS has access to updated data on high-risk areas (demographic, socio-economic) disaggregated by age, gender and disability especially from authorities.  The NS documents key information and decisions in the form of minutes which are used for information sharing across levels and sectors. It has a standardised Situation Report format and these reports are analysed to adapt response plans.

component_details.title: Testing and Learning
component_details.description: Drills and Simulations allow the organization to test, identify and learn from the results of these type of exercises and incorporate learning into future preparedness and response planning.

component_responses.notes: This is a weak component of the DRCS. The NS HQ does not regularly test its early action and response system through simulation and drills in order to drawn lessons informing revisions of emergency procedures. Branches in high-risk areas test their response system through drills and simulations which are conducted with local authorities and other organisations.

component_details.title: Activation of regional and international support
component_details.description: Procedures for requesting and accepting regional and international support in operations, including triggering coordination mechanisms for funding, materials and human resources deployments.

component_responses.notes: The NS key staff are familiar with the available IFRC support (technical, financial, material and HR). The mechanism to coordinate response with respective IFRC offices is widely understood (with a familiarity with IFRC emergency funding mechanisms) but is not available in the form of formal documented SOPs. NS procedures (not documented SOPs) include procedures to request and incorporate regional and global support/teams into their response system, including prior to imminent crisis/disaster, and assigns a focal point to act as counterpart to regional/international responders. NS informs IFRC within 24 hours for which assistance may be required. In this regard, a focal person is identified but she has not been trained.

component_details.title: CHEMICAL, BIOLOGICAL, RADIOLOGICAL AND NUCLEAR (CBRN) EMERGENCY PREPAREDNESS
MANAGEMENT OF DEAD BODIES TO FACILITATE THEIR IDENTIFICATION

component_responses.notes: The NS staff and volunteers are capable of provide quality RFL services and procedures and agreements with ICRC on RFL are in place.

component_details.title: NS-specific areas of intervention
component_details.description: Sector-specific or services provided by the NS in case of emergencies, it is in line with the NS mandate and legislation in country. It includes Community Based DP/DRR, Evacuation, Health in Emergencies, Epidemic and Pandemic, First aid, WASH, Food security and Livelihoods, Search and rRescue, Shelter, Management of dead bodies, RFL, Transition to recovery, and CBRN preparedness.

component_responses.notes: Evacuation is part of NS's response strategy but is not identified in different scenarios. The NS is part of government led mechanism for evacuation of communities in high-risk areas. This is a low priority area of intervention by the NS.

First Aid is part of NS's response strategy and is identified in different scenarios. It is part of NS DRM/CBDRR strategy. The NS has trained and equipped teams of First Aid volunteers for quick and effective response.

Water and sanitation is part of the NS's response strategy and is identified in different scenarios. WASH technical support in emergencies is available in the NS. The NS response teams (national and branch) have the appropriate WASH training, skills and equipment with a mechanism to obtain surge services/equipment. The NS engages and coordinates with other organizations and networks active in WASH in the country.

NS is not supporting communities to develop health contingency plans and does not conduct relevant periodic assessments. CBHFA volunteer training includes all the standard sessions but volunteers are not engaged in simulation planning, implementation, evaluation and referrals. Active volunteers from different sectors are trained in basic First Aid.

component_details.title: Coordination with local community level responders
component_details.description: Engagement with Community Disaster Response Teams (CDRTs), through training, coordination, and the development of community disaster preparedness and response plans.

component_responses.notes: The NS has strong links with the communities in which they communicate and work from HQ to branch level and then onward to communities and vice versa. They have set up liaisons with CDRTs, so that information especially risk information can ready be shared and branches and the HQ, and advise the decision-making. The HQ and branch liaison focal points use mobile phones and WhatsApp channels to stay connected. The DRCS supports the community level by liaising with CDRTs and maintaining communication to support local response actions.

component_details.title: Cooperation with private sector
component_details.description: Mechanism that allows cooperation with private sector that often plays a strong role in response, particularly if there is impact on their staff and businesses. There is often a willingness to donate goods and services. Advance agreements help to expedite response actions.

component_responses.notes: The DRCS does not do due diligence in selecting donors and their background check because it is a small island context and businesses are known. While the NS upholds the visibility and protection of the organisation’s reputational risk, they do interact with cooperate sector by providing trainings and building corporate sector capacity. They also advertise the opportunity for cooperate personnel to become the NS volunteers.

component_details.title: Coordination with External Agencies and NGOs
component_details.description: Mechanism that facilitates coordination and collaboration with Non-Governmental Organization (NGO), both local and international NGOs, civil society organizations (CSOs) and United Nations agencies in country.

component_responses.notes: This component is not as strong within the area of coordination. The NS is not an active member of the humanitarian community (UN, NGO) for coordination and efficiency of response and thus not aware of UN-led appeal and strategic processes. It does not have any Partnership agreements in place with the key humanitarian actors (UN/NGO) and is not aware of IFRC's role in the shelter cluster coordination.

component_details.title: Civil Military Relations
component_details.description: Dialogue and interaction with military actors, essential to protect and promote humanitarian principles, avoid competition, minimize inconsistency and, when appropriate, pursue common goals.

component_details.title: Coordination with Movement
component_details.description: Mechanisms that facilitate the coordination with ICRC, IFRC, and PNS in-country.

component_responses.notes: IFRC, ICRC and any PNS are not physically present in Dominica. However, there is strong coordination with movement partners to share information on needs assessment, plan of actions, progress against operations and operational capacities and emerging gaps in resources. DRCS utilises different communication channels to share information with neighbouring NSs to coordinate response actions. The NS also ensures that there are systems in place to liaise with the IFRC to accept international assistance. They did identify these procedures are not documented in SOPs and have happened only in times of emergency, thus far.

component_details.title: Coordination with authorities
component_details.description: Mechanism that facilitates coordination and cooperation with local and national authorities. It is connected to the NS auxiliary role for humanitarian assistance.

component_responses.notes: The NS knows their role in the national response framework and keeps regular communication with the RCRC and other national agencies to ensure assistance can be effectively given in times of emergency. The NS knows the capacities of national authorities and identifies areas within a response to fulfil their auxiliary role. It has control over its resources, assets and emblem when responding. The DRCS has even been able to structure agreements with local authorities to provide critical services such as water with government sectoral agencies.

component_details.title: Staff and volunteer management
component_details.description: Well-functioning staff and volunteer management systems and practices allow for effective recruitment, supervision, support and encouragement of staff and volunteers.

component_responses.notes: The DRCS deploys and equips responders according to assigned tasks; documented ToRs do not exit. Responders have official IDs and vests and are acknowledged by the authorities. Procedures, as part of Disaster Response & Contingency Plan, exist to activate, deploy and manage branch and national response teams. NS has an accessible, up-to-date database of responders’ contacts and capacities at branch and HQ level.   Response volunteers are inducted randomly but they are then trained as per their profiles. NS does not have expedited procedures (including screening) to incorporate spontaneous volunteers and manage the scale during emergencies. It had a perception that in a small island context, staff/volunteers know the persons being inducted as new volunteers. However, from Hurricane Maria experience, a lesson learnt is to conduct the screening. NS also does not have set procedures for appreciation of volunteers during emergencies. Most of staff at HQ and branches sign the Code of Conduct (CoC) but as a one-time occurrence. Almost all response team members sign the CoC. Only few volunteers who were involved in Hurricane Maria response signed the CoC.   Learning paths for responders are not in place and various trainings (e.g. NIT, First Aid, WASH, Warehouse and Logistics) are conducted based on funding and are not very structured. Training of responders in quality and accountability standards is almost non-existent (limited to PS); they only signed Code of Conduct during Hurricane Maria response and Sphere elements were promoted during the WASH training. They are briefed on safety before any deployment however, no specific Safer Access analysis is conducted by the NS. Volunteers were insured after Hurricane Maria but not insured at the moment.

component_details.title: Safety and security management
component_details.description: Addresses policy and procedures to ensure the safety of staff and volunteers. This include awareness, effective recruitment, training and management processes in place to ensure that personnel are capable of undertaking the roles demanded of them (from NS operational, management and leaders) according to the Stay Safe (IFRC) and Safer Access (ICRC). Based on safer access framework, including concepts of access, perception, identification and acceptance, and protection and violence prevention.

component_responses.notes: The NS does not implement Safer Access and have no safety and security policy and compliance system. However, information on context and risk analysis is provided to responders on an ongoing basis. Staff uses informal briefings and reminders informally and information/advisories are not documented/structured. Some staff members have completed Stay Safe training  After Hurricane Maria, there was a safety arrangement for the premises but no longer exists. The NS does not have dedicated trained security focal points at HQ and branches however, some mechanisms are in place e.g. padlocks, security system. NS has communication mechanisms for staff and volunteers to report safety and security risks and incidents.

component_details.title: Communication in emergencies
component_details.description: Incorporates a system of public messaging to enable the NS to share timely, accurate information before, during, and after a disaster or crisis.

component_responses.notes: The NS has identified a focal point for communications only at HQ, but the person is not trained. It designates an official spokesperson in an emergency. The NS uses public and social media to draw attention to the unmet needs of affected people, and key public awareness messages are developed and shared with staff regularly. It has capacity to track negative media and social media and react accordingly. However, NS neither has standard templates for communication and any plan for external communication during an emergency, nor it has a social networking policy or guidelines to ensure appropriate conduct of staff and volunteers. NS is not always able to provide information to public on an emergency within 24 hours.  The NS coordinates with IFRC (no ICRC presence) on joint communication and has capacity to generate evidence-based results/messages (in the form of assessment reports and photos) to advocate to targeted audiences i.e. decision makers and communities.

component_details.title: Operations Monitoring, Evaluation, Reporting and Learning
component_details.description: The PMERL is designed to implement a results-based planning, monitoring and evaluation system that provides an evidence base of NS performance, including relevance, efficiency, effectiveness, sustainability and impact. A reliable and trusted organization is accountable, providing transparent and timely information and building systems to strengthen data collection and reporting. It is data-driven, analytical and results-based.

component_responses.notes: The NS does not have a dedicated PMER function in general as well as for emergency operations. It refers to and uses lessons from previous operations in response planning. It has a plan in the form of Disaster Response & Contingency Plan however that does not include specific results and indicators to measure them. The NS has a mechanism at field level to collect, manage and report on data to all levels against the set objectives of the operation.  The NS revises operational plans based on intended and unintended outcomes of operations e.g. Hurricane Maria operation, together with IFRC. It allocates resources to conducts reviews of the operations for course correction and future learnings. It also reports to partners in line with agreement, using appropriate templates. For Movement-wide contributions, NS cooperates with IFRC on PMER activities but does not lead.

component_details.title: Finance and Admin policy and emergency procedures
component_details.description: Overall budgeting, accounting, treasury, assets, financial reporting and financial services operations. it also includes the efficient delivery , cost effective and timely services to the NS. Pre-approved, auditable, expedited procedures that allow for flexibility during a disaster/crisis. These must meet transparency, oversight and accountability standards. Procedures may include faster approval processes, fewer signatures, different authority levels. The Emergency Procedures are activated for a specific period of time.

component_responses.notes: The NS has an automated accounting and financial system and procedures to account for and report regularly on funds and expenditures. NS has a couple of personnel trained in Finance and Admin emergency support procedures (IFRC); for branches, few volunteers were trained who are inactive now. The activation of procedures is not linked to the EOC SOPs as SOPs are non-existent.  For transparency, financial reporting mechanism is in place, but the mechanism needs to be further strengthened. In order to prevent acts of fraud and/or corruption during an emergency, NS is improving processes post Hurricane Maria and Tropical Storm Erika. All MoUs or agreements for compliance are not documented, and staff and/or relevant volunteers need to be sensitized on existing MoUs.

component_details.title: Information and Communication Technology (ICT)
component_details.description: Refers to technologies that provide access to information through telecommunications. This includes the Internet, wireless networks, mobile phones, radios and other communication mediums.

component_responses.notes: Staff has office issued phones but those are not paid by the NS. Phones are available but phone cards are not given to volunteers, so they use radios. The NS key personnel always carry contact lists with critical numbers saved on their mobile phones. NS has approved Emergency Notification SOPs followed by all staff and volunteers. It has an agreed social media platform (esp. WhatsApp) for emergency communications and messaging.  Australian High Commission has donated equipment (e.g. radio system), it is placed at HQ right now, and will be setup at all branches. Handheld radios are assigned to key trained staff and NS vehicles are equipped with radios, with approved frequencies. The NS agreed mobile and radio communication procedures however these are not documented. It has only one satellite phone which is placed at HQ. There are enough generators at HQ and attempts are being made to shift to/setup at branches, but these are not ready yet. Two branches have been constructed but power system has not been installed yet. The NS has an internet capable router to provide data connectivity for operational staff, staff does not have portable WiFi devices; they used their mobile devices. In addition, the NS has a trained IT support focal point able to support technical issues and equipment.

component_details.title: Resource Mobilisation
component_details.description: A documented strategy for raising domestic funds from the government, private sector, general public and other in-country actors to support the national society’s response. This would include allocation of responsibilities, practical mechanisms for accepting funds and for being accountable on funds.

component_responses.notes: This is another weak component of the DRCS. The NS key staff are neither familiar with the resource mobilisation options for humanitarian operations nor NS has any strategy, SOPs or resource mobilisation focal point in place at HQ as well as branches level. Similarly, pre-disaster agreements with partners and donors are not established. It has only limited funds available for preparedness activities, through projects and other resources. NS reaches out to private sector through written letters to explore funding/donations as no formal mechanism (e.g. pre-agreements) is in place. The NS has not established a national emergency fund with criteria for proper use.  The NS relies on verbal updates to communicate changes across departments (technical teams and support services) and report on outcomes of resources provided. It has a platform (phone number, bank account, online, etc.) able to accept national and/or international donations within 48 hours of an emergency, with a donation tracking system. However, NS does not have a pre-defined list of acceptable in-kind donations and makes decision on an ad hoc basis to mitigate image or reputational risks.

Logistics management: The NS has 2 persons dedicated to logistics including warehousing functions who have clearly defined roles and have received training to carry out their tasks. They together with the management of NS are familiar with IFRC logistics services to support NS emergency operations. The NS has prepositioned stock at 2 locations in addition to HQ and does not have pre-existing agreements with the suppliers. The NFIs meet standards and reflect the needs of populations at risk. The NS has volunteers trained in logistics who can act as surge capacity during an emergency response.//Supply chain management: The NS does not have an agreement with the government, however in times of emergency it can get taxes waved on relief items. It coordinates its stock and equipment with local authorities for the sake of response planning and coordination. As most of branches are under construction, no documented procedures exist, and the logistic support have planned to be provided from 3 strategic locations. The NS does not have SOPs in place for accepting (or rejecting), storing, disposing and reporting on in-kind donations. For import of good, it relies on the government policy/procedures.//Procurement: The NS has trained personnel for procurement. It does not have documented and approved emergency procurement procedures, database of suppliers and pre-agreements with suppliers to immediately access supplies and/or services necessary for humanitarian response.//Fleet and transportation management: The NS does not have a fleet manual. It does not have enough vehicles for disaster response. The existing vehicles are insured, and their use is fully documented using logbooks, maintenance records, fuel checks etc. There are working seatbelts in all vehicles, first aid kits in some vehicles, and fire extinguishers only in ambulance and bus. The NS uses licensed mechanics/workshops for the maintenance of its vehicle. There are documented procedures for reporting of accidents and insurance claims. The NS has mapped in-country resources to rent vehicles during a response. The NS has informal procedures to induct and test new drivers. The drivers are regularly tested and have valid licenses for the types of vehicles they are driving. Almost all drivers are trained in First Aid but need refresher training; they have not been given any other training. The NS does not have emergency procedures to guide the hours for drivers including non-standard hours and compensation.//Warehouse and stock management: The NS has an approved warehouse and stock management manual with standard forms and templates and the 2 relevant staff are trained in that. It has a secure, dedicated and appropriate space with 24/7 access to receive, store and dispatch relief supplies and response equipment, enough to cover target number of households as per its response plan. In addition, the NS has 2 storage places at strategic locations owned by the NS.

component_details.title: Quality and accountability
component_details.description: Describes the essential elements of principled, accountable, and high-quality humanitarian action. The RCRC Movement provides support to the most vulnerable people in line with the Sphere and CHS standards, Code of Conduct for the RCRC Movement and NGOS in Disaster Relief and the Code for Good Partnership of the RCRC Movement, Gender & Diversity, inclusion and protection, BPI/ Do no harm, context-sensitive analysis, violence prevention, accountability to affected population and disability considerations, Community engagement and accountability (CEA).

component_responses.notes:
La Sociedad Nacional (SN) cuenta con una estrategia, políticas y procedimientos para la implementación del enfoque de Participación Comunitaria y Rendición de Cuentas (CEA) en emergencias. Dispone de 24 puntos focales distribuidos en las juntas provinciales, de los cuales 7 son personal remunerado y el resto voluntarios.

La CRE ha desarrollado un plan de CEA con procedimientos y plantillas estándar que incluyen encuestas de satisfacción, mecanismos de retroalimentación y reclamo mediante buzones físicos, formularios digitales, correo electrónico, código QR, la herramienta Cruz Roja Escúchame y un chatbot. Estas herramientas permiten registrar, remitir, responder y monitorear inquietudes y solicitudes de las comunidades, garantizando respuestas adecuadas y oportunas.

La organización ha capacitado a los puntos focales de CEA en la sede central y en las juntas provinciales, fortaleciendo sus habilidades para asegurar una respuesta humanitaria efectiva, centrada en las personas y construida junto con la comunidad. Este proceso incluye evaluaciones de necesidades (EVIN), planificación conjunta, implementación colaborativa y monitoreo participativo, utilizando espacios de diálogo, grupos focales y encuestas.

En materia de protección, la CRE cuenta con una Política de Integridad, Género y Protección (IGP), aprobada en mayo de 2024, basada en el modelo de la IFRC e incluyendo un apartado de protección infantil. Asimismo, aplica el Plan Nacional de Preparación y Respuesta (PNPR), que integra el enfoque de Protección, Género e Inclusión (PGI) y asegura la protección de grupos vulnerables conforme a las Normas Esfera, la Norma Humanitaria Esencial y las Directrices del IASC.

Actualmente, la CRE trabaja con la Política de Protección contra la Explotación y el Abuso Sexual de la IFRC, mientras avanza en la aprobación de su propia política nacional. Estas normas y políticas fortalecen los servicios especializados, como espacios seguros para la niñez, apoyo a menores no acompañados y separados, prevención de violencia sexual y de género, apoyo psicosocial, restablecimiento del contacto entre familiares y accesibilidad de instalaciones e información.

Además, la CRE promueve las normas mínimas de Dignidad, Acceso y Seguridad (DAF), con cursos e-learning para voluntarios, y aplica las Normas Mínimas de Género y Diversidad en programas motivados por emergencias, garantizando equidad e inclusión. Todos los planes y procedimientos están diseñados bajo el principio de "no hacer daño", mediante evaluaciones de riesgos y medidas preventivas que eviten impactos sociales, económicos y ambientales adversos.

Finalmente, la SN cuenta con herramientas complementarias en proceso de aprobación y un checklist verificable 2025 que respalda la aplicación práctica del enfoque CEA en todas sus actividades y programas.

Recomendación: Desarrollar una caja de herramientas adaptada al contexto nacional para fortalecer la participación comunitaria y la rendición de cuentas. Esta incluirá herramientas estandarizadas que faciliten su implementación en distintos escenarios, garantizando enfoques alineados con las necesidades y realidades locales.

component_details.title: DRM Policy
component_details.description: Reflects the NS mission, RCRC principles and mandate. It acknowledges other relevant NS policies, and aligns with the government policy (where applicable), incorporating the general rules that the NS will obey in order to achieve something (i.e mandate, strategy, etc.)

component_responses.notes:
El borrador de la política de Gestión del Riesgo de Desastres (GRD) se encuentra en proceso de revisión por parte de las autoridades. Sin embargo, este hallazgo ya se había identificado en el simulacro anterior, lo que indica una demora en su aprobación. Aunque el contenido incluye principios y valores fundamentales, así como aportes de diversas áreas sobre temas clave como la protección del emblema, Protección, Género e Inclusión, el proceso de revisión por parte de las áreas técnicas ha prolongado su validación. Como consecuencia, al no estar aprobada, la política aún no se integra dentro de los planes y estrategias existentes de la Sociedad Nacional.

Recomendación: Agilizar el proceso de revisión mediante una hoja de ruta clara con plazos específicos y responsables designados para cada etapa. Asimismo, considerar la posibilidad de validar los temas esenciales y nuevas tendencias (Clima y Ambiente, Crisis prolongadas y complejas, otros) con un grupo representativo de áreas técnicas para facilitar el consenso y avanzar hacia su aprobación socializacióne implementación a nivel Nacional así como su integración a los documentos existentes para el manejo de emergencias como por ejemplo,  Plan de Respuesta, Estrategia de GRD entre otros.

component_details.title: DRM Laws, Advocacy and Dissemination
component_details.description: Designed to support the NS in improving legal preparedness for disasters and crisis and to promote the use of the IDRL Guidelines in order to reduce human vulnerability.

component_responses.notes:
No se identificó un plan o estrategia específica para la implementación del IDRL; sin embargo, la diplomacia humanitaria ha sido promovida a través de la ley orgánica de GRD. El marco legal ecuatoriano facilita la respuesta humanitaria mediante exoneraciones tributarias y decretos especiales en emergencias, permitiendo el ingreso ágil de ayuda. La Cruz Roja Ecuatoriana (CRE) fortalece la difusión del Derecho Internacional Humanitario (DIH) con 10 puntos focales y una malla formativa especializada. 

Recomendación: 
Se recomienda desarrollar un Plan de Diplomacia Humanitaria en IDRL, basado en la lista de verificación de la IFRC, que permita estructurar acciones de incidencia y mejorar el reconocimiento del rol de la CRE en la legislación nacional. Es fundamental ampliar la malla formativa para incluir específicamente el Derecho Internacional para la Respuesta a Desastres (IDRL). Además, se recomienda documentar y evidenciar de manera más estructurada los procedimientos legales que permiten la exoneración de impuestos y el ingreso expedito de ayuda humanitaria en emergencias, asegurando que esta información sea accesible para el personal clave. 

Asimismo, se sugiere reforzar la incidencia con el Estado y actores humanitarios, participando en mesas de trabajo interinstitucionales y publicando informes anuales sobre la aplicación del IDRL y el DIH. Estas acciones permitirán consolidar la estrategia legal y de difusión de la CRE, fortaleciendo su capacidad de respuesta y su papel en la diplomacia humanitaria. El poder contar con un punto focal de IDRL en la SN y que coordine las acciones de la mano de IFRC y CICR para mejorar la calidad de la asistencia en emergencias y desastres llevada a cabo por la SN.

Llevar a cabo un trabajo de diplomacia humanitaria para garantizar el uso adecuado y la protección del emblema, tanto a nivel interno como externo. Esto incluirá un monitoreo continuo a nivel local para identificar situaciones en las que el emblema pueda estar siendo utilizado de manera incorrecta. En los casos en los que se detecten usos indebidos que infrinjan la normativa vigente, se realizará el seguimiento correspondiente para tomar las medidas necesarias.

Asimismo, se recomienda que en el próximo Ejercicio Nacional de Equipos de Respuesta (ENER) o futuros simulacros, se incluyan escenarios específicos que permitan evaluar el uso adecuado del emblema en situaciones operativas, así como su aplicación en el contexto de Movilidad Humana, garantizando el cumplimiento de los principios humanitarios y el marco legal vigente.

component_details.title: RC auxiliary role, Mandate and Law
component_details.description: A constitutional reference to the role of the NS in responding to disasters and crises, which may be legislated or included/ recognized in the National Response System.

component_responses.notes:
La Sociedad Nacional emplea diversos mecanismos para difundir el concepto de rol auxiliar entre su personal, voluntarios y actores externos. Esto incluye su plataforma de formación e-learning, que ofrece módulos específicos sobre el rol auxiliar y gobernanza, así como espacios clave como asambleas de rendición de cuentas y encuentros interinstitucionales e interagenciales para acciones de abogacía y divulgación. Además, se elaboran mensajes estratégicos dirigidos a organizaciones y medios de comunicación para fortalecer el conocimiento sobre el rol auxiliar de la Cruz Roja Ecuatoriana.
El mandato de la Sociedad Nacional está alineado con las políticas y estrategias globales del Movimiento, integrando marcos clave como el Código de Conducta, el Derecho Relativo al Desastre y la Estrategia 2030. Se refleja en documentos fundamentales como el Estatuto de la Sociedad Nacional, su Plan Estratégico, el Plan Nacional de Preparación y Respuesta a Desastres, y sus políticas operativas. Su difusión se refuerza mediante plataformas digitales, aplicaciones móviles y espacios de interacción con la membresía, donde los órganos de gobierno tienen la responsabilidad de socializarlo.
Asimismo, se promueve el Derecho Internacional Humanitario (DIH) entre autoridades, agencias humanitarias y actores cívico-militares, aprovechando espacios de coordinación preexistentes, como mesas técnicas, para su difusión y aplicación.

Recomendación: Continuar promoviendo la formación de líderes y brindar acceso al personal de Gobierno al programa de formación existente en la escuela de voluntariado. De igual forma se podrían explorar otras modalidades para el aprendizaje como espacios de mentoría entre líderes experimentados y nuevos líderes, donde se compartan buenas prácticas y experiencias

component_details.title: DRM Strategy
component_details.description: An outline of the overall goal that the NS seeks to achieve in its disaster and crisis response operations. The goal considers: context analysis, ongoing/regular all-hazards risk assessments: it may define the target proportion of affected population that will be reached, and a definition of the areas/sectors where a NS will usually respond during an emergency.

component_responses.notes: La estrategia de Gestión del Riesgo de Desastres de la Cruz Roja Ecuatoriana está alineada con su misión humanitaria y se enfoca en la prevención, respuesta y recuperación temprana ante las crisis y desastres, fortaleciendo la coordinación interinstitucional y el apoyo comunitario. Aunque se revisa regularmente, la estrategia podría mejorar la definición de indicadores de éxito y estructurar de manera más explícita su proceso de revisión periódica. La respuesta institucional es integral, con equipos especializados y un sistema de soporte que garantiza una respuesta rápida y eficiente.

component_details.title: Scenario planning
component_details.description: A set of practical operation plans that closely mirror the generic disaster or crisis response plan but are tailored to a specific hazard type (e.g. earthquake, dengue epidemic, floods, cyclone) and a specific scenario (i.e. number of people affected, their locations and other important factors).

component_responses.notes:
Los planes de contingencia incluyen escenarios de emergencia que permiten definir las acciones de respuesta de la Sociedad Nacional en diferentes sectores. Se han establecido escenarios específicos para amenazas como el Volcán Cotopaxi y el Fenómeno de El Niño, lo que facilita la planificación operativa y la implementación de acciones de respuesta. A nivel provincial, los planes de contingencia están diseñados para adaptarse a las particularidades y riesgos de cada territorio, garantizando una preparación más efectiva y coordinada.
Estos planes, junto con los planes de respuesta, están alineados con el Sistema Nacional de Gestión del Riesgo de Desastres (GRD), incluyendo protocolos de activación de alertas y criterios establecidos a nivel nacional. Durante el Ejercicio Nacional de Equipos de Respuesta (ENER) 2025, se incorporaron escenarios de seguridad para evaluar la aplicabilidad de los procedimientos existentes en este ámbito.
Además, existen mecanismos de coordinación dentro del Convenio de Cooperación entre Colombia, Ecuador y Perú, fortaleciendo la respuesta regional ante emergencias. No obstante, se ha identificado que los planes de contingencia requieren actualización para garantizar su vigencia y efectividad.
Recomendación 
Es fundamental actualizar los planes de contingencia del Volcán Cotopaxy y planes de contigencia provinciales preexistentes para garantizar su integración con el nuevo Plan Nacional de Respuesta. Esta actualización debe incluir un análisis detallado de los riesgos emergentes y cambios en el entorno, incorporando nuevos escenarios multiamenazas potenciales que reflejen las amenazas actuales en el territorio.
El proceso de actualización debe considerar:
✔ Alineación con el Plan Nacional de Respuesta (actualizado), asegurando coherencia con los lineamientos y protocolos en proceso de validación
✔ Inclusión de escenarios actualizados, basados en estudios recientes de riesgo, cambio climático y crisis humanitarias emergentes o complejas y que utlicen proyecciones climáticas o potenciales escenarios planteadas por organizaciones técnico científicas.

component_details.title: Hazard, Context and Risk Analysis, Monitoring and Early Warning
component_details.description: Describes how the NS monitors and maps past, present and potential hazards, disasters and crises (e.g. hazard, vulnerability assessments, gathering information from communities and government authorities) and systematically evaluates the damage that could be caused by a potential disaster/crisis, the frequency, severity of the impact, and the alert the relevant areas to scale the preparedness actions to reduce population vulnerability.

component_responses.notes:
La Cruz Roja Ecuatoriana (CRE) ha establecido un sistema formal de monitoreo de riesgos, vinculado a la preparación y acción temprana, con mecanismos de coordinación a nivel nacional. Dispone de una sala de monitoreo operativa permanentemente para vigilar eventos adversos y una Sala de Crisis interna con protocolos específicos para el seguimiento de emergencias.
Para la recopilación de datos, la CRE utiliza equipos EVIN, participa en las mesas técnicas sectoriales del COE Nacional y consulta información en fuentes oficiales y redes sociales. Además, forma parte de la red de monitoreo nacional, activándose según los cinco niveles de alerta definidos por la Secretaría de Gestión de Riesgos (SNGR), asegurando una respuesta alineada con los sistemas de alerta temprana oficiales.
El Plan Nacional de Preparación y Respuesta (PNPR) integra un sistema de criterios para la activación y desactivación de alertas que permite actuar de manera oportuna. La CRE ha trabajado en el fortalecimiento de los Sistemas de Alerta Temprana Comunitaria, además de establecer umbrales específicos para amenazas que son parte de los PATs.
En el ámbito comunitario, la CRE implementa la metodología AVCA dentro de sus proyectos, analizando el tejido social y la resiliencia de las comunidades para fortalecer su organización y capacidad de respuesta ante emergencias. Sin embargo, se ha identificado la necesidad de incluir información sobre ingresos económicos y factores culturales en los análisis de vulnerabilidad.
Por otro lado, la CRE mantiene tres protocolos de respuesta con Colombia en temas de Salud, Movilidad Humana y la actividad de los volcanes Chile y Cerro Negro, incluyendo el intercambio de información geográfica y datos sobre poblaciones en movilidad humana.

Recomendaciones: 
Ampliación del alcance y capacidad de monitoreo: fortalecer el monitoreo mediante la incorporación de variables clave relacionadas con los Protocolos de Acción Temprana, asegurando un análisis integral de riesgos.

Optimización del flujo de información: Mejorar la comunicación entre los equipos técnicos y la sala de monitoreo, estableciendo protocolos claros para el envío y actualización de datos en tiempo real, garantizando así una gestión más ágil y efectiva de la información.

Coordinación interdepartamental para el monitoreo de despliegues al terreno: En colaboración con los equipos de comunicaciones y seguridad, diseñar e implementar un mecanismo de seguimiento en tiempo real del despliegue de unidades, asegurando un monitoreo eficiente y una respuesta rápida ante posibles incidencias.

component_details.title: Preparedness plans and budgets
component_details.description: Plans identifying organisational resources, determining roles and responsibilities, and developing policies, procedures and activities in order to reach a level of preparedness to be able to respond effectively to a disaster or crisis. Budgets ensure that the necessary financial support is secured to allow capacities to be built and readiness maintained.

component_responses.notes:
La CRE ha establecido rutas de aprendizaje con dos mallas formativas y 63 cursos para personal rentado y voluntario. El Plan Nacional de Respuesta y Preparación define acciones clave, incluyendo los Simulacros Nacionales, que fortalecen las capacidades de los equipos de respuesta.
Recursos Humanos diagnostica anualmente las necesidades de formación, y tras cada Simulacro Nacional (cada dos años), se priorizan las actividades de preparación, incluidas en los Planes Operativos Anuales con presupuesto asignado y apoyo de la cooperación internacional.

Recomendación: Se recomienda desarrollar un Plan Único de Preparación, que integre las prioridades y necesidades de la Sociedad Nacional (SN) y esté alineado con las nuevas tendencias en acción humanitaria. Además de integrar las lecciones aprendidas del ENER 2025, lecciones aprendidas de las últimas operaciones, los resultados de la encuesta de expectativas de necesidades de formación, las actividades de Preparación establecidas en el Plan Nacional de Respuesta, entre otras.

component_details.title: Business continuity
component_details.description: A strategy to counter any potential or anticipated obstacles to effective functioning of the NS, with an eye to ensuring that personnel and assets are protected and able to function in the event of a disaster/crisis.

component_responses.notes:
La Cruz Roja Ecuatoriana (CRE) ha implementado estrategias de continuidad en la práctica, pero no cuenta con un plan genérico que garantice la continuidad de los servicios esenciales en caso de crisis o desastres. Durante la pandemia de Covid-19, se elaboró un plan específico para asegurar el funcionamiento de la SN.
No se ha identificado un procedimiento formal para la reutilización de fondos ante necesidades inesperadas. Sin embargo, en la práctica, se han reorientado recursos de proyectos para cubrir nuevas necesidades surgidas en emergencias. Además, el Plan Nacional de Respuesta, en su módulo 3, establece un mecanismo de coordinación que permite ajustar los planes de acción para reforzar la respuesta o definir estrategias de recuperación.

Recomendación: Desarrollar un Plan o Estrategia de Continuidad de las Actividades para las amenazas potenciales que ponen en riesgos las funciones y servicios esenciales que brinda la CRE a la población, empleados, voluntarios y colaboradores en general durante una crisis o desastre.
