component_responses.notes: IDRL: The NS and government undertook a workshop and desk review in 2013/14. Since then, there have been no further activities on IDRL, perhaps due to few international level responses.  Some key areas of IDRL (e.g. customs, taxes) are known. Others, such as how many international staff can be in-country, should be investigated to mitigate any issues.  An IHL focal point is in place and, with ICRC, strong activities take place with external partners.

component_details.title: Quality and accountability
component_details.description: Describes the essential elements of principled, accountable, and high-quality humanitarian action. The RCRC Movement provides support to the most vulnerable people in line with the Sphere and CHS standards, Code of Conduct for the RCRC Movement and NGOS in Disaster Relief and the Code for Good Partnership of the RCRC Movement, Gender & Diversity, inclusion and protection, BPI/ Do no harm, context-sensitive analysis, violence prevention, accountability to affected population and disability considerations, Community engagement and accountability (CEA).

component_responses.notes: Various global standards (RC internal as well as external) are noted in the draft DRM Policy. There is increased understanding of gender and mainstreaming into programming. CEA is at early stage and a recent review notes its integration into some documents, BDRT and NDRT training and capacity building of regional and HQ staff etc. This has potentially resulted into improved participation of conflict/disaster affected women in beneficiary selection as well as complaint mechanism committees at zonal offices level. However, there are gaps in the absence of a comprehensive plan, established safe and accessible complaints and feedback mechanism (although there is a draft 2017 Manual). Based on learning from the CEA pilot, ERCS is developing a comprehensive and standardised approach for DRM. The NS has not adopted the Protection for Sexual Exploitation and Abuse policy. There is a high reputation risk to the organization as there is a low level of knowledge on CEA issues and its importance.

component_details.title: RC auxiliary role, Mandate and Law
component_details.description: A constitutional reference to the role of the NS in responding to disasters and crises, which may be legislated or included/ recognized in the National Response System.

component_responses.notes: There is an up to date and applied charter and application of auxiliary role with an excellent understanding by all on their auxiliary role. The Charter, mandate and auxiliary role are embedded in policy and procedures and there is active engagement with authorities on IHL.

component_details.title: Hazard, Context and Risk Analysis, Monitoring and Early Warning
component_details.description: Describes how the NS monitors and maps past, present and potential hazards, disasters and crises (e.g. hazard, vulnerability assessments, gathering information from communities and government authorities) and systematically evaluates the damage that could be caused by a potential disaster/crisis, the frequency, severity of the impact, and the alert the relevant areas to scale the preparedness actions to reduce population vulnerability.

component_responses.notes: The NS has increased its actions around this component in the last 2 years. It is actively involved in the national system and improving processes such as the Contingency and Response Planning exercises. The EOC is also new and consolidating its EWS to be integrated with decision making. Cross-border activities are weak. This component has potential to improve based on continued application of new processes in the coming years.

component_details.title: Scenario planning
component_details.description: A set of practical operation plans that closely mirror the generic disaster or crisis response plan but are tailored to a specific hazard type (e.g. earthquake, dengue epidemic, floods, cyclone) and a specific scenario (i.e. number of people affected, their locations and other important factors).

component_responses.notes: A comprehensive set of response options/strategy for all scenarios is not available (long-term). NS prepares contingency plans for imminent risks or response priorities for the year e.g. 2019 response plan or contingency plans for AWD or civil unrest.

component_details.title: Risk management
component_details.description: A mapping of the potential risks in every area, along with its related mitigation measures. Including financial, reputational, organizational risks etc.

component_responses.notes: The NS does not have a comprehensive risk management plan and may be underestimating the potential risks, particularly in light of crisis responses. Some examples were noted by departments but this has not pushed the NS to develop a full risk matrix that is systematic and at high level. There is no dedicated function for crisis management although there is potential to increase risk management as per the RM Policy approach to investment risk. Applying a strategy similar to Resource Mobilization (RM) Policy in the DRM policy would provide a process to show the NS has completed due diligence in case of a complaint, allegation or other reputational risks.

component_details.title: Preparedness plans and budgets
component_details.description: Plans identifying organisational resources, determining roles and responsibilities, and developing policies, procedures and activities in order to reach a level of preparedness to be able to respond effectively to a disaster or crisis. Budgets ensure that the necessary financial support is secured to allow capacities to be built and readiness maintained.

component_responses.notes: The NS has some processes in place which should be carried forward to ensure good practices are replicated. As an example, PER was used to review all 2018 emergency operations resulting a 2019 response plan including capacity building elements based on the gaps in the review. It is recommended to carry out such exercises on annual/regular basis. Movement partners should continue to support as appropriate and as per the Principles and Rules.

component_details.title: Business continuity
component_details.description: A strategy to counter any potential or anticipated obstacles to effective functioning of the NS, with an eye to ensuring that personnel and assets are protected and able to function in the event of a disaster/crisis.

component_responses.notes: An up-to-date, approved business continuity plan for major emergency/crisis situations does not exist. The RM Policy does provide some guidance on re-directing funds.

component_details.title: Emergency Response Procedures (SOPs)
component_details.description: Written guidelines that describe duties and rights of personnel, command structures, coordination with other organizations, and reporting requirements, etc. Includes detailed organogram, decision-making flow chart, and defined roles and responsibilities.

component_responses.notes: SOPs are not approved and not disseminated yet at HQ as well as branches. There is a need for an up-to-date organogram with contact details which the NS plans after its program reconfiguration process is completed.

component_details.title: Response and recovery planning
component_details.description: A documented set of procedures for the disaster/crisis response and recovery process. Including use of local capacities, transition to recovery, type of activities and serivices provided during response and recovery activities and exit strategies, procedures for DREF & EA, and templates for planning, budgeting and accessing funds.

component_responses.notes: There is a strong 2019 Response plan developed based on lessons from the 2018 process. Planning does not consider secondary disasters and risk reduction during a response. Exit, handover or transition strategy are not systematic or explicit. As a result of the 2018 review, the logistics review and benchmarking is underway. DM Policy and SOPs refer to recovery assessments. This requires more details including transition and other actors’ role.

component_details.title: Pre-disaster meetings and agreements
component_details.description: A commitment to arrange meetings and agreements with Movement stakeholders and external actors to identify, plan for and address gaps for any upcoming disaster season (e.g. monsoon, floods or cyclones, or for any generic disaster/crisis event (e.g Epidemic, pandemic, confilict situations). Pre-disaster agreements should set out each partner's role in the event of a disaster/crisis.

component_responses.notes: The NS is increasing preparedness actions including with partners. These processes are relatively new and need to be aligned with the Principles and Rules to ensure that each partner knows and applies their assigned roles.

The NS only engages in Acute Watery Diarrhoea (AWD) and to a limited level malaria but with a well-defined role. Safety protocols for staff and volunteers are not in place. Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) provision should be strengthened. Recent Dead Body Management training did not include necessary kits. There are specific health activities mandated in the RC Charter that should be reviewed to ensure full capacity for a response.

component_details.title: Early Action Mechanisms
component_details.description: Designed to translate warnings into anticipatory actions to help reduce the impact of specific disaster or crisis events. They focus on consolidating available forecasting information and putting procedures in place to ensure that a NS can act ahead of any disaster/crisis. Forecast-based financing is included within the scope of this area.

component_responses.notes: The NS is actively engaged in EWEA including the establishment of FbF taskforce. They are following multiple information challenges from Government, UN, ICRC and the EOC and forthcoming Security Working group  will augment  already established procedures.  This good start needs to be have extended application

component_details.title: Cash Based Intervention (CBI)
component_details.description: An effective and flexible way, including all forms of cash and voucher-based assistance, to support people affected by emergencies, maintaining their dignity and choice, while fostering local economies. Cash should also be mainstreamed into other sectors (including Relief, shelter, livelihoods) and services (Logistics, Finance, etc.)

component_responses.notes: CTP has been used in one response successfully however there is much more work to be done. There are draft process and establishment of some procedures. The commitment to resource this over and above the PNS investment should be clear. CTP requires a close relationship with Communications department.

component_details.title: Emergency Needs Assessment
component_details.description: Assess the extent and impact of the damage caused by the disaster/crisis and the degree of vulnerability of the affected population. The first step in any emergency response, such an assessment will identify the needs that require external intervention and the gaps to be filled. It is a vital component of the programme-planning process.

component_responses.notes: Overall, there is good capacity in Damage and Needs Assessments. NDRT and BDRTs are trained and have experience in the use of templates and new procedures to upload these to the EOC will improve timeliness. Cross-cutting themes should be strengthened in data collection tools leading to more effective and relevant response. Analysis of secondary risks and impact on local social and markets should be systematized.

component_details.title: Affected population selection
component_details.description: Identification and selection of target Affected population for interventions, using a pre-defined set of criteria based on need and vulnerability. This includes consideration of specific vulnerabilities such as disability, age and gender.

component_responses.notes: There are procedures for beneficiary selection, including providing selection criteria to the community. This has been evidenced through secondary data that NS is doing better tailoring of the needs of women, children and vulnerable groups e.g. collection of information about women and vulnerable groups after the BDRT training; prior to that they only reported a total number of affected people. Data management/security needs to be improved (development of policy as well as execution). In connection with the EOC, NS just initiated a process for BDRTs to collect data and send to the EOC for processing, dissemination and necessary decision making.

component_details.title: Emergency Operations Centre (EOC)
component_details.description: A central command and control facility responsible for carrying out disaster/crisis management functions at a strategic level in an emergency situation. The common functions are to collect and analyze data; facilitate decision making that protects life and livelihoods; and disseminate those decisions to all concerned agencies and individuals. Generally located at the headquarter level of an organization.

component_responses.notes: The NS EOC role has operated well in the past without a formal set up and the new EOC should augment the past less formal operations center approach. The formal EOC is very new, not tested (planned for June 2019). When fully operational, the EOC will address many aspects of coordination, decision making, Early Warning, mapping, reporting, etc. As EOC SOPs are not final, they have not been disseminated as yet. All equipment is brand new. With time, the value added of this investment should be demonstrated.

component_details.title: Information Management (IM)
component_details.description: Ability to manage information including requesting, receiving, analyzing and disseminating as per its procedures and partner requirements (IFRC and public authorities in particular). There should be a clear digital/paper trail that documents what, when and how the NS has acted and provides key information for the development of Emergency Plan of Actions. Includes IM between levels, between departments and Situational Reports, mapping, visualisation of data, GO platform (IFRC).

component_responses.notes: The NS has most IM systems in place and uses SharePoint to manage information. Branch level use could be improved.

component_details.title: Testing and Learning
component_details.description: Drills and Simulations allow the organization to test, identify and learn from the results of these type of exercises and incorporate learning into future preparedness and response planning.

component_responses.notes: There was a simulation when the BDRTs and NDRTs were trained. However, with many new and drafted processes (SOPs, DRM Policy, technical sectors and applying vertical integration and connecting with CBO/CDRT teams) this will be vital to ensure smooth application by testing through simulations if not yet done through real-time assessment. Branches participate in government led simulations at local level. CDRTs also conduct simulations as part of CBDRR activities.

component_details.title: Activation of regional and international support
component_details.description: Procedures for requesting and accepting regional and international support in operations, including triggering coordination mechanisms for funding, materials and human resources deployments.

component_responses.notes: Due to the capacity of NS and country context, there have been limited requirements for regional and international support, thus the NS has had little exposure to the requirements of large responses and how to apply the Principles and Rules. The NS is familiar and capable of using IFRC tools such as DREF and EPOA. The EOC provides opportunity to improve on this component through its linkages to Movement tools, websites and the ability to quickly upload information to IFRC regional and global tools.

component_details.title: CHEMICAL, BIOLOGICAL, RADIOLOGICAL AND NUCLEAR (CBRN) EMERGENCY PREPAREDNESS

component_responses.notes: This is relatively new sector based on recent climate related events that require both mitigation and recovery measures. Additional focus including staff is forthcoming. There are opportunities to link this sector to CBDRM.

For this broad sub-component, NS has a limited scope of work in accordance with its mandate and its given capacities. NS is mandated to distribute NFIs and shelters. NS is one of the leading actors in this sector. NS is also a distribution mechanism for other actors. NS does not have a replenishment protocol in place to fully realize its mandate although there are plans within Resource Mobilization and Logistics to maintain this capacity are under way.

component_details.title: MANAGEMENT OF DEAD BODIES TO FACILITATE THEIR IDENTIFICATION

component_responses.notes: RFL is a mandated role of the NS. It works closely with ICRC and manuals and procedures are in place. There are plans for continual improvement including modern tools, additional services such as PSS. RFL is well incorporated into most programs.
While there are recovery actions, there is no deliberate approach and considerations in planning. Linkages to CBDRM creates options for increasing capacity.

component_details.title: NS-specific areas of intervention
component_details.description: Sector-specific or services provided by the NS in case of emergencies, it is in line with the NS mandate and legislation in country. It includes Community Based DP/DRR, Evacuation, Health in Emergencies, Epidemic and Pandemic, First aid, WASH, Food security and Livelihoods, Search and rRescue, Shelter, Management of dead bodies, RFL, Transition to recovery, and CBRN preparedness.

component_responses.notes: First Aid is a strength of the NS, particularly in its Commercial First Aid Engagement. There is an opportunity to increase first aid skills through CBDRM programs. The importance for all staff and volunteers to be trained in basic First Aid was noted as a gap during the Airline Crash 2019 response.

The NS has good coordination and arrangements with government authorities for technical, HR and equipment support as well as established support mechanism with Movement partners. Good coordination with external actors is also in practice. WASH staff at HQ are not trained as part of the NDRT and are limited to a coordination and compliance role. The NS does not have basic equipment such as professional GPS and is fully dependent on the government office and private contractors.

There is a solid approach and strong linkages with the government health system but this is mainly project specific. The core structure is limited. There is no simulation, but refresher training. There are some CBHFA related mandated activities in the Charter which should be prioritized.

When applied as Food Aid during Response this is a strength of the NS. It has key partnerships with WFP for nutritious food supplements. In 2019, it added food aid with the government and other actors in-country and are a partner of choice due to their access and trust. The NS role is appropriate for its capacities and does not over stretch the NS yet brings recognition both with partners and communities.

CBDRM is a new sector for ERCS and there is a strong intention to continue with the approach as a means to connect with community, improve local capacities and ensure ERCS has access and trust when large responses are needed. The CBDRR process follows good practice of the Movement by integrating the community across appropriate aspects of response. More practice and expansion are anticipated as Branches see this program as value added and it is incorporated into the Theory of Change and Program Reconfiguration Process.

component_details.title: Mapping of NS capacities
component_details.description: A list of the NS capacities including HR (staff, response teams and volunteers) and equipment that are available for disaster/crisis response. Teams could include branch and national response teams. This should be defined by technical speciality where relevant.

component_responses.notes: There is knowledge of capacities but these are not systematically mapped and updated. Aligning gaps and needs to training plans could be improved. BDRTs’ and NDRT’s capacity should be maintained through regular refreshment with strong commitments to this by Branches and NS leadership.

component_details.title: Coordination with External Agencies and NGOs
component_details.description: Mechanism that facilitates coordination and collaboration with Non-Governmental Organization (NGO), both local and international NGOs, civil society organizations (CSOs) and United Nations agencies in country.

component_responses.notes: The NS has increased its engagement with multiple UN and INGO actors through coordination mechanism but also direct partnerships and projects. The selection of partners could be more strategic and the NS could demonstrate their leadership more than an implementing partner. There has been a strategic decision not to engage with national NGO consortia as per the principle of impartiality.

component_details.title: Civil Military Relations
component_details.description: Dialogue and interaction with military actors, essential to protect and promote humanitarian principles, avoid competition, minimize inconsistency and, when appropriate, pursue common goals.

component_details.title: Coordination with Movement
component_details.description: Mechanisms that facilitate the coordination with ICRC, IFRC, and PNS in-country.

component_responses.notes: Movement Coordination is overall good in terms of the relationships between the parties. The NS needs to take a stronger role as per the Principles and Rules and actively lead the Movement Coordination. Re-engaging in the SMCC could be a consideration.

component_details.title: Coordination with authorities
component_details.description: Mechanism that facilitates coordination and cooperation with local and national authorities. It is connected to the NS auxiliary role for humanitarian assistance.

component_responses.notes: The ERCS relationship with authorities is strong, based on a good understanding of the Charter. There is a good relationship including the government engagement in process such as the DRM review. There is an improved balance of independence. There is good cross-sectoral engagement.

component_details.title: Coordination with local community level responders
component_details.description: Engagement with Community Disaster Response Teams (CDRTs), through training, coordination, and the development of community disaster preparedness and response plans.

component_responses.notes: Community Based Disaster Response is recent but the long-term relationship with the community as a trusted, neutral partner has assured access to all parts of the country. Adding CBDRM programming will enhance this.

component_details.title: Cooperation with private sector
component_details.description: Mechanism that allows cooperation with private sector that often plays a strong role in response, particularly if there is impact on their staff and businesses. There is often a willingness to donate goods and services. Advance agreements help to expedite response actions.

component_responses.notes: The NS has increased its engagement primarily through its Resource Mobilization activities. There are now more opportunities for private sector engagement in Ethiopia but also more competition for these resources. The NS is aware of possible risks and impacts of working with corporations and are addressing these through the Resource Mobilization policy/strategy and SOPs.

component_details.title: Resource Mobilisation
component_details.description: A documented strategy for raising domestic funds from the government, private sector, general public and other in-country actors to support the national society’s response. This would include allocation of responsibilities, practical mechanisms for accepting funds and for being accountable on funds.

component_responses.notes: There is a strategic commitment of the NS to increasing their local resources to ensure on-going functionality. The Resource Mobilization (RM) policy is being implemented. Finalization of draft Strategy and SOPs is in process. There is an ambitious plan to grow. NS has a good understanding of its costs but less of the requirements to maintain core mandated programs as per the Charter. Branches have been involved in the development of documents and are in agreement with procedures. Some branches struggle with RM at their level due to constraints of size, membership etc. Others have more opportunities such as rentals and land use options.

NS HQ has a dedicated function to carry out and coordinate all logistics activities with trained staff. However, there is a need to adapt and align logistics functions with the needs during response. It is developing an optimal supply chain options including framework agreements and pre-qualified suppliers. NS has 4 strategic warehouses, and for relief items is following one standard closely reflecting population needs. Volunteers are not trained is specific logistics functions as a surge capacity (e.g. logistics NDRT, BDRT).//NS maintains an up-to-date inventory of their stock and equipment, and reports are shared with DRM team on a monthly basis. It has all the necessary privileges for importation and gets help (payment etc.) from IFRC for international procurement. There is an established mechanism for branches to request need-based additional items from HQ (and in many cases from neighbouring branches). NS has procedures for the management of in-kind donations. The NS inventory processes should be improved by linking with SAP B1. //NS is in process of updating database of and pre-agreements with suppliers for key items and services for emergency response. This includes blacklisting and compliance mechanism. Procurement procedures are recent but not aligned with SAP B1. There are no expedited procedures and NFI replenishment is not timely.//The Fleet is in a range of condition, with HQ in good condition but branches have older vehicles, in need of replacement which is in process. New templates are being used while the Fleet and Transportation Manual is in the process of revision. While drivers are trained in basic First Aid, there are insufficient safety measure and driver skill development. Seatbelts for all passengers is not enforced. Maintenance arrangements vary depending on level/ tiers and magnitude of work.//Most of warehouses are owned by NS and it may also rent in case of big response. Some branches rent out extra space to other actors to generate income.

component_details.title: Staff and volunteer management
component_details.description: Well-functioning staff and volunteer management systems and practices allow for effective recruitment, supervision, support and encouragement of staff and volunteers.

component_responses.notes: Currently, while the NS is piloting the Leadership Competency Framework, learning paths are not in place and competencies per required roles are not identified especially for staff. However, the consultative development of competency framework (in year 5) leads to ownership by ERCS and supports analysis of leadership improvement process. The framework outlines the competencies required by the executive and senior management staff as well as a professional development plan with options to address areas that require improvement. There is limited training on protection and self-care. Staff and volunteers are not briefed on security prior to deployment. Code of Conduct (CoC) is signed by staff but is not annually updated. Volunteers do not sign CoC at all. There is limited training on CoC i.e. only for response teams. The NS does not have a formal personnel rotation and retention strategy for response.

component_details.title: Safety and security management
component_details.description: Addresses policy and procedures to ensure the safety of staff and volunteers. This include awareness, effective recruitment, training and management processes in place to ensure that personnel are capable of undertaking the roles demanded of them (from NS operational, management and leaders) according to the Stay Safe (IFRC) and Safer Access (ICRC). Based on safer access framework, including concepts of access, perception, identification and acceptance, and protection and violence prevention.

component_responses.notes: The NS has taken recent steps to improve safety and security. SAF is actively being applied including with BDRTs and NDRT. There is a new Safety Officer and a Steering Committee will shortly be started. Improving and including protocols in the SOPs and EOC through EWS will enhance this component. During deployment, security support should be increased including briefings before and regular updates while in the field. The NS should ensure security risks are regularly reviewed/mitigated as part of Risk Management.

component_details.title: Communication in emergencies
component_details.description: Incorporates a system of public messaging to enable the NS to share timely, accurate information before, during, and after a disaster or crisis.

component_responses.notes: The NS has a good communications structure but need to enhance Communications in Emergencies (CiE) and recognize the importance and potential risks if CiE protocols are not standardized. This includes identifying and training key spokespersons for the NS as well as ensuring staff and volunteers take care in communicating, even as individuals, in social media.

component_details.title: Operations Monitoring, Evaluation, Reporting and Learning
component_details.description: The PMERL is designed to implement a results-based planning, monitoring and evaluation system that provides an evidence base of NS performance, including relevance, efficiency, effectiveness, sustainability and impact. A reliable and trusted organization is accountable, providing transparent and timely information and building systems to strengthen data collection and reporting. It is data-driven, analytical and results-based.

component_responses.notes: There have been many reviews, learnings and after action reviews by the NS in the last few years indicating a high focus on learning. However, follow-up and tracking of key lessons and recommendations from reviews, evaluations and lessons learned are weak. CEA (including complaints and feedback) mechanism remains to be fully established to ensure community level impacts and recommendations are integrated.

component_details.title: Finance and Admin policy and emergency procedures
component_details.description: Overall budgeting, accounting, treasury, assets, financial reporting and financial services operations. it also includes the efficient delivery , cost effective and timely services to the NS. Pre-approved, auditable, expedited procedures that allow for flexibility during a disaster/crisis. These must meet transparency, oversight and accountability standards. Procedures may include faster approval processes, fewer signatures, different authority levels. The Emergency Procedures are activated for a specific period of time.

component_responses.notes: Procedures and processes are strong including sufficient resources for auditing. The Charter requires annual audited statements which is in practice. The department could be more proactive in identifying opportunities to expedite for responses and create procedures that allow for rapid support including quick financial approvals. Stronger linkages to the DRM planning process particularly on budgets is one of the areas for further focussed.

component_details.title: Information and Communication Technology (ICT)
component_details.description: Refers to technologies that provide access to information through telecommunications. This includes the Internet, wireless networks, mobile phones, radios and other communication mediums.

component_responses.notes: Technologies are being used appropriately including use of mobile phones, social media and equipment. This could be improved by use of dedicated equipment and phones for key staff rather than personal phones. There needs to be backups such as landlines in the event of loss of cell phone and reliable internet services.

component_details.title: RC auxiliary role, Mandate and Law
component_details.description: A constitutional reference to the role of the NS in responding to disasters and crises, which may be legislated or included/ recognized in the National Response System.

component_details.title: DRM Strategy
component_details.description: An outline of the overall goal that the NS seeks to achieve in its disaster and crisis response operations. The goal considers: context analysis, ongoing/regular all-hazards risk assessments: it may define the target proportion of affected population that will be reached, and a definition of the areas/sectors where a NS will usually respond during an emergency.

component_details.title: DRM Policy
component_details.description: Reflects the NS mission, RCRC principles and mandate. It acknowledges other relevant NS policies, and aligns with the government policy (where applicable), incorporating the general rules that the NS will obey in order to achieve something (i.e mandate, strategy, etc.)

component_details.title: DRM Laws, Advocacy and Dissemination
component_details.description: Designed to support the NS in improving legal preparedness for disasters and crisis and to promote the use of the IDRL Guidelines in order to reduce human vulnerability.

component_details.title: Quality and accountability
component_details.description: Describes the essential elements of principled, accountable, and high-quality humanitarian action. The RCRC Movement provides support to the most vulnerable people in line with the Sphere and CHS standards, Code of Conduct for the RCRC Movement and NGOS in Disaster Relief and the Code for Good Partnership of the RCRC Movement, Gender & Diversity, inclusion and protection, BPI/ Do no harm, context-sensitive analysis, violence prevention, accountability to affected population and disability considerations, Community engagement and accountability (CEA).

component_details.title: Business continuity
component_details.description: A strategy to counter any potential or anticipated obstacles to effective functioning of the NS, with an eye to ensuring that personnel and assets are protected and able to function in the event of a disaster/crisis.

component_details.title: Emergency Response Procedures (SOPs)
component_details.description: Written guidelines that describe duties and rights of personnel, command structures, coordination with other organizations, and reporting requirements, etc. Includes detailed organogram, decision-making flow chart, and defined roles and responsibilities.

component_details.title: Response and recovery planning
component_details.description: A documented set of procedures for the disaster/crisis response and recovery process. Including use of local capacities, transition to recovery, type of activities and serivices provided during response and recovery activities and exit strategies, procedures for DREF & EA, and templates for planning, budgeting and accessing funds.

component_details.title: Pre-disaster meetings and agreements
component_details.description: A commitment to arrange meetings and agreements with Movement stakeholders and external actors to identify, plan for and address gaps for any upcoming disaster season (e.g. monsoon, floods or cyclones, or for any generic disaster/crisis event (e.g Epidemic, pandemic, confilict situations). Pre-disaster agreements should set out each partner's role in the event of a disaster/crisis.

component_details.title: Hazard, Context and Risk Analysis, Monitoring and Early Warning
component_details.description: Describes how the NS monitors and maps past, present and potential hazards, disasters and crises (e.g. hazard, vulnerability assessments, gathering information from communities and government authorities) and systematically evaluates the damage that could be caused by a potential disaster/crisis, the frequency, severity of the impact, and the alert the relevant areas to scale the preparedness actions to reduce population vulnerability.

component_details.title: Scenario planning
component_details.description: A set of practical operation plans that closely mirror the generic disaster or crisis response plan but are tailored to a specific hazard type (e.g. earthquake, dengue epidemic, floods, cyclone) and a specific scenario (i.e. number of people affected, their locations and other important factors).

component_details.title: Risk management
component_details.description: A mapping of the potential risks in every area, along with its related mitigation measures. Including financial, reputational, organizational risks etc.

component_details.title: Preparedness plans and budgets
component_details.description: Plans identifying organisational resources, determining roles and responsibilities, and developing policies, procedures and activities in order to reach a level of preparedness to be able to respond effectively to a disaster or crisis. Budgets ensure that the necessary financial support is secured to allow capacities to be built and readiness maintained.

component_details.title: Mapping of NS capacities
component_details.description: A list of the NS capacities including HR (staff, response teams and volunteers) and equipment that are available for disaster/crisis response. Teams could include branch and national response teams. This should be defined by technical speciality where relevant.

component_details.title: Early Action Mechanisms
component_details.description: Designed to translate warnings into anticipatory actions to help reduce the impact of specific disaster or crisis events. They focus on consolidating available forecasting information and putting procedures in place to ensure that a NS can act ahead of any disaster/crisis. Forecast-based financing is included within the scope of this area.

component_details.title: Cash Based Intervention (CBI)
component_details.description: An effective and flexible way, including all forms of cash and voucher-based assistance, to support people affected by emergencies, maintaining their dignity and choice, while fostering local economies. Cash should also be mainstreamed into other sectors (including Relief, shelter, livelihoods) and services (Logistics, Finance, etc.)

component_details.title: Emergency Needs Assessment
component_details.description: Assess the extent and impact of the damage caused by the disaster/crisis and the degree of vulnerability of the affected population. The first step in any emergency response, such an assessment will identify the needs that require external intervention and the gaps to be filled. It is a vital component of the programme-planning process.

component_details.title: Affected population selection
component_details.description: Identification and selection of target Affected population for interventions, using a pre-defined set of criteria based on need and vulnerability. This includes consideration of specific vulnerabilities such as disability, age and gender.

component_details.title: Emergency Operations Centre (EOC)
component_details.description: A central command and control facility responsible for carrying out disaster/crisis management functions at a strategic level in an emergency situation. The common functions are to collect and analyze data; facilitate decision making that protects life and livelihoods; and disseminate those decisions to all concerned agencies and individuals. Generally located at the headquarter level of an organization.

component_details.title: Information Management (IM)
component_details.description: Ability to manage information including requesting, receiving, analyzing and disseminating as per its procedures and partner requirements (IFRC and public authorities in particular). There should be a clear digital/paper trail that documents what, when and how the NS has acted and provides key information for the development of Emergency Plan of Actions. Includes IM between levels, between departments and Situational Reports, mapping, visualisation of data, GO platform (IFRC).

component_details.title: Testing and Learning
component_details.description: Drills and Simulations allow the organization to test, identify and learn from the results of these type of exercises and incorporate learning into future preparedness and response planning.

component_details.title: Activation of regional and international support
component_details.description: Procedures for requesting and accepting regional and international support in operations, including triggering coordination mechanisms for funding, materials and human resources deployments.

component_details.title: CHEMICAL, BIOLOGICAL, RADIOLOGICAL AND NUCLEAR (CBRN) EMERGENCY PREPAREDNESS
MANAGEMENT OF DEAD BODIES TO FACILITATE THEIR IDENTIFICATION
NS-specific areas of intervention
component_details.description: Sector-specific or services provided by the NS in case of emergencies, it is in line with the NS mandate and legislation in country. It includes Community Based DP/DRR, Evacuation, Health in Emergencies, Epidemic and Pandemic, First aid, WASH, Food security and Livelihoods, Search and rRescue, Shelter, Management of dead bodies, RFL, Transition to recovery, and CBRN preparedness.

component_details.title: Coordination with local community level responders
component_details.description: Engagement with Community Disaster Response Teams (CDRTs), through training, coordination, and the development of community disaster preparedness and response plans.

component_details.title: Cooperation with private sector
component_details.description: Mechanism that allows cooperation with private sector that often plays a strong role in response, particularly if there is impact on their staff and businesses. There is often a willingness to donate goods and services. Advance agreements help to expedite response actions.

component_details.title: Coordination with External Agencies and NGOs
component_details.description: Mechanism that facilitates coordination and collaboration with Non-Governmental Organization (NGO), both local and international NGOs, civil society organizations (CSOs) and United Nations agencies in country.

component_details.title: Civil Military Relations
component_details.description: Dialogue and interaction with military actors, essential to protect and promote humanitarian principles, avoid competition, minimize inconsistency and, when appropriate, pursue common goals.

component_details.title: Coordination with Movement
component_details.description: Mechanisms that facilitate the coordination with ICRC, IFRC, and PNS in-country.

component_details.title: Coordination with authorities
component_details.description: Mechanism that facilitates coordination and cooperation with local and national authorities. It is connected to the NS auxiliary role for humanitarian assistance.

component_details.title: Staff and volunteer management
component_details.description: Well-functioning staff and volunteer management systems and practices allow for effective recruitment, supervision, support and encouragement of staff and volunteers.

component_details.title: Safety and security management
component_details.description: Addresses policy and procedures to ensure the safety of staff and volunteers. This include awareness, effective recruitment, training and management processes in place to ensure that personnel are capable of undertaking the roles demanded of them (from NS operational, management and leaders) according to the Stay Safe (IFRC) and Safer Access (ICRC). Based on safer access framework, including concepts of access, perception, identification and acceptance, and protection and violence prevention.

component_details.title: Resource Mobilisation
