component_details.title: DRM Strategy
component_details.description: An outline of the overall goal that the NS seeks to achieve in its disaster and crisis response operations. The goal considers: context analysis, ongoing/regular all-hazards risk assessments: it may define the target proportion of affected population that will be reached, and a definition of the areas/sectors where a NS will usually respond during an emergency.

component_responses.notes: "•	GRCS has DRM Strategy in place (2020 – 2024) and reflects the NS mandate, analysis of country context, trends, operational objectives, success indicators for the Strategic Pillars. •	It considers different specific areas of intervention, such as DM, WASH, Shelter, Livelihood, RFL, as well as cross-cutting themes.  •	There is a plan to review the Strategy every 4 years. The review will be interdepartmental which includes representation from HQ and branches as well.  •	Among ""Natural Hazards and Vulnerabilities"" , the DRM strategy identifies some public health risks such as epidemics / disease outbreaks. •	There appears to be no sectorial plans of actions linked to the DRM Strategy. •	DRM Strategy seems to also lack dissemination among staff and volunteers. "

component_details.title: DRM Policy
component_details.description: Reflects the NS mission, RCRC principles and mandate. It acknowledges other relevant NS policies, and aligns with the government policy (where applicable), incorporating the general rules that the NS will obey in order to achieve something (i.e mandate, strategy, etc.)

component_responses.notes: "•	NS doesn’t have DRM Policy; however, DRM Strategy contains some elements, which provide a framework for the NS to guide decision-making on the response approach and actions.  •	Specific GRCS overarching Policy priorities identifying for how NS shall conduct all its disaster risk management operations and programs, as well as linkages with various Movement and government frameworks still need to be outlined."

component_details.title: DRM Laws, Advocacy and Dissemination
component_details.description: Designed to support the NS in improving legal preparedness for disasters and crisis and to promote the use of the IDRL Guidelines in order to reduce human vulnerability.

component_responses.notes: "•	The Act that establishes the NS has elements of International Diplomacy but there are no specific IDRL plans in place or documents signed. •	The NS Communications Manager was trained in IHL in an emergency. •	NS doesn’t have exemptions for tax, importation custom costs etc. However, the current review of the Act (hasn’t been approved yet) includes some aspect of facilitation of International Disaster Relief and waivers of tax and duties on import of relief materials.  •	NS management understands and complies with domestic legal and policy framework relating to public health risks and public health emergencies. ICRC is supporting the NS in data policy for epidemic control to align it with the National Data Protection Commission."

component_details.title: Quality and accountability
component_details.description: Describes the essential elements of principled, accountable, and high-quality humanitarian action. The RCRC Movement provides support to the most vulnerable people in line with the Sphere and CHS standards, Code of Conduct for the RCRC Movement and NGOS in Disaster Relief and the Code for Good Partnership of the RCRC Movement, Gender & Diversity, inclusion and protection, BPI/ Do no harm, context-sensitive analysis, violence prevention, accountability to affected population and disability considerations, Community engagement and accountability (CEA).

component_responses.notes: "•	CEA included into the DRM Strategy as cross cutting sector and integrated to the planning of operations and programs. •	GRCS has some CEA mechanisms in place, communities are involved in the assessment, design, and implementation of activities.  •	CEA ToT has been conducted for selected HQ and regional staff, as well as volunteers. However, more subsequent training is required. •	GRCS doesn’t have HQ CEA focal point, some regional managers act as CEA FPs for the branches. •	NS doesn’t have CEA plan developed, however, some activities for improvement are incorporated to the DRM Strategy.  •	Elements of the feedback mechanism exist (suggestion boxes installed in the communities where intervention is taking place), however mechanism could be improved especially in the areas of and analyzing the received information and conducting follow-ups. •	Information on SGBV is collected through CEA mechanisms. However, the capacity of NS to respond to SGBV concerns is unclear (i.e., referral pathways).  •	NS doesn’t have PSEA Policy, however, some elements of it are included in the Code of Conduct for Staff."

component_details.title: Business continuity
component_details.description: A strategy to counter any potential or anticipated obstacles to effective functioning of the NS, with an eye to ensuring that personnel and assets are protected and able to function in the event of a disaster/crisis.

component_responses.notes: "•	NS doesn't have up-to-date and approved BCP for major emergency/crisis situation.  •	In the beginning of pandemic in 2019 GRCS developed COVID-19 Business Continuity Plan to ensure the organization can keep working. It was the first time that brought out the BCP idea to NS.  •	NS had experience of communication with donors to repurpose funds for unexpected or emerging needs (e.g., requesting repurposing funds of the DRR Climate Change Swiss Red Cross project)."

component_details.title: Emergency Response Procedures (SOPs)
component_details.description: Written guidelines that describe duties and rights of personnel, command structures, coordination with other organizations, and reporting requirements, etc. Includes detailed organogram, decision-making flow chart, and defined roles and responsibilities.

component_responses.notes: "•	NS doesn’t have up-to-date, approved SOPs for all specific areas of intervention and support services to respond to disasters and crises. •	When government SOPs are developed, and GRCS takes part in discussions along with other partners. •	NS provided financial and technical support to NADMO with SOPs development for 2 regions. •	Decision making flowchart which assigns decision making responsibility accordingly at each level is included to the DRM Strategy."

component_details.title: Response and recovery planning
component_details.description: A documented set of procedures for the disaster/crisis response and recovery process. Including use of local capacities, transition to recovery, type of activities and serivices provided during response and recovery activities and exit strategies, procedures for DREF & EA, and templates for planning, budgeting and accessing funds.

component_responses.notes: "•	NS does not have a pre-disaster response plan for potential hazards. NS normally develops its own response plan based on government plan and when a disaster or emergency has happened (COVID-19, Floods, Apeate Explosions, Elections) with support from partners. •	However, gender, age, disability and diversity complexities and community capacities considerations are included in the response plans.  •	Response plans include wide participation of community, staff, volunteers, governance, management, and technical inputs from IFRC where relevant. Community engagement and accountability is a high priority and embedded in all activities and planning. •	During IFRC supported operations GRCS conduct lessons learned. NS analyses the previous operation (e.g., during Apeate Explosions response)."

component_details.title: Pre-disaster meetings and agreements
component_details.description: A commitment to arrange meetings and agreements with Movement stakeholders and external actors to identify, plan for and address gaps for any upcoming disaster season (e.g. monsoon, floods or cyclones, or for any generic disaster/crisis event (e.g Epidemic, pandemic, confilict situations). Pre-disaster agreements should set out each partner's role in the event of a disaster/crisis.

component_responses.notes: "•	Pre-Disaster meetings are mostly held between the NS and communities and sometimes with donors. NS also participants in coordination meetings with the government and other actors. However, they mostly happen on ad hoc basis. •	Good example of pre-disaster planning are meetings that have been happening among NS and partners before the Elections.  •	NS doesn't have pre-disaster agreements with key suppliers of goods and services. The agreement with financial service provider (Fidelity bank) is signed and can be activated.  •	It does not appear that all contractors have signed the CoC, however, some elements of CoC could have been included to the contracts (to be verified by NS). •	No agreements exist in terms of import of Humanitarian aid items which poses a challenge in clearance of imported humanitarian goods. However, an agreement exists with Ministry of Foreign Affairs which helps with Visa issuance for personnel."

component_details.title: Hazard, Context and Risk Analysis, Monitoring and Early Warning
component_details.description: Describes how the NS monitors and maps past, present and potential hazards, disasters and crises (e.g. hazard, vulnerability assessments, gathering information from communities and government authorities) and systematically evaluates the damage that could be caused by a potential disaster/crisis, the frequency, severity of the impact, and the alert the relevant areas to scale the preparedness actions to reduce population vulnerability.

component_responses.notes: "•	NS has some elements of risk monitoring on national and regional levels. For example, through participating in pre-disaster meetings, information exchange with other stakeholders. It appears there is no risk monitoring focal point in NS. •	NS monitors the situation in the field and reports on major emerging, social and economic trends. In addition to primary data, the information about high-risk communities also comes from other resources (secondary data), for e.g., NADMO. NS starts with the secondary data and then goes to communities to verify it and plan and deliver an intervention. •	GRCS had experience in cross-border coordination with neighbouring countries (e.g., with Cote-d'Ivoire re Ebola response). Moreover, NS branches coordinate risk monitoring across the regions.  •	NS doesn’t have Early Warning systems established.  •	NS has experience in conducting VCAs for the communities mostly in projects’ supported locations."

component_details.title: Scenario planning
component_details.description: A set of practical operation plans that closely mirror the generic disaster or crisis response plan but are tailored to a specific hazard type (e.g. earthquake, dengue epidemic, floods, cyclone) and a specific scenario (i.e. number of people affected, their locations and other important factors).

component_responses.notes: "•	NS doesn't develop pre-disaster scenarios. Analysis is done when EpoA for a specific response is being developed.  •	NS hasn't developed humanitarian scenarios for high-risk areas in the country. •	NS doesn't have Contingency plans. Some regional government plans exist with the RC role mentioned for certain areas of response."

component_details.title: Risk management
component_details.description: A mapping of the potential risks in every area, along with its related mitigation measures. Including financial, reputational, organizational risks etc.

component_responses.notes: "•	The NS does not conduct risk management holistically across technical sectors and does not identify and operationalize mitigation measures (including in cases of reputational risks).  •	However, systematic finance procedure and internal control mechanism are in place for financial risks (for example, fraud and corruption prevention) •	Risk management responsibility has not been assigned to a trained and dedicated staff member.  •	The NS does not have a crisis management unit/function to manage critical incidents in a systematic way.  •	It appears that NS ensures the protection of first responders; they are only deployed after necessary training and provision of essential PPE. •	It was also noted that the NS has identified trusted sources of communication to ensure community engagement and public health messaging."

component_details.title: Preparedness plans and budgets
component_details.description: Plans identifying organisational resources, determining roles and responsibilities, and developing policies, procedures and activities in order to reach a level of preparedness to be able to respond effectively to a disaster or crisis. Budgets ensure that the necessary financial support is secured to allow capacities to be built and readiness maintained.

component_responses.notes: "•	This component needs improvement but participation of Ghana Red Cross in 2017 OCAC, Cash Preparedness assessments, as well as 2022 PER self-assessment process validates the commitment of GRCS towards preparedness elements.  •	It has been noted that necessary coordination exists among health and DM/Health teams for epidemic preparedness. •	Currently, there is an ongoing development of preparedness plan and budget (Standby DREF) for Flooding. •	Financial gaps for preparedness and early actions are not identified, and there is no preparedness fund available. •	In some regions there are limited prepositioned items with support of partners (e.g., shelter replenishment kits and family tents), however, not all areas are covered. Moreover, the items are not replenished. •	It was noted that having NFIs, jerry cans prepositioned in high-risk areas would also be helpful, as well as conducting a regular mapping of those areas."

"•	Considered in the DRM strategy among DRR and Livelihood areas of focus. •	Food Security approached from a community-based angle, with Mothers club including some elements. However, no systematic collection and analysis of data on food security.  •	No dedicated staff, as food interventions are not a priority for NS."

"•	Strengthening capacities of the NS in search and rescue is part of the Strategic Pillar 1 in the DRM Strategy. •	NDTRs and CDRTs are trained in Search and Rescue, but equipment is not available. •	Leadership is with the NADMO, however whereas the NS disposes of more capacities, it takes the lead. •	GRCS has ongoing collaboration with other partners, including for evacuation. "

"•	NS Interventions are community led with involvement of all the groups. However, it was noted that inclusion of marginalized groups needs to be strengthened in planning and design of programs.  •	GRCS has Community based early warning systems in projects' supported areas. The volunteers are linked up with the reports from the weather-related agencies and they feedback the communities with the information.  •	GRCS is engaged in regular awareness raising and public education on disasters and crises through Mass media, radio stations (e.g., District disaster response teams (DDRTs) participate in radio panel discussions), TV. There is also some engagement on social media, however, it could be improved.  •	The CDPRTs are trained to respond to various disasters (e.g., floods). Some trainings on Epidemics control have been conducted. However, not for all the regions."

component_details.title: Mapping of NS capacities
component_details.description: A list of the NS capacities including HR (staff, response teams and volunteers) and equipment that are available for disaster/crisis response. Teams could include branch and national response teams. This should be defined by technical speciality where relevant.

component_responses.notes: "•	Some sectors of intervention (e.g., Shelter, Livelihoods) are missing focal points. Both at HQ and regional level staff play multiple roles (e.g., in Upper West region there is FP for Health, but also covers WASH and CVA). •	GRCS has trained staff (e.g. Head of Disaster Manager and Health Coordinator), as well as volunteers to lead the initial response. However, NS could use more trained staff, as well as equipment. •	Staff and volunteers receive trainings regarding specific areas of intervention; however, they are not regular across the country, don’t include refresher trainings and are mostly linked with the specific projects.   •	NS doesn’t have database for response materials and equipment. •	The available resources are not sufficient to cover all branches. However, in terms of warehouse stocks, materials may be shared amongst regions when needed."

"•	During Health interventions NS collaborates with Ghana Health Services department (e.g., by conducting joint multisectoral assessments and data sharing).  •	NS can identify multisectoral response needs in epidemic outbreaks (e.g., considered economic impact during epidemics. Livelihood support provided through CVA during COVID-19). •	GRCS has expertise in RCCE and surveillance (passive referral). It engages with community various groups; however, feedback and complaints mechanisms could be improved.  •	NS has experience in cross-border coordination (e.g., EVD 2015). •	GRCS doesn’t have pre-positioned items for the epidemic response (only water treatment units and mosquito nets). •	There is a lack of staff-back up, NS staff and volunteers at regional and district levels might require some capacity building (e.g., organising health in emergencies related trainings). "

component_details.title: Early Action Mechanisms
component_details.description: Designed to translate warnings into anticipatory actions to help reduce the impact of specific disaster or crisis events. They focus on consolidating available forecasting information and putting procedures in place to ensure that a NS can act ahead of any disaster/crisis. Forecast-based financing is included within the scope of this area.

component_responses.notes: "•	Elements of EWEA system exist in project supported areas. •	Main modalities include: door to door and community information centers run by communities (radio and TV). Advantage: local language + community ownership. Disadvantage: low coverage    •	No modern systems for EW/EA: text messages alerts, google forecasts.  •	Clear 2-way communication channels exist within the NS in case of emergencies, however, not always used properly. Sometimes volunteers bypass the chain of communication and contact headquarter directly without informing lead volunteer."

component_details.title: Cash Based Intervention (CBI)
component_details.description: An effective and flexible way, including all forms of cash and voucher-based assistance, to support people affected by emergencies, maintaining their dignity and choice, while fostering local economies. Cash should also be mainstreamed into other sectors (including Relief, shelter, livelihoods) and services (Logistics, Finance, etc.)

component_responses.notes: "•	In October 2021 GRCS engaged in CVA preparedness self-assessment to determine key action points to enhance delivery of response through CVA modality. As a result of the assessment clear PoA with timelines and budget was developed for 2022. •	NS has CBI trained and experienced staff, however, no dedicated focal point. •	NS is a part of TWG led by IFRC. •	However, there is no pre- disaster market feasibility analysis done. Most times it is conducted during a response operation in a particular region. •	Some CBI SOPs are available. One of the disadvantages of the current process is that GRCS does not get reports from the bank to track how many people received the transfer. Recommendation would be to have cash distribution report done at the end of each cash intervention for monitoring and compliance. •	GRCS has an agreement signed with Fidelity Bank (finance service provider for CVA)."

component_details.title: Emergency Needs Assessment
component_details.description: Assess the extent and impact of the damage caused by the disaster/crisis and the degree of vulnerability of the affected population. The first step in any emergency response, such an assessment will identify the needs that require external intervention and the gaps to be filled. It is a vital component of the programme-planning process.

component_responses.notes: "•	GRCS doesn't have specific assessment team in place, but has some volunteers trained in data collection. NS adopts IFRC data collection templates and adjusts them based on particular disaster.  •	Data is collected through Kobo using tablets, which are usually at HQ and deployed during the disaster. Challenges include time of deployment of tablets to field, data synchronization, uploading to servers and data protection mechanisms. •	GRCS collects data disaggregated by Age, Gender, and Disability. •	Most of the assessments are done in coordination with NADMO and other partners. •	Emergency needs assessment results are cross checked and validated with community members."

component_details.title: Affected population selection
component_details.description: Identification and selection of target Affected population for interventions, using a pre-defined set of criteria based on need and vulnerability. This includes consideration of specific vulnerabilities such as disability, age and gender.

component_responses.notes: "•	GRCS affected population selection is:  - agreed with community leaders and representatives of different groups;  - developed based on intended response to a particular disaster;  - consider specific vulnerabilities;  - shared and aligned with other stakeholders.  •	Beneficiary list is cross checked with communities to ensure that targeted criteria are met. In addition, if another credible agency (e.g., NADMO or UN) already plans an assessment, it is not repeated, but rather coordinated.  •	Data collected by Kobo is uploaded to an Excel file through a server channel. Volunteers are trained on Data Collection (templates, tools etc.) before deployment especially during Detailed assessment linked to a response. •	GRCS does not have Data protection policy in place."

component_details.title: Emergency Operations Centre (EOC)
component_details.description: A central command and control facility responsible for carrying out disaster/crisis management functions at a strategic level in an emergency situation. The common functions are to collect and analyze data; facilitate decision making that protects life and livelihoods; and disseminate those decisions to all concerned agencies and individuals. Generally located at the headquarter level of an organization.

component_responses.notes: "•	NS EOC does not exist. However, for operational response, roles and responsibilities among NS staff are known. Usually Head of Disaster Management takes the lead with the support of technical staff and regional managers for regions concerned by the disaster. SG endorses response strategy.  •	National EOC is managed by the government. NS is a part of the Government EOC structure.  •	GRCS has a contact list with details of relevant HQ and Regional personnel. "

component_details.title: Information Management (IM)
component_details.description: Ability to manage information including requesting, receiving, analyzing and disseminating as per its procedures and partner requirements (IFRC and public authorities in particular). There should be a clear digital/paper trail that documents what, when and how the NS has acted and provides key information for the development of Emergency Plan of Actions. Includes IM between levels, between departments and Situational Reports, mapping, visualisation of data, GO platform (IFRC).

component_responses.notes: "•	Key staff at HQ and branches are familiar with IM templates, methodology and procedures. However, they are not used systematically. •	NS has access to some equipment to compile, visualize and share information at HQ level (e.g., tablets, projectors, laptops etc.), but not at the branches. •	NS has elements of the system to store and share files, however only few staff are storing information on the cloud. Organizational Teams and SharePoint exist, however, not used by all staff consistently. Most of staff prefer to store directly in their devices.  •	There is no centralized space at HQ or Regional level to store documents’ hard copies.  •	Information and decisions are not documented and filed."

component_details.title: Testing and Learning
component_details.description: Drills and Simulations allow the organization to test, identify and learn from the results of these type of exercises and incorporate learning into future preparedness and response planning.

component_responses.notes: "•	Simulation and drills conducted on the base of funds available.  •	Testing of EWEA systems established depends on funds.  •	Lessons learnt exercises conducted systematically and recommendations applied in future operations.  •	GRCS doesn’t conduct cross-border simulations."

component_details.title: Activation of regional and international support
component_details.description: Procedures for requesting and accepting regional and international support in operations, including triggering coordination mechanisms for funding, materials and human resources deployments.

component_responses.notes: "•	Key staff are familiar with the available IFRC/ICRC support, specifically in their sectors of intervention.  •	GRCS has good coordination with the IFRC Cluster and Movement partners.  •	Head of Disaster Management, Health Coordinator and other FPs are trained on emergency response and are aware of when and how to request International Assistance, including sharing SitRep and launching alerts on GO platform.  •	GRCS has worked on DREFs for several responses including, but not limited the most recent Apeate Explosions response. •	NS requests PNS in country for support as well, when disasters happen."

component_details.title: CHEMICAL, BIOLOGICAL, RADIOLOGICAL AND NUCLEAR (CBRN) EMERGENCY PREPAREDNESS

component_responses.notes: "•	DRM Strategy includes Livelihood as one of the areas of focus.  •	Experience in CVA (i.e., vouchers distribution for floods and explosion responses). However, livelihood activities not implemented systematically during responses. •	No focal point identified."

"•	Shelter is a part of areas of focus as per DRM Strategy. •	Collaboration with government agencies and stakeholders for needs assessments. •	Limited HH items (tents) and non-food items prepositioned at the central warehouse to be deployed for major disasters. Prepositioning done with partners support; items are not restocked. •	Selected GRCS volunteers are trained in setting up the family tents. •	GRCS has experience in CVA to cover shelter needs (e.g., 202 houses built by affected population during past floods operation). •	NS doesn’t have dedicated Shelter focal point."

component_details.title: MANAGEMENT OF DEAD BODIES TO FACILITATE THEIR IDENTIFICATION

component_responses.notes: "•	GRCS doesn't have direct engagement in management of dead bodies and SDB (including training, teams and equipment). "

"•	RFL considered as area of focus in the DRM Strategy. •	Support and expertise provided by ICRC, within the framework of the annual agreement. •	Focal point:  - HQ: DM Coordinator  - Region: Regional managers reporting to the DM Coordinator  •	Some volunteers are trained on RFL as well. •	RFL was included during Apeate Explosions operation, and volunteers deployed for it. "

"•	Elements of Transition to recovery role of NS are included to the DRM Strategy. •	GRCS recovery mandate is mentioned in the Act. Every time recovery activities are implemented; coordination needs to be done with NADMO and other relevant authorities. •	Even though NS is mostly focused on emergency response, it had some experience supporting recovery efforts for the communities. For example, during floods in 2018 in Upper East region and Northern region in 2021, GRCS has been engaged in reconstruction and repairing houses activities. This involved distributing vouchers for construction materials. •	NS conducts joint needs assessments with NADMO and other relevant stakeholders when response comes, and then it is determined whether or not longer-term recovery activities will be required and what kind of intervention will have maximum impact on the affected communities. •	NS works to mitigate epidemic-related stigma to enable survivor reintegration into society (e.g., during COVID-19, cholera, EVD). Some health promotion and awareness activities are also done through Mothers clubs in Upper East and Northern regions."

component_details.title: NS-specific areas of intervention
component_details.description: Sector-specific or services provided by the NS in case of emergencies, it is in line with the NS mandate and legislation in country. It includes Community Based DP/DRR, Evacuation, Health in Emergencies, Epidemic and Pandemic, First aid, WASH, Food security and Livelihoods, Search and rRescue, Shelter, Management of dead bodies, RFL, Transition to recovery, and CBRN preparedness.

component_responses.notes: "•	Evacuation is included in NS DRM Strategy as part of detailed operational guidelines. Evacuation happens in collaboration with other stakeholders (e.g., fire department).  •	Unclear whether the NS has appropriate equipment and personnel to perform it. "

"•	First aid is a key area of NS response, but has limited funding (i.e., kits and their replenishment, availability and certification of first aid instructors). •	Knowledge of the NS service by Government and other stakeholders, including communities. •	NS staff and volunteers trained in First Aid available, but refresher sessions and equipment are required. •	First aid is mainstreamed in NS DRR related projects."

"•	WASH is among pillars of DRM strategy, and NS is committed to continue strengthening it.  •	GRCS was engaged in a WASH project with 160 volunteers working on water systems at the community level and social promotion of drinking water (giving people cash vouchers to purchase water). •	NDRTs, regional managers and selected HQ staff are trained on WASH, however, capacities both for staffing and equipment not consistent across the country. •	NS is a part of technical platform for WASH with Government being a lead, however, the participation in coordination meetings is not consistent and not homogeneous across regions."

"•	No experience reported in development of community health contingency plans. District organizers and branches guide response on the base of needs. Competences more developed in projects implementation locations.  •	All Regional Managers are trained in CBHFA including reporting of suspect health events (passive referral). CBHFA currently implemented in 2-3 regions. •	CBHFA linked with health facilities (smaller level) and door to door awareness raising through Mothers’ clubs. "

component_details.title: Coordination with local community level responders
component_details.description: Engagement with Community Disaster Response Teams (CDRTs), through training, coordination, and the development of community disaster preparedness and response plans.

component_responses.notes: "•	NS has procedures to manage information between different levels. Regional Managers along with volunteers on different levels facilitate information sharing from districts, branches and communities to headquarters. However, sometimes this information chain is not followed properly. •	NS decision making is based on the information from the communities collected by community volunteers during community meetings. The meeting notes/reports are submitted to the Regional Manager, but not systematically. •	There are some gaps in the feedback mechanisms in the communities, as well as challenges in getting information in the villages where there are no volunteers."

component_details.title: Cooperation with private sector
component_details.description: Mechanism that allows cooperation with private sector that often plays a strong role in response, particularly if there is impact on their staff and businesses. There is often a willingness to donate goods and services. Advance agreements help to expedite response actions.

component_responses.notes: "•	NS always ensures due diligence in terms of accepting funds, items, goods. Before acceptance, background checks are done, research on website, offices, locations etc.  •	NS ensures appropriate use of emblem (Integrity Policy available), however, there have been some cases of the emblem misuse by some agencies. •	 NS use solely RC community volunteers for activities. Sometimes the Ghana Health Services volunteers are engaged to train RC volunteers.  •	GRCS has partnered with Joy FM, as well as other regional radios, to disseminate COVID health messages.  •	GRCS doesn’t have any official established agreements with private companies. "

component_details.title: Coordination with External Agencies and NGOs
component_details.description: Mechanism that facilitates coordination and collaboration with Non-Governmental Organization (NGO), both local and international NGOs, civil society organizations (CSOs) and United Nations agencies in country.

component_responses.notes: "•	NS has some engagement with the Humanitarian community (UNOCHA, UNICEF etc. as well as other NGOs like Welcome Trust, etc.), including engagement for epidemic risk management. •	GRCS is aware of the IFRC shelter coordination. Often support is sought from IFRC and they receive such supports especially in Tents, Blankets etc. as part of NFIs. •	NS has an open-ended Emergency standing MOU with UNICEF to respond to emergencies (specifically epidemics, for example COVID, measles).  •	Visibility and engagement in coordination meetings within humanitarian. community could be strengthened."

component_details.title: Civil Military Relations
component_details.description: Dialogue and interaction with military actors, essential to protect and promote humanitarian principles, avoid competition, minimize inconsistency and, when appropriate, pursue common goals.

component_responses.notes: "•	GRCS has a working relationship with the Military and sometimes lectures the Military on the ICRC mandate, IHL, Fundamental Principles. •	It was noted that NS could expand its educational engagement with military (for example, by conducting more workshops in the regions). •	ICRC plans to strengthen its Safer access support to NS, especially focusing on high-risk regions.  •	The NS is recognized as one of the first level responders and is granted unrestricted access to communities and freedom of movement."

component_details.title: Coordination with Movement
component_details.description: Mechanisms that facilitate the coordination with ICRC, IFRC, and PNS in-country.

component_responses.notes: "•	GRCS adheres to coordination and cooperation principles and mechanisms are established with IFRC and PNS in-country. Individual Cooperation agreement with IFRC and agreement with Swiss Red Cross exist, but not an overall Movement one.  •	SMCC structure is not in place as a formal mechanism of coordination. Meetings with IFRC, ICRC and PNS are primarily bilateral.  •	The NS is part of a Subregional Westcoast ADMAG network, where information is exchanged between neighboring NSs (mostly focused on DM). •	Iran Red Crescent has a Medical Team in a Hospital in Ghana (Iran Clinic) and medical outreaches are done in a coordinated manner. Official partnership with the Iran Red Crescent is established through 10-year MOU. NS also partners with GHS and MoH on Medical services."

component_details.title: Coordination with authorities
component_details.description: Mechanism that facilitates coordination and cooperation with local and national authorities. It is connected to the NS auxiliary role for humanitarian assistance.

component_responses.notes: "•	GRCS features in the national humanitarian coordination systems and partners with NADMO, MoH (including the National Ambulance Services), Road Safety, Ministry of Interior, Military and Ghana Police. They work hand in hand on activities within the country and are provided with info of RCRC capacities and support required. •	There is an act that has established use of the Emblem (NRCDP 1973). This act has helped the NS gain control on the use of the emblem. The Military and Ambulance have also access to the use of the emblem. However, some bodies or individuals are found guilty of misuse.  •	The NADMO oversees RCCE working group and the NS has a representative that is part of the WG.  •	Engagement with authorities at national and local level to be strengthened for a better positioning of the NS as a leader in certain areas of expertise."

component_details.title: Staff and volunteer management
component_details.description: Well-functioning staff and volunteer management systems and practices allow for effective recruitment, supervision, support and encouragement of staff and volunteers.

component_responses.notes: "•	Responders are deployed and equipped according to ToRs (Volunteer Policy). GRCS is able to effectively activate, deploy and manage branch and national response teams. •	Multiple trainings have been provided to the responders, however, there is no learning paths identified.   •	The Code of Conduct fully highlights the need for staff to comply and act according to standards that have been set out especially related to CEA, Protection, SGBV and clearly defines terms in Endnotes. •	Staff and Volunteers must sign the Code of Conduct before deployment, however, not clear whether it’s systematically reinforced. •	Safety and security risks briefing is provided on needs basis, but not systematic. In IFRC supported operations, volunteers are covered with IFRC insurance. However, the insurance is not available for other operations. •	NS has database of responders; however, it is not centralized, appears outdated and not linked to compensation system. Some regions maintain their own volunteer database, which contains volunteers ID number, contact information and specialty. This could be potentially replicated in other regions. •	NS incorporates response volunteers from relevant sectors to maintain a diverse workforce (reinforced by Volunteer Policy). •	The importance of volunteers' appreciation is highlighted in Volunteers Policy; however, it is not systematically done in practice. •	Some EPC trainings have been provided, along with PPEs during COVID."

component_details.title: Safety and security management
component_details.description: Addresses policy and procedures to ensure the safety of staff and volunteers. This include awareness, effective recruitment, training and management processes in place to ensure that personnel are capable of undertaking the roles demanded of them (from NS operational, management and leaders) according to the Stay Safe (IFRC) and Safer Access (ICRC). Based on safer access framework, including concepts of access, perception, identification and acceptance, and protection and violence prevention.

component_responses.notes: "•	NS has a Security focal point at HQ, who relies on information shared by Regional Managers, however it appears there is no formal safety/security guidelines. Currently the ICRC is in the process of supporting Ghana RC with the Safer Access Framework in selected high-risk locations (for e.g., Northern Branches). •	Some selected staff have completed the IFRC Security trainings on online learning platform. However, most of the managers haven’t done security training, and the overall level of knowledge for safety and security rules and procedures among responders is unclear. •	GRCS analyzes contextual risks, sometimes volunteers are sensitized before they are engaged, but not systematically briefed.  •	Volunteers Policy includes clause on ensuring the provision of assistance and protection for volunteers. However, the application of the Policy is not clear. •	NS has some informal communication mechanisms available for staff and volunteers to report safety and security risks and incidents and to share to share security information.  •	The NS takes epidemic considerations into account and uses information and risk analysis from the Ghana Health Service and Ministry of Health to share with responders. "

component_details.title: Communication in emergencies
component_details.description: Incorporates a system of public messaging to enable the NS to share timely, accurate information before, during, and after a disaster or crisis.

component_responses.notes: "•	GRCS Communications Manager is identified as NS overall Communications focal point and acts as emergencies spokesperson along with the SG. Regional Managers act as Communications focal points for branches in coordination with HQ.  •	NS has a Communication Policy (2018), however, no standard templates for communication are available •	National Society ensures that all information for internal circulation (for members, staff and volunteers working with the National Society) is made accessible and available as needed in the facilitation of its work. •	NS Visibility on social media could be improved.  •	Staff and volunteers need training on the use of social media.  •	There are no specific mechanisms in place to monitor negative media. "

component_details.title: Operations Monitoring, Evaluation, Reporting and Learning
component_details.description: The PMERL is designed to implement a results-based planning, monitoring and evaluation system that provides an evidence base of NS performance, including relevance, efficiency, effectiveness, sustainability and impact. A reliable and trusted organization is accountable, providing transparent and timely information and building systems to strengthen data collection and reporting. It is data-driven, analytical and results-based.

component_responses.notes: "•	NS has one dedicated PMER staff at HQ level with occasional support from volunteers. There are no PMER focal points in the regions. •	Lessons Learned are systematically conducted and findings are used for future response planning. However, evaluations are conducted when funds are available. •	NS has tools and mechanisms to collect, analyze and report on data (e.g. Kobo data collection). Tablets are kept at regional level and sent to the field on the needs basis.  •	There are some gaps in using of electronic systems in the field due to internet coverage. •	NS at HQ level uses appropriate reporting templates/formats according to the agreements with partners.  •	NS also has good general knowledge on IFRC tools and reporting templates.  •	Some elements of monitoring community feedback exist but needs   strengthening. "

component_details.title: Finance and Admin policy and emergency procedures
component_details.description: Overall budgeting, accounting, treasury, assets, financial reporting and financial services operations. it also includes the efficient delivery , cost effective and timely services to the NS. Pre-approved, auditable, expedited procedures that allow for flexibility during a disaster/crisis. These must meet transparency, oversight and accountability standards. Procedures may include faster approval processes, fewer signatures, different authority levels. The Emergency Procedures are activated for a specific period of time.

component_responses.notes: "•	GRCS has just installed automated accounting and financial system (SAGE), which will be rolled out shortly. Not clear whether staff has received training on it. So far NS has been using Excel. •	NS has peacetime financial procedures, which they have used during response. Do not have dedicated emergency financial procedures.  •	NS has Finance and Accounting manual, as well as Integrity policy to facilitate transparency.  •	NS has mechanisms to prevent fraud and corruption (for e.g.  Internal Audit department is in place, as well documents review by the board). •	There is a good knowledge of finance procedures across the NS, however, chain of approvals is not always followed (sometimes volunteers and personnel from the field call HQ directly for approval instead of going through Regional Managers)."

component_details.title: Information and Communication Technology (ICT)
component_details.description: Refers to technologies that provide access to information through telecommunications. This includes the Internet, wireless networks, mobile phones, radios and other communication mediums.

component_responses.notes: "•	No phones are provided for staff at the HQ level, personal phones and sim cards are used. Similar situation is at the branch level, staff use their personal phones. However, there is some ICT tools available at the HQ and regional levels, especially for data collection (for e.g., tablets).  •	Support to communication might be available through project funds only. •	Contact lists with critical numbers exists, but not standardized. It unclear whether all staff have it on their phones. •	WhatsApp is used for emergency communications and messaging by staff, as well as volunteers at the branch level. Relevant personnel share the information. •	No radio systems nor Sat phones are in place. The Generators are available, but only for a few branches.  •	NS has Wi-Fi connection at HQ, phone hotspot is used in the field. Some branches have access to Wifi. •	PMER staff acts as NS IT focal point. Maintenance of the equipment outsourced. "

component_details.title: Resource Mobilisation
component_details.description: A documented strategy for raising domestic funds from the government, private sector, general public and other in-country actors to support the national society’s response. This would include allocation of responsibilities, practical mechanisms for accepting funds and for being accountable on funds.

component_responses.notes: "•	Finance and Resource Mobilization are one of the NS key priorities identified in DRM strategy and other plans. •	GRCS Resource Mobilization Policy (5 year, 2018-2023) exists with primary objective to ensure financial sustainability of NS through diversified resource mobilization efforts. However, it has not been fully used/operationalized. •	Resource Mobilization Strategy refers to establishing Red Cross Business and resource center governed by a management committee. However, currently this hasn’t been done. •	NS has limited capacity for RM in the regions including income generating activities. "

"•	Department composed by 3 staff: Logistics, Warehouse and Transport Officers. No logistics focal points in the regions. Some logistics functions are fulfilled by regional managers (for e.g., local procurement of First Aid kits). •	NS doesn’t have emergency logistic procedures. •	Staff involved in logistics have a clearly defined role in their job descriptions and have received internal and IFRC training, as well as some trainings organized by other stakeholders. However, GRCS logistics capacity still could be improved. •	GRCS key staff are familiar with IFRC logistics services to support NS emergency operations. •	List of service providers available which comply with minimum standards (IFRC and National Procurement authority). There appears to be no framework agreement. In case of an emergency, email sent to all services providers. •	Some pre-positioned relief items are available only in Swiss RC project supported areas (Northern part of the country). For e.g., tents and NFIs in Boga. Some mosquito nets are available at HQ Warehouse."//"•	Currently, the IFRC Status agreement with the Ghana Government has been signed but not endorsed (this means it is still inactive). However, it will provide NS with duty and tax exemptions. Logistics Focal Point is fully aware of this process. •	GRCS uses the IFRC standard catalogue for procurement of items. •	No specific document in place for request of additional relief items. Branches send those type of requests by email copying the relevant FPs.  •	There are no specific procedure/SoPs in place.  •	However, certain confirmations and checks are conducted including quality checks, expiry dates (where applicable).  The FPs for these checks is led by the Logistics but also includes Health, DM focal points and Warehouse Officer."//"•	The Logistics Officer is responsible for procurement and has been trained on processes. There is also support from IFRC procurement unit, especially when it comes to international procurement. •	There is an approved procurement procedure with relevant tools, expertise and templates in place. •	NS has a database of suppliers who comply with IFRC minimum standard requirements. •	There are some MoUs in place to ensure suppliers are able to deliver on time. However, framework agreements only exist with FSPs, Vehicle Service providers and servicing of IT equipment."//"•	NS has a Fleet Manual; however, it appears that not all staff may be familiar with it. •	Although most GRCS branches have at least 1 vehicle, NS doesn’t have sufficient vehicles for response. Sometimes NS hires trucks to carry items with MoUs done before utilization.  •	All NS drivers have valid license and trained in First Aid, however, regular testing and refresher trainings are not provided. •	There are also no emergency procedures for afterhours, and no compensation for drivers. "//"•	GRCS has three warehouses (Accra, Northern Region and Upper East). •	NS warehouse managers use the IFRC stock management manual. Relevant staff are aware of procedures and use of forms.   •	There is a dedicated space to receive items and can be dispatched to affected locations with the trucks owned by the NS (or contracted trucks). However, there pre-positioned stocks availability is very limited. •	No storage spaces in high-risk areas. Sometimes the office spaces are used for that purpose, but most times stocks are sent directly from HQ to field for distribution"

component_details.title: DRM Strategy
component_details.description: An outline of the overall goal that the NS seeks to achieve in its disaster and crisis response operations. The goal considers: context analysis, ongoing/regular all-hazards risk assessments: it may define the target proportion of affected population that will be reached, and a definition of the areas/sectors where a NS will usually respond during an emergency.

component_details.title: DRM Policy
component_details.description: Reflects the NS mission, RCRC principles and mandate. It acknowledges other relevant NS policies, and aligns with the government policy (where applicable), incorporating the general rules that the NS will obey in order to achieve something (i.e mandate, strategy, etc.)

component_details.title: DRM Laws, Advocacy and Dissemination
component_details.description: Designed to support the NS in improving legal preparedness for disasters and crisis and to promote the use of the IDRL Guidelines in order to reduce human vulnerability.

component_responses.notes: Office of the Prime Minister of Saint Vincent and the Grenadines exempted the SVGRCS from import taxes/customs for any incoming humanitarian aid transport in 2013 floods response. Doc 12-DREF

component_details.title: Quality and accountability
component_details.description: Describes the essential elements of principled, accountable, and high-quality humanitarian action. The RCRC Movement provides support to the most vulnerable people in line with the Sphere and CHS standards, Code of Conduct for the RCRC Movement and NGOS in Disaster Relief and the Code for Good Partnership of the RCRC Movement, Gender & Diversity, inclusion and protection, BPI/ Do no harm, context-sensitive analysis, violence prevention, accountability to affected population and disability considerations, Community engagement and accountability (CEA).

component_responses.notes: "The SVGRCS hired a communication officer for three months to ensure that all the affected communities were included in the operational two-way feedback system; the official also focused on the operation’s beneficiary feedback mechanism and its integration with all the sectors, which was intended to guarantee that specific needs linked to gender, age, disability, ethnicity and other factors that increase vulnerability were considered. A complaint mechanism was also put in place, and accountability to beneficiaries was enhanced through the realization of a beneficiary satisfaction survey, which had a sample size of 250 families, and the provision of a feedback mechanism that allowed the affected communities to send feedback to the National Society’s headquarters."

component_details.title: RC auxiliary role, Mandate and Law
component_details.description: A constitutional reference to the role of the NS in responding to disasters and crises, which may be legislated or included/ recognized in the National Response System.

component_details.title: Hazard, Context and Risk Analysis, Monitoring and Early Warning
component_details.description: Describes how the NS monitors and maps past, present and potential hazards, disasters and crises (e.g. hazard, vulnerability assessments, gathering information from communities and government authorities) and systematically evaluates the damage that could be caused by a potential disaster/crisis, the frequency, severity of the impact, and the alert the relevant areas to scale the preparedness actions to reduce population vulnerability.

component_responses.notes: 2014 DM plan highlights focal points and sub-committees

component_details.title: Scenario planning
component_details.description: A set of practical operation plans that closely mirror the generic disaster or crisis response plan but are tailored to a specific hazard type (e.g. earthquake, dengue epidemic, floods, cyclone) and a specific scenario (i.e. number of people affected, their locations and other important factors).

component_details.title: Risk management
component_details.description: A mapping of the potential risks in every area, along with its related mitigation measures. Including financial, reputational, organizational risks etc.

component_responses.notes: when asked questions about documentation most persons seemed unaware if that is done.

component_details.title: Preparedness plans and budgets
component_details.description: Plans identifying organisational resources, determining roles and responsibilities, and developing policies, procedures and activities in order to reach a level of preparedness to be able to respond effectively to a disaster or crisis. Budgets ensure that the necessary financial support is secured to allow capacities to be built and readiness maintained.

component_details.title: Business continuity
component_details.description: A strategy to counter any potential or anticipated obstacles to effective functioning of the NS, with an eye to ensuring that personnel and assets are protected and able to function in the event of a disaster/crisis.

component_details.title: Emergency Response Procedures (SOPs)
component_details.description: Written guidelines that describe duties and rights of personnel, command structures, coordination with other organizations, and reporting requirements, etc. Includes detailed organogram, decision-making flow chart, and defined roles and responsibilities.

component_details.title: Response and recovery planning
component_details.description: A documented set of procedures for the disaster/crisis response and recovery process. Including use of local capacities, transition to recovery, type of activities and serivices provided during response and recovery activities and exit strategies, procedures for DREF & EA, and templates for planning, budgeting and accessing funds.

component_details.title: Pre-disaster meetings and agreements
component_details.description: A commitment to arrange meetings and agreements with Movement stakeholders and external actors to identify, plan for and address gaps for any upcoming disaster season (e.g. monsoon, floods or cyclones, or for any generic disaster/crisis event (e.g Epidemic, pandemic, confilict situations). Pre-disaster agreements should set out each partner's role in the event of a disaster/crisis.

component_responses.notes: A MoU was signed recently before the 2013 floods DREF opereation between the SVGRCS and the CWSA for collaboration with the new water purification unit before and during emergencies. Doc12-DREF
NS volunteers assisted with general collective centre management in 2016 floods response. Doc 11-DREF
Volunteers attended to first aid issues in collective centres during 2016 floods esponse. Doc 11-DREF

NS provides safe water (has EW403D water purification unit).Challenge in 2016 floods: jerrycans were not distributed during the critical phase of the emergency, which meant that when the items finally arrived, the sense of urgency surrounding them had diminished. . Doc 11-DREF
NS assisted food and water distributions in 2016 floods response. Doc 11-DREF

NS supported assessments in 2016 floods response. CDRTs and community volunteers active in 2016 floods response. Lessons Learned: If the community were provided with tools to help themselves, they would respond in a responsible and mature way to bring relief to affected members in the community. Doc 11-DREF

component_details.title: Mapping of NS capacities
component_details.description: A list of the NS capacities including HR (staff, response teams and volunteers) and equipment that are available for disaster/crisis response. Teams could include branch and national response teams. This should be defined by technical speciality where relevant.

component_responses.notes: NS provides PSS support and comfort kits.Challenges in the 2016 floods: Community Health networks for the management of health an WASH  issues were weak and non-existent in some cases; People lacked awareness of the consequences of various public health threats e.g. leptospirosis, Zika and other waterborne diseases. Doc 11-DREF

component_details.title: Early Action Mechanisms
component_details.description: Designed to translate warnings into anticipatory actions to help reduce the impact of specific disaster or crisis events. They focus on consolidating available forecasting information and putting procedures in place to ensure that a NS can act ahead of any disaster/crisis. Forecast-based financing is included within the scope of this area.

component_details.title: Cash Based Intervention (CBI)
component_details.description: An effective and flexible way, including all forms of cash and voucher-based assistance, to support people affected by emergencies, maintaining their dignity and choice, while fostering local economies. Cash should also be mainstreamed into other sectors (including Relief, shelter, livelihoods) and services (Logistics, Finance, etc.)

component_details.title: Emergency Needs Assessment
component_details.description: Assess the extent and impact of the damage caused by the disaster/crisis and the degree of vulnerability of the affected population. The first step in any emergency response, such an assessment will identify the needs that require external intervention and the gaps to be filled. It is a vital component of the programme-planning process.

component_responses.notes: "CDRTs and volunteers formed part of the Red Cross’s damage and needs assessment teams that were deployed to the affected areas immediately following the National Authority’s authorization for the 2016 floods; they were also involved in the continuous assessment process, which included focus group discussions and community consultations. Learnings: Community volunteers were invaluable members of the damage and needs assessment teams; for example, they were able to help the teams locate and access persons in locations that were not familiar to the officials, and they were also critical to the verification of information, which helped to speed up the assessments; The damage and needs assessment process ought to conduct an analysis of the special circumstances of some communities including history, ethnicity, social/economic and cultural aspects; for example, indigenous people constitute more than 80 per cent of the population of Sandy Bay, London, Magum, Overland and Owia.Doc 11-DREF"

component_details.title: Affected population selection
component_details.description: Identification and selection of target Affected population for interventions, using a pre-defined set of criteria based on need and vulnerability. This includes consideration of specific vulnerabilities such as disability, age and gender.

component_responses.notes: "Selection of beneficiaries in 2016 floods DREF response was based on NEMO’s and SVGRC’s damage and needs assessments and selection criteria. In collaboration with NEMO, the SVGRCS used NEMO’s standard questionnaire to conduct the initial needs assessment. Red Cross volunteers and community volunteers were deployed as data collectors, and the continuous needs assessment were conducted through focus group discussions while being sensitive to the gender, ethnicity, disability, health and poverty issues during the discussions. Doc 11-DREF. In 2013 floods, In coordination with the Ministry of Public Health (MoPH) and NEMO, the affected families were registered Four community consultations were done to discuss operations and to evaluate the performance of the operations and to use feedback to improve performance. Doc 11-DREF"

component_details.title: Emergency Operations Centre (EOC)
component_details.description: A central command and control facility responsible for carrying out disaster/crisis management functions at a strategic level in an emergency situation. The common functions are to collect and analyze data; facilitate decision making that protects life and livelihoods; and disseminate those decisions to all concerned agencies and individuals. Generally located at the headquarter level of an organization.

component_details.title: Information Management (IM)
component_details.description: Ability to manage information including requesting, receiving, analyzing and disseminating as per its procedures and partner requirements (IFRC and public authorities in particular). There should be a clear digital/paper trail that documents what, when and how the NS has acted and provides key information for the development of Emergency Plan of Actions. Includes IM between levels, between departments and Situational Reports, mapping, visualisation of data, GO platform (IFRC).

component_details.title: Testing and Learning
component_details.description: Drills and Simulations allow the organization to test, identify and learn from the results of these type of exercises and incorporate learning into future preparedness and response planning.

component_details.title: Activation of regional and international support
component_details.description: Procedures for requesting and accepting regional and international support in operations, including triggering coordination mechanisms for funding, materials and human resources deployments.

component_responses.notes: 3 DREF operations. IFRC DM delegates deployed to coordinate the plan of action with the NS in the 2016 floods DREF response + PIRAC support. Doc 11-DREF. Barbados Red Cross Society donated items in 2013 floods response and  Antigua, Barbuda Red Cross, Jamaica Red Cross, Trinidad and Tobago Red Cross Society and St Kitts and Nevis Red Cross also provided support to the operation by donating items.. Doc 12-DREF

component_details.title: CHEMICAL, BIOLOGICAL, RADIOLOGICAL AND NUCLEAR (CBRN) EMERGENCY PREPAREDNESS

component_responses.notes: NS assisted with general collective centre management and food and water distributions in 2016 floods response. NS has pre-positioned good that were distributed. Doc 11-DREF

component_details.title: MANAGEMENT OF DEAD BODIES TO FACILITATE THEIR IDENTIFICATION
NS-specific areas of intervention
component_details.description: Sector-specific or services provided by the NS in case of emergencies, it is in line with the NS mandate and legislation in country. It includes Community Based DP/DRR, Evacuation, Health in Emergencies, Epidemic and Pandemic, First aid, WASH, Food security and Livelihoods, Search and rRescue, Shelter, Management of dead bodies, RFL, Transition to recovery, and CBRN preparedness.

component_details.title: Coordination with External Agencies and NGOs
component_details.description: Mechanism that facilitates coordination and collaboration with Non-Governmental Organization (NGO), both local and international NGOs, civil society organizations (CSOs) and United Nations agencies in country.

component_responses.notes: "The UNDP offered the National Society some support in 2013 floods response to reach the affected communities that were cut off from the road and OFDA supported by funding three high pressure washing systems in country to support the cleaning campaigns in affected communities. EU monitoring visit of 2013 floods response. Doc 12-DREF"

component_details.title: Civil Military Relations
component_details.description: Dialogue and interaction with military actors, essential to protect and promote humanitarian principles, avoid competition, minimize inconsistency and, when appropriate, pursue common goals.

component_details.title: Coordination with Movement
component_details.description: Mechanisms that facilitate the coordination with ICRC, IFRC, and PNS in-country.

component_responses.notes: IFRC Caribbean Disaster Coordinator/DM delegate and PIRAC assisted development of the 2016 floods response plan of action. CADRIM support lesson learned workshop. Doc 11-DREF

component_details.title: Coordination with authorities
component_details.description: Mechanism that facilitates coordination and cooperation with local and national authorities. It is connected to the NS auxiliary role for humanitarian assistance.

component_responses.notes: NS coordinated with NEMO and MoH in 2016 and 2013 floods DREF responses and the Ministry of Wellness and the Environment and Central Water Sewage Authority (CWSA) throughout the operations. Doc 11-DREF. Collaboration and coordination with non-Red Cross actors worked well during the operation. Doc 12-DREF

component_details.title: Coordination with local community level responders
component_details.description: Engagement with Community Disaster Response Teams (CDRTs), through training, coordination, and the development of community disaster preparedness and response plans.

component_details.title: Cooperation with private sector
component_details.description: Mechanism that allows cooperation with private sector that often plays a strong role in response, particularly if there is impact on their staff and businesses. There is often a willingness to donate goods and services. Advance agreements help to expedite response actions.

component_details.title: Staff and volunteer management
component_details.description: Well-functioning staff and volunteer management systems and practices allow for effective recruitment, supervision, support and encouragement of staff and volunteers.

component_responses.notes: SVG RC has multidisciplinary Community Disaster Response Team (CDRT), 10 RIT trained members, 86 general NIT members and 150 volunteers. Challenge in 2016 floods response:Mobilizing community volunteers to attend workshops in Kingstown due to the volume of work to be attended to in their communities. Do have database/system to manage? Doc 11-DREF

Lastly, the team headed by a CADRIM technical officer conducted an evaluation of the DREF. Doc 11-DREF"

The stock replenishment was done according to the procurement plan, and donations were coordinated to ensure the rotation of the existing stocks to avoid overloading the National Society’s warehouse capacity. The NS has a Contingency Plan which was developed based on one hazard- hurricanes. The RCRC Movement provides support to the most vulnerable people in line with the Sphere and CHS standards, Code of Conduct for the RCRC Movement and NGOS in Disaster Relief and the Code for Good Partnership of the RCRC Movement, Gender & Diversity, inclusion and protection, BPI/ Do no harm, context-sensitive analysis, violence prevention, accountability to affected population and disability considerations, Community engagement and accountability (CEA).

component_details.title: Hazard, Context and Risk Analysis, Monitoring and Early Warning
component_details.description: Describes how the NS monitors and maps past, present and potential hazards, disasters and crises (e.g. hazard, vulnerability assessments, gathering information from communities and government authorities) and systematically evaluates the damage that could be caused by a potential disaster/crisis, the frequency, severity of the impact, and the alert the relevant areas to scale the preparedness actions to reduce population vulnerability.

component_responses.notes: There does not seem to be a formal process for the monitoring of risks by the NS. While there is a general appreciation of the potential risk which potentially prevent the NS from delivering its humanitarian services, this is not done as a formal exercise. here the NS maintains its presence in communities, there is a general appreciation of the risks that confronts that geographical area which is documented through the VCA process; this does not seem to be a widespread practice, however it is something that SVGRCS are working to expand. The NS does not currently possess or manage any warning systems; however, it works in conjunction with NEMO and local actors and supports early warnings to communities through hatsApp, SMS and communication with Red Cross groups & CDRTs.

component_details.title: Scenario planning
component_details.description: A set of practical operation plans that closely mirror the generic disaster or crisis response plan but are tailored to a specific hazard type (e.g. earthquake, dengue epidemic, floods, cyclone) and a specific scenario (i.e. number of people affected, their locations and other important factors).

component_responses.notes:
This was rated as partially exists because the National Society has a drafted Contingency Plan for hurricanes, but there is no analysis of this or any other threat to include secondary ones to facilitate preparations and planning. 

Regarding the epidemic component here, the benchmark was considered as unmet as the NS has not developed specific scenarios neither have they been successful with developing a partnership with the Ministry of Health to undertake developments in this regard.

component_details.title: Risk management
component_details.description: A mapping of the potential risks in every area, along with its related mitigation measures. Including financial, reputational, organizational risks etc.

component_details.title: Preparedness plans and budgets
component_details.description: Plans identifying organisational resources, determining roles and responsibilities, and developing policies, procedures and activities in order to reach a level of preparedness to be able to respond effectively to a disaster or crisis. Budgets ensure that the necessary financial support is secured to allow capacities to be built and readiness maintained.

component_responses.notes: The SVGRCS does not have a designated DM and so all actions that would be undertaken by this role is carried out by the Operations Manager (who was engaged for the La Soufriere operation & was not previously considered a full time position). The NS does not formally audit its preparedness capacity to ascertain gaps nor review its strategy to scale as per its existing capabilities. There are no existing policies and procedures to allocate funds for capacity building for the NS.

component_details.title: Business continuity
component_details.description: A strategy to counter any potential or anticipated obstacles to effective functioning of the NS, with an eye to ensuring that personnel and assets are protected and able to function in the event of a disaster/crisis.

component_details.title: Emergency Response Procedures (SOPs)
component_details.description: Written guidelines that describe duties and rights of personnel, command structures, coordination with other organizations, and reporting requirements, etc. Includes detailed organogram, decision-making flow chart, and defined roles and responsibilities.

component_responses.notes: While the NS has existing procedures, this remains in draft as it have not been approved by the Board formally. All the NS’ sectors of intervention are not covered in keeping with its mandate and it is not immediately clear what are all the roles and responsibilities, and their attendant protocols as would be supported by flow-charts and accompanying narratives. The development of the existing SOPs did not benefit from widespread internal consultations as evidenced by the number of persons who are aware of the document’s existence. In addition, this SOP only reflects their collaboration with the local national disaster office and does not reflect their internal procedures.

component_details.title: Response and recovery planning
component_details.description: A documented set of procedures for the disaster/crisis response and recovery process. Including use of local capacities, transition to recovery, type of activities and serivices provided during response and recovery activities and exit strategies, procedures for DREF & EA, and templates for planning, budgeting and accessing funds.

component_responses.notes: This component was rated as "partially exists" despite the NS’ response with “No” to all benchmarks. This was on the premise that the NS has some institutional capacity to undertake response and recovery planning and have been doing so in collaboration with the Federation. It has accessed DREFs in the past and is currently executing an Appeal for the response to the volcanic eruption. The NS acknowledges its mandate and where it intersects with government and other response and recovery actors. While the NS has a Contingency Plan for hurricanes, it does not have a Response and Recovery Plan detailing how it will transition from response to recovery aligned to its DRM Policy.

component_details.title: Pre-disaster meetings and agreements
component_details.description: A commitment to arrange meetings and agreements with Movement stakeholders and external actors to identify, plan for and address gaps for any upcoming disaster season (e.g. monsoon, floods or cyclones, or for any generic disaster/crisis event (e.g Epidemic, pandemic, confilict situations). Pre-disaster agreements should set out each partner's role in the event of a disaster/crisis.

component_responses.notes: This was rated needs improvement based on a lack of formalised documents such as agreements or memoranda of understanding. The NS has good relationships with the local authorities and suppliers that allow them concessions and expedited services.

The NS has representation across the islands through community groups and  Community Disaster Response Teams (CDRTs). Not all groups are formally trained but provide support in times of emergencies particularly for assessments and distributions. Existing groups operate at various strengths and capacities with some having a governance structure and reporting directly to the headquarters in Kingstown.   

CDRTs, once trained, form part of the national response system and are sometimes “lost” to that system. This has created a disconnect between CDRT and Red Cross groups as they are no longer synonymous.

This component is considered as partially existing as the NS considers this a part of its mandate which is evidenced in its Contingency Plan.  SVGRCS’ supports the authorities with evacuations as per the volcano hazard plan.  It is not known however if this is considered part of the NS’ mandate irrespective of the event. Notwithstanding this however, it is  not fully integrated into the NS' mechanism and supported by the requisite capacity.  

The NS supported the authorities with evacuations for the volcanic eruption and also participates in drills and simulations.

There were positive responses for some of the benchmarks in this component, but the overall rating of the component was “partially exists” as there is no existing health programme. Initiatives are usually carried out through projects, such as the Zika Virus project, which eventually end  and was largely geared towards epidemic prevention and control in communities. While some capacity was built in this area and the NS was provided with tools for data collection, surveillance and reporting to the authorities and the Movement, this was discontinued.  
The NS would also have been involved in COVID-19 responses in partnership with the ministry of health with support from the Federation. Additionally, the NS continues to employ safety measures geared at Infection, Prevention and Control (IPC) for covid-19 transmission prevention. 
The NS also expressed significant interest in expanding this area through the development and commercialisation of an ambulatory service.

SVGRCS strives to expose its staff and volunteers to this sector as much as possible as this is considered part of its mandate. Staff and volunteers will have to refreshed and others newly trained to realise this goal. The NS has a certified master trainer and hopes to revamp and commercialise their First Aid and CPR programme in the future.

The SVGRCS has identified water and sanitation to be further integrated into their response operations. It is not presently one of the sectors with a clearly outlined strategy as per the potential scenarios that the SVGRCS can be faced with and the resulting humanitarian need. At present, the NS stocks jerry-cans for distribution but is aware that it can scale-up as needed through surge support from Movement partners for responses. There is no formal focal point as this is an area that would also be the responsibility of the Operations Manager. There are volunteers who have received training in the sector, however they remain largely inactive.

The NS presently has a Livelihoods Officer who was recruited under the La Soufriere Response Operations. There is no existing policy or strategy which highlights this sector and how the NS intends to treat with it. The NS has coordinated with the authorities in responses and other non-governmental organizations in the past to support communities impacted. Volunteers require additional training in data collection methods and community engagement to undertake work in communities to transition from response to recovery.

component_details.title: MANAGEMENT OF DEAD BODIES TO FACILITATE THEIR IDENTIFICATION
CHEMICAL, BIOLOGICAL, RADIOLOGICAL AND NUCLEAR (CBRN) EMERGENCY PREPAREDNESS

component_responses.notes:
One benchmark was met in this component. There has not been any active engagement of the volunteers trained in this area as this often happens through projects like Zika and in the absence of a health program. This area however remains very important to the NS.  

The NS also executed a Disaster Response Emergency Fund (DREF) in November 2020 in response to a Dengue outbreak.

component_details.title: Mapping of NS capacities
component_details.description: A list of the NS capacities including HR (staff, response teams and volunteers) and equipment that are available for disaster/crisis response. Teams could include branch and national response teams. This should be defined by technical speciality where relevant.

component_responses.notes:
