component_details.title: Quality and accountability
component_details.description: Describes the essential elements of principled, accountable, and high-quality humanitarian action. The RCRC Movement provides support to the most vulnerable people in line with the Sphere and CHS standards, Code of Conduct for the RCRC Movement and NGOS in Disaster Relief and the Code for Good Partnership of the RCRC Movement, Gender & Diversity, inclusion and protection, BPI/ Do no harm, context-sensitive analysis, violence prevention, accountability to affected population and disability considerations, Community engagement and accountability (CEA).

component_details.title: Business continuity
component_details.description: A strategy to counter any potential or anticipated obstacles to effective functioning of the NS, with an eye to ensuring that personnel and assets are protected and able to function in the event of a disaster/crisis.

component_details.title: Emergency Response Procedures (SOPs)
component_details.description: Written guidelines that describe duties and rights of personnel, command structures, coordination with other organizations, and reporting requirements, etc. Includes detailed organogram, decision-making flow chart, and defined roles and responsibilities.

component_details.title: Response and recovery planning
component_details.description: A documented set of procedures for the disaster/crisis response and recovery process. Including use of local capacities, transition to recovery, type of activities and serivices provided during response and recovery activities and exit strategies, procedures for DREF & EA, and templates for planning, budgeting and accessing funds.

component_details.title: Pre-disaster meetings and agreements
component_details.description: A commitment to arrange meetings and agreements with Movement stakeholders and external actors to identify, plan for and address gaps for any upcoming disaster season (e.g. monsoon, floods or cyclones, or for any generic disaster/crisis event (e.g Epidemic, pandemic, confilict situations). Pre-disaster agreements should set out each partner's role in the event of a disaster/crisis.

component_details.title: Hazard, Context and Risk Analysis, Monitoring and Early Warning
component_details.description: Describes how the NS monitors and maps past, present and potential hazards, disasters and crises (e.g. hazard, vulnerability assessments, gathering information from communities and government authorities) and systematically evaluates the damage that could be caused by a potential disaster/crisis, the frequency, severity of the impact, and the alert the relevant areas to scale the preparedness actions to reduce population vulnerability.

component_details.title: Scenario planning
component_details.description: A set of practical operation plans that closely mirror the generic disaster or crisis response plan but are tailored to a specific hazard type (e.g. earthquake, dengue epidemic, floods, cyclone) and a specific scenario (i.e. number of people affected, their locations and other important factors).

component_details.title: Risk management
component_details.description: A mapping of the potential risks in every area, along with its related mitigation measures. Including financial, reputational, organizational risks etc.

component_details.title: Preparedness plans and budgets
component_details.description: Plans identifying organisational resources, determining roles and responsibilities, and developing policies, procedures and activities in order to reach a level of preparedness to be able to respond effectively to a disaster or crisis. Budgets ensure that the necessary financial support is secured to allow capacities to be built and readiness maintained.

component_details.title: Mapping of NS capacities
component_details.description: A list of the NS capacities including HR (staff, response teams and volunteers) and equipment that are available for disaster/crisis response. Teams could include branch and national response teams. This should be defined by technical speciality where relevant.

component_details.title: Early Action Mechanisms
component_details.description: Designed to translate warnings into anticipatory actions to help reduce the impact of specific disaster or crisis events. They focus on consolidating available forecasting information and putting procedures in place to ensure that a NS can act ahead of any disaster/crisis. Forecast-based financing is included within the scope of this area.

component_details.title: Cash Based Intervention (CBI)
component_details.description: An effective and flexible way, including all forms of cash and voucher-based assistance, to support people affected by emergencies, maintaining their dignity and choice, while fostering local economies. Cash should also be mainstreamed into other sectors (including Relief, shelter, livelihoods) and services (Logistics, Finance, etc.)

component_details.title: Emergency Needs Assessment
component_details.description: Assess the extent and impact of the damage caused by the disaster/crisis and the degree of vulnerability of the affected population. The first step in any emergency response, such an assessment will identify the needs that require external intervention and the gaps to be filled. It is a vital component of the programme-planning process.

component_details.title: Affected population selection
component_details.description: Identification and selection of target Affected population for interventions, using a pre-defined set of criteria based on need and vulnerability. This includes consideration of specific vulnerabilities such as disability, age and gender.

component_details.title: Emergency Operations Centre (EOC)
component_details.description: A central command and control facility responsible for carrying out disaster/crisis management functions at a strategic level in an emergency situation. The common functions are to collect and analyze data; facilitate decision making that protects life and livelihoods; and disseminate those decisions to all concerned agencies and individuals. Generally located at the headquarter level of an organization.

component_details.title: Information Management (IM)
component_details.description: Ability to manage information including requesting, receiving, analyzing and disseminating as per its procedures and partner requirements (IFRC and public authorities in particular). There should be a clear digital/paper trail that documents what, when and how the NS has acted and provides key information for the development of Emergency Plan of Actions. Includes IM between levels, between departments and Situational Reports, mapping, visualisation of data, GO platform (IFRC).

component_responses.notes: • Have standardised reports for SitReps (MS Word template). SitReps included affected populations, sectors, recommendations, and profiling of affected populations (e.g. sex-age disaggregate). • They use the SitReps to plan the response and HQ level. Branches fill the SitRep, and email to HQ, but if connectivity not good, can call or text. • Has access to equipment, but sometimes internet not working, or do not have enough ink. • NS have started using QGIS for mapping of current projects running for where Health and DM beneficiaries are located. Not yet being used for response but aspire to. • Shares information to clusters. Sends to the NDMO and they compile with other organisations. • Currently has shared drive to store and share information, but only available at HQ, not accessible to branches. They share information vial email to branches. • During emergency, they would have core group meetings to record decisions, but not backed up. • Information related to beneficiary stored on shared drive. When sharing information (i.e. reports) they aggregate data and remove any confidential information. • Different permissions of the shared drive of information.

component_details.title: Testing and Learning
component_details.description: Drills and Simulations allow the organization to test, identify and learn from the results of these type of exercises and incorporate learning into future preparedness and response planning.

component_details.title: Activation of regional and international support
component_details.description: Procedures for requesting and accepting regional and international support in operations, including triggering coordination mechanisms for funding, materials and human resources deployments.

component_details.description: Sector-specific or services provided by the NS in case of emergencies, it is in line with the NS mandate and legislation in country. It includes Community Based DP/DRR, Evacuation, Health in Emergencies, Epidemic and Pandemic, First aid, WASH, Food security and Livelihoods, Search and rRescue, Shelter, Management of dead bodies, RFL, Transition to recovery, and CBRN preparedness.

component_details.title: Coordination with local community level responders
component_details.description: Engagement with Community Disaster Response Teams (CDRTs), through training, coordination, and the development of community disaster preparedness and response plans.

component_details.title: Cooperation with private sector
component_details.description: Mechanism that allows cooperation with private sector that often plays a strong role in response, particularly if there is impact on their staff and businesses. There is often a willingness to donate goods and services. Advance agreements help to expedite response actions.

component_details.title: Coordination with External Agencies and NGOs
component_details.description: Mechanism that facilitates coordination and collaboration with Non-Governmental Organization (NGO), both local and international NGOs, civil society organizations (CSOs) and United Nations agencies in country.

component_details.title: Civil Military Relations
component_details.description: Dialogue and interaction with military actors, essential to protect and promote humanitarian principles, avoid competition, minimize inconsistency and, when appropriate, pursue common goals.

component_details.title: Coordination with Movement
component_details.description: Mechanisms that facilitate the coordination with ICRC, IFRC, and PNS in-country.

component_details.title: Coordination with authorities
component_details.description: Mechanism that facilitates coordination and cooperation with local and national authorities. It is connected to the NS auxiliary role for humanitarian assistance.

component_details.title: Staff and volunteer management
component_details.description: Well-functioning staff and volunteer management systems and practices allow for effective recruitment, supervision, support and encouragement of staff and volunteers.

component_responses.notes: • For deployment of responders, VRC has visibility items (emblem, vests), insurance. Only partially ID, equipment and PPE for responders. No visual photo ID, with name etc.. • No clear TOR/JD for person being deployed. Team leader has responsibilities, but this is developed and shared ad hoc (sometimes after being deployed). Team 15 leader has specific boundaries and accountability for their tasks, but if they cannot manage, they request support from DRM HQ. Other team members, directed by team leaders on actions – they do not have set objectives defined. • NS responders trained in sectoral areas (e.g. WASH, Shelter, Health), but not in quality accountability (e.g. Community Engagement and Accountability (CEA)) and safety and security. ERT training does however covers sectoral areas and safety and security. • At branch level, P and S branch, have more trainings because they are more at risk to hazards. Other branches less trainings. • Some lists of who and when people are trained (updated after trainings) and includes contact information. Volunteer management database exists, at HQ, but limited access and connection between the different branch databases. • Aspire to send copy of the branch database to HQ and keep copy to themselves. Information not updated throughout entire database. Branch may have different information than HQ. • Procedures to deploy exist within the SOPS and DM Plan, and requires revision/updating. • When HQ requires volunteers, they contact the Branch, and the branch calls the volunteers. • Appears difficult to find right volunteer (based on profile) with existing databases. • Branches can call volunteer from nearby branches. • NS volunteers/staff sign Code of Conduct, Child Protection Policy and complete police clearance, volunteer registration form. • If NS has limited time to induct volunteer, the NS has Induction Video which describes the NS, principles and response standards, if they do not have HR support to induct many people quickly (i.e. spontaneous volunteers). • Some branches and HQ have volunteer rewards/recognition. Not standardised. • Volunteer Unit have plans to scale-up recruitment of volunteers. Currently less than 300 active volunteers. In the Volunteer workplan, are working on developing retention strategies by July 2019 at National-level. At branch-level, they have a plan to engage volunteers that return after inactive period. Branches have some retention strategies, but its not standardised across the NS. • PSS is available and taught to Volunteers on how to deal with communities. First point of contact is field team leader however there is a lack of Self- Care Guide for volunteers and staffs and proper management of PSS internally • Sufficient compensation provided meeting national standard. When volunteers travel they get staff rate, otherwise use 1,500 Vatu per day. • Demoralised when volunteers go to other organisations (e.g. UN) who pay higher per diems. Difficult to retain. But can be compensated in other ways through trainings.

Based on safer access framework, including concepts of access, perception, identification and acceptance, and protection and violence prevention.

component_details.description: Incorporates a system of public messaging to enable the NS to share timely, accurate information before, during, and after a disaster or crisis.

component_details.title: Operations Monitoring, Evaluation, Reporting and Learning
component_details.description: The PMERL is designed to implement a results-based planning, monitoring and evaluation system that provides an evidence base of NS performance, including relevance, efficiency, effectiveness, sustainability and impact. A reliable and trusted organization is accountable, providing transparent and timely information and building systems to strengthen data collection and reporting. It is data-driven, analytical and results-based.

Procedures may include faster approval processes, fewer signatures, different authority levels. The Emergency Procedures are activated for a specific period of time.

1. Fortalecer la Socialización de Herramientas y Procedimientos:

Capacitación Continua: Realizar jornadas periódicas de capacitación para socializar las herramientas, protocolos, procedimientos y políticas existentes, asegurando su comprensión y aplicación a todos los niveles (voluntarios, técnicos, líderes comunitarios, CODEM y CODEL).
Material Didáctico y Guías Simplificadas: Desarrollar materiales de fácil comprensión y guías rápidas para su aplicación en el campo, garantizando el acceso a la información durante emergencias.
2. Integrar el Enfoque de Vulnerabilidad en la Planificación y Respuesta:

Actualización de los PAT (Planes de Acción Temprana): Incluir criterios de vulnerabilidad en los PAT para tormentas y sequías, priorizando las zonas más expuestas y de mayor riesgo.
Movilidad Humana y Migración: Asegurar que el enfoque de movilidad humana y vulnerabilidad sea transversal en los planes de respuesta y en el Plan de Emergencia de Respuesta (PER).
3. Sistematizar la Consolidación y Actualización de Información:

Monitoreo y Análisis de Contextos: Implementar procesos sistemáticos para la recolección, consolidación y análisis de información actualizada, identificando tendencias y riesgos emergentes.
Herramientas de Información Digitalizada: Fortalecer el uso de plataformas digitales para registrar y analizar información en tiempo real, mejorando la toma de decisiones y la planificación anticipatoria.
4. Mejorar la Coordinación Interinstitucional y Difusión de Información:

Espacios de Coordinación Formalizados: Fortalecer la participación en los espacios de coordinación como CODEM y CODEL, integrando información actualizada desde la Cruz Roja Hondureña.
Uso de Tecnologías de Información y Comunicación (TIC): Optimizar la difusión a través de redes sociales, chats comunitarios y plataformas digitales, asegurando información clara, oportuna y accesible.
5. Actualizar y Socializar el Manual de Procedimientos Operativos:

Revisión y Actualización Continua: Modernizar el manual de procedimientos operativos, alineándolo con las nuevas amenazas y prioridades identificadas.
Socialización a Todos los Niveles: Asegurar que el manual actualizado sea ampliamente distribuido y comprendido por todos los actores involucrados, incluyendo personal operativo y voluntarios.
6. Reforzar la Coordinación con la Secretaría de Salud:
Monitoreo de Enfermedades y Alertas Epidemiológicas: Mantener y fortalecer la coordinación para la vigilancia epidemiológica, garantizando la integración de datos en tiempo real y respuestas rápidas.
Estas recomendaciones buscan optimizar los mecanismos de alerta temprana, fortaleciendo la capacidad de respuesta de la Cruz Roja Hondureña para enfrentar emergencias de manera eficiente y coordinada.

component_details.title: Emergency Needs Assessment
component_details.description: Assess the extent and impact of the damage caused by the disaster/crisis and the degree of vulnerability of the affected population. component_responses.notes: La Sociedad Nacional lidera actualmente el Grupo de Trabajo de País de transferencias de efectivo conformado por ONG, Agencias de Naciones Unidas y entes estatales.+P222+L214

component_details.title: Emergency Needs Assessment
component_details.description: Assess the extent and impact of the damage caused by the disaster/crisis and the degree of vulnerability of the affected population. The first step in any emergency response, such an assessment will identify the needs that require external intervention and the gaps to be filled. It is a vital component of the programme-planning process.

component_responses.notes: Se cuenta con personas formadas para evaluaciones detalladas, pero los equipos de evaluación multisectorial y sectorial no estan constituidos oficialmente.

component_details.title: Affected population selection
component_details.description: Identification and selection of target Affected population for interventions, using a pre-defined set of criteria based on need and vulnerability. This includes consideration of specific vulnerabilities such as disability, age and gender.

component_responses.notes: Existe un procedimiento de distribución de ayuda humanitaria que normaliza la selección de beneficiarios mediante criterios, de aceurdo a los diferentes escenarios, es importante institucionalizar herramientas y mecanismos para la protección de datos.

component_details.title: Emergency Operations Centre (EOC)
component_details.description: A central command and control facility responsible for carrying out disaster/crisis management functions at a strategic level in an emergency situation. The common functions are to collect and analyze data; facilitate decision making that protects life and livelihoods; and disseminate those decisions to all concerned agencies and individuals. Generally located at the headquarter level of an organization.

component_responses.notes: "Se pudo evidenciar que existe un manual de procedimiento versión 2013, en las entrevistas se menciono la existencia de un manual actualizado no aprobado y que es solo conocido por el  área de GR. En la entrevista se comento que la activación de COE se realiza a traves de procedimientos, y que el personal realiza periodos operacionales, en el caso de las filiales se pudo observar que el personal no tenia conocimientos sobre la existencia de los  procedimientos, sin embargo en las entrevistas con los voluntarios se constato de que no se establecieron periodos operacionales, si se visualizó la existencia de las area segun la dotrina COE. A nivel central el COE e cuentan con instalaciones que cumplen con los criterios de evaluación, en las filiales se pudo observar que tienen espacios destinados para estas areas, sin embargo cuentan con el equipamiento básico, no se pudo constatar que tengan identificado a nivel central un COE alterno en el caso de colapsar el actual.  Se pudo observar que las decisiones eran canalizadas hacia las áreas responsables, si se observaron algunas discrepancias en las decisiones tomadas, a nivel de filiales se observo que hubo poca priorización de las situaciones presentadas. Si cuentan con sistema de radio comunicación funcionando con cobertura a nivel nacional, no se evidencio que exista  teléfono satelital en el caso de que colapse las redes de radios, se constato que esta en proceso la firma del contrato con la empresa que esta encargadas del mantenimiento preventivo, en las filiales se observo poco uso de la redes de radios existentes(Base, movil y portatil) tienen 8 pares de frecuencias, con 8 repetidoras, ademas de un inventario que es manejado por el departamento de radios y se han realizado formaciones para el personal que opera los radios. Se pudo observar que a nivel de filiales y sede central se hacen uso de herramientas de gestión de información, el personal demuestra competencias."

component_details.title: Information Management (IM)
component_details.description: Ability to manage information including requesting, receiving, analyzing and disseminating as per its procedures and partner requirements (IFRC and public authorities in particular). There should be a clear digital/paper trail that documents what, when and how the NS has acted and provides key information for the development of Emergency Plan of Actions. Includes IM between levels, between departments and Situational Reports, mapping, visualisation of data, GO platform (IFRC).

component_responses.notes: Se cuenta con una plataforma de manejo de información que es alimentada a traves de ODK y visualizada a traves de klipfolio la cual esta siendo programada para ventos programados, pero se esta trabajando actualmente para ser utilizado en evento súbito.   Se evidenció en la sede central el procesamiento de  información, reuniones para presentación de informes, existencia de unidades encargadas del manejo de información, sin embargo a nivel local se observo poco recurso humano con la capacidad para la administración de la información.  Se emitieron los informes de situación en tiempo y forma.

component_details.title: Testing and Learning
component_details.description: Drills and Simulations allow the organization to test, identify and learn from the results of these type of exercises and incorporate learning into future preparedness and response planning.

component_responses.notes: La sociedad nacional realiza periodicamente ejercicios de simulaciones, simulacros, talleres de lecciones aprendidas como parte de su procesos de aprendizajes enfocados en la respuesta, sin embargo la Sociedad Nacional esta actualemnte en un proceso de implantacion del mecanismo de Preparacion basada en Pronostico, el cual debera de incorporarse dentro de estos procesos de aprendizajes.

component_details.title: Activation of regional and international support
component_details.description: Procedures for requesting and accepting regional and international support in operations, including triggering coordination mechanisms for funding, materials and human resources deployments.

component_responses.notes: es importante mantener procesos de socializacion y diseminacion  con actores claves dentro de la Sociedad Nacional. Se puede observar que se dispone de una unidad responsables para la elaboración del Plan Accion, y que este es el resultado de las necesidades presentadas durante el ejercicio . Se emitieron los informes de situación en tiempo y forma.  Se tiene identificado el personal para subir el informe de situación en la plataforma Go, utilizando los procedimiento y plataforma propuestos por la IFRC. Se evidencio capacidad instalada, presencia de la oficina del clúster en el país, el personal clave conoce los procedimientos utilizados por FICR, se participa en una comision que esta  impulsando a traves de una propuesta la firma de un acuerdo para el ingreso rapido de ayuda humanitaria.

component_details.title: CHEMICAL, BIOLOGICAL, RADIOLOGICAL AND NUCLEAR (CBRN) EMERGENCY PREPAREDNESS

component_responses.notes: El tema de Medios de Vida se ha incorporado en la planificación operativa y se realizan acciones a nivel de terreno con los proyectos; en la respuesta a desastre es uno de los sectores prriorizados

component_details.title: MANAGEMENT OF DEAD BODIES TO FACILITATE THEIR IDENTIFICATION

component_responses.notes: Aunque no es un mandato de la Sociedad Nacional se ha indentificado la necesidad y posibilidad de implementar esta línea tematica

Se observa que existe personal con competencias en la Sociedad Nacional para el manejo de RCF, si se observa que esta linea de acción es prioritaria para la sociedad nacional, en el plan de acción presentado en el ejercicio se plantearon actividades a realizar en el plan de acción

component_details.title: NS-specific areas of intervention
component_details.description: Sector-specific or services provided by the NS in case of emergencies, it is in line with the NS mandate and legislation in country. It includes Community Based DP/DRR, Evacuation, Health in Emergencies, Epidemic and Pandemic, First aid, WASH, Food security and Livelihoods, Search and rRescue, Shelter, Management of dead bodies, RFL, Transition to recovery, and CBRN preparedness.

component_responses.notes: La Cruz Roja Hondureña se ha posicionado como un referente de Primeros Auxilios ante la sociedad

En Honduras la maayoría de las emergencias producidas por fenómenos naturales  han estado vinculados a la necesidad de la disponibilidad de agua y saneamiento, por lo cual se considera mejorar la parte del Equipo Logístico y Tècnico, sera necesario el fortalecer los equipos especializados de Agua Saneamiento y Promoción de Higiene.

component_details.title: Coordination with External Agencies and NGOs
component_details.description: Mechanism that facilitates coordination and collaboration with Non-Governmental Organization (NGO), both local and international NGOs, civil society organizations (CSOs) and United Nations agencies in country.

component_responses.notes: Se pudo observar que existen fuertes coordinaciones con las ONG presentes en la zona, con los cuales se realizan actividades de formación, y se rigen a lo establecido por el sistema de protección civil y con los cuales coordina a través de los diferentes niveles Se pudo observar que existen buenas relaciones con el sistema de naciones unidas y que personal de la CRH, participa en las reuniones de REDHUM.

component_details.title: Civil Military Relations
component_details.description: Dialogue and interaction with military actors, essential to protect and promote humanitarian principles, avoid competition, minimize inconsistency and, when appropriate, pursue common goals.

component_responses.notes: Se constato la existencia de buenas relaciones con las instituciones cívicos militares, que estas fueron fortalecidas con los disturbios internos, la SN brinda formaciones ademas de que se coordinan actividades con las fuerzas militares.

component_details.title: Coordination with Movement
component_details.description: Mechanisms that facilitate the coordination with ICRC, IFRC, and PNS in-country.

component_responses.notes: se pudo observar que existe una coordinación con la Unidad de Respuesta de FICR de acuerdos procedimientos existentes, en las operaciones anteriores se ha recibido asistencia internacional y se han hecho la rendicion de cuentas conforme a los requisitos establecidos. Se realizan la firma de memoradum de entendimiento con las PNS, ademas de la existencia de un borrador de una estrategia de cooperación, ademas de la existencia de una versión final pendiente de aprobación por el Comite Ejecutivo de cooperación y realizan periódicamente reuniones con los cooperantes (diferentes PNS) Se evidencio la existencia de acuerdos con PNS, IFCR, para el caso de emergencias, desastres y crisis, ademas de la existencia de un acuerdo de colaboracion entre paises vecinos

component_details.title: Coordination with authorities
component_details.description: Mechanism that facilitates coordination and cooperation with local and national authorities. It is connected to the NS auxiliary role for humanitarian assistance.

component_responses.notes: Se pudo evidenciar que existe buena coordinación con las autoridades publicas, sin embargo el personal entrevistado manifestó no conocer el Plan Nacional de Respuesta, si se observó que existe un intercambio de información durante las emergencias.

component_details.title: Coordination with local community level responders
component_details.description: Engagement with Community Disaster Response Teams (CDRTs), through training, coordination, and the development of community disaster preparedness and response plans.

component_responses.notes: Se observo que existe una conexión con las redes comunitarias a nivel de las filiales sobre todo de las comunidades y barrios mas vulnerables sin embargo las acciones y los vínculos responde a acciones puntuales que realizan los proyectos dentro de sus actividades

component_details.title: Cooperation with private sector
component_details.description: Mechanism that allows cooperation with private sector that often plays a strong role in response, particularly if there is impact on their staff and businesses. There is often a willingness to donate goods and services. Advance agreements help to expedite response actions.

component_responses.notes: Se tienen coordinaciones con la empresa privada durante las emergencias, se tienen ya elaboradores borradores para poder firmar acuerdos con proveedores,

component_details.title: Staff and volunteer management
component_details.description: Well-functioning staff and volunteer management systems and practices allow for effective recruitment, supervision, support and encouragement of staff and volunteers.

component_responses.notes: Durante las entrevistas se pudo evidenciar que se cumplen los criterios de evaluación para seleccionar personal voluntario y permanente contratado Durante las entrevistas se evidenció que la SN cumple con los criterios de identificación y selección de voluntarios. También acuerdos con universidades que están validando la profesionalización los voluntarios. Cuentan con formatos para solicitar permisos a las empresas para que los empleados puedan prestar más horas de servicio en caso de desastres. No se evidenció actividades de apoyo psicosocial para los voluntarios involucrados en la respuesta a la emergencia para la protección de la salud mental.

component_details.title: Safety and security management
component_details.description: Addresses policy and procedures to ensure the safety of staff and volunteers. This include awareness, effective recruitment, training and management processes in place to ensure that personnel are capable of undertaking the roles demanded of them (from NS operational, management and leaders) according to the Stay Safe (IFRC) and Safer Access (ICRC). Based on safer access framework, including concepts of access, perception, identification and acceptance, and protection and violence prevention.

component_responses.notes: Se cuenta con un referente nacional en el tema de seguridad, ademas de contar con una estrategia de seguridad, también se evidencia que existe  personal formado 158 personas, se coordina con recursos humanos ademas de hacer gestiones con seguridad publica para la contratación de personal.

component_details.title: Communication in emergencies
component_details.description: Incorporates a system of public messaging to enable the NS to share timely, accurate information before, during, and after a disaster or crisis.

component_responses.notes: Se evidenció que existe una estrategia de comunicación aprobada en el 2017, pero de acuerdo a la fuente consultada falta incluir algunos componentes. Hay una Red de comunicadores, 30 personas distribuidas en todo el país. Las fuentes entrevistadas dijeron que hay una red de comunicadores de 30 en las cuatro regiones y que continuaran con las capacitaciones. También expresaron que las demás áreas y departamentos de la SN fortalecieran la coordinación con el área de comunicación, sobre todo en eventos programados.

component_details.title: Operations Monitoring, Evaluation, Reporting and Learning
component_details.description: The PMERL is designed to implement a results-based planning, monitoring and evaluation system that provides an evidence base of NS performance, including relevance, efficiency, effectiveness, sustainability and impact. A reliable and trusted organization is accountable, providing transparent and timely information and building systems to strengthen data collection and reporting. It is data-driven, analytical and results-based.

component_responses.notes: Existe una unidad de monitoreo, evaluación y reportes que trabaja en coordinación con los equipos EDAN-PMER. También se observó que han tomado en cuenta los resultados y recomendaciones de otras evaluaciones, diagnósticos y operaciones de respuesta a emergencias. Se evidenció que la SN tiene una comunicación permanente con las instituciones del sistema  Se evidenció en la sede central el procesamiento de  información, reuniones para presentación de informes, existencia de unidades encargadas del manejo de información, sin embargo a nivel local se observo poco recurso humano con la capacidad para la administración de la información. Tambien se observo la utilización de herramientas  de visualización de datos para operativos como semana santa, semana Morazánica, entre otras.

component_details.title: Finance and Admin policy and emergency procedures
component_details.description: Overall budgeting, accounting, treasury, assets, financial reporting and financial services operations. it also includes the efficient delivery , cost effective and timely services to the NS. Pre-approved, auditable, expedited procedures that allow for flexibility during a disaster/crisis. These must meet transparency, oversight and accountability standards. Procedures may include faster approval processes, fewer signatures, different authority levels. The Emergency Procedures are activated for a specific period of time.

component_responses.notes: Se observo que se cuenta con un sistema de auditoria y finanzas que les permite tomar decisiones en el tiempo requerido, ademas de la existencia de una unidad de monitoreo y auditoria

component_details.title: Information and Communication Technology (ICT)
component_details.description: Refers to technologies that provide access to information through telecommunications. This includes the Internet, wireless networks, mobile phones, radios and other communication mediums.

component_responses.notes: Si cuentan con sistema de radio comunicación funcionando con cobertura a nivel nacional, no se evidencio que exista  teléfono satelital en el caso de que colapse las redes de radios, se constato que esta en proceso la firma del contrato con la empresa que esta encargadas del mantenimiento preventivo, en las filiales se observo poco uso de la redes de radios existentes(Base, movil y portatil) tienen 8 pares de frecuencias, con 8 repetidoras, ademas de un inventario que es manejado por el departamento de radios y se han realizado formaciones para el personal que opera los radios.

component_details.title: Resource Mobilisation
component_details.description: A documented strategy for raising domestic funds from the government, private sector, general public and other in-country actors to support the national society’s response. This would include allocation of responsibilities, practical mechanisms for accepting funds and for being accountable on funds.

component_responses.notes: EHay mecanismos pero no hay acuerdos firmados. Tienen 13 planes de negocio y un borrador de guía de responsabilidad social-empresarial. 2 consejos han logrado completar el plan y se les asignará capital. Durante las entrevistas de determinó que la SN cuenta con fondo de emergencias de USD$,5000.00, aproximadamente.

Durante las entrevistas se evidenció que la SN cuenta con procedimientos para compra, sin embargo no cuenta con una lista de proveedores para la adquisición de productos a la hora de una emergencia. Los niveles regionales y locales se adhieren a los procesos de compras implementados por la sede central. También se evidenció que aunque el plan de respuesta no incluye dentro de sus líneas de intervención centros de acopio, en la última emergencia el Consejo de Choluteca lo utilizaron como forma de adquisición de bienes.//Se evidenció que los vehículos cuentan con bitácoras para la realización de mantenimiento cada 5,000 km. Los conductores asignados son sometidos a prueba de manejo interna de la SN. No se cuenta con el mínimo de vehiculos necesarios para el desevolvimiento básico de los Consejos.//La SN cuenta con 5 almacenes, uno en el nivel nacional y uno por cada región. En las entrevistas se evidenció que cuentan con un sistema de control de  los artículos presposicionados en tres de los cinco almacenes, lo que les permite una listeza operacional en caso de un desastre.

component_details.title: RC auxiliary role, Mandate and Law
component_details.description: A constitutional reference to the role of the NS in responding to disasters and crises, which may be legislated or included/ recognized in the National Response System.

component_details.title: DRM Strategy
component_details.description: An outline of the overall goal that the NS seeks to achieve in its disaster and crisis response operations. The goal considers: context analysis, ongoing/regular all-hazards risk assessments: it may define the target proportion of affected population that will be reached, and a definition of the areas/sectors where a NS will usually respond during an emergency.

component_details.title: DRM Policy
component_details.description: Reflects the NS mission, RCRC principles and mandate. It acknowledges other relevant NS policies, and aligns with the government policy (where applicable), incorporating the general rules that the NS will obey in order to achieve something (i.e mandate, strategy, etc.)

component_details.title: DRM Laws, Advocacy and Dissemination
component_details.description: Designed to support the NS in improving legal preparedness for disasters and crisis and to promote the use of the IDRL Guidelines in order to reduce human vulnerability.

component_details.title: Quality and accountability
component_details.description: Describes the essential elements of principled, accountable, and high-quality humanitarian action. The RCRC Movement provides support to the most vulnerable people in line with the Sphere and CHS standards, Code of Conduct for the RCRC Movement and NGOS in Disaster Relief and the Code for Good Partnership of the RCRC Movement, Gender & Diversity, inclusion and protection, BPI/ Do no harm, context-sensitive analysis, violence prevention, accountability to affected population and disability considerations, Community engagement and accountability (CEA).

component_details.title: Hazard, Context and Risk Analysis, Monitoring and Early Warning
component_details.description: Describes how the NS monitors and maps past, present and potential hazards, disasters and crises (e.g. hazard, vulnerability assessments, gathering information from communities and government authorities) and systematically evaluates the damage that could be caused by a potential disaster/crisis, the frequency, severity of the impact, and the alert the relevant areas to scale the preparedness actions to reduce population vulnerability.

component_details.title: Scenario planning
component_details.description: A set of practical operation plans that closely mirror the generic disaster or crisis response plan but are tailored to a specific hazard type (e.g. earthquake, dengue epidemic, floods, cyclone) and a specific scenario (i.e. number of people affected, their locations and other important factors).

component_details.title: Risk management
component_details.description: A mapping of the potential risks in every area, along with its related mitigation measures. Including financial, reputational, organizational risks etc.

component_details.title: Preparedness plans and budgets
component_details.description: Plans identifying organisational resources, determining roles and responsibilities, and developing policies, procedures and activities in order to reach a level of preparedness to be able to respond effectively to a disaster or crisis. Budgets ensure that the necessary financial support is secured to allow capacities to be built and readiness maintained.

component_details.title: Business continuity
component_details.description: A strategy to counter any potential or anticipated obstacles to effective functioning of the NS, with an eye to ensuring that personnel and assets are protected and able to function in the event of a disaster/crisis.

component_details.title: Emergency Response Procedures (SOPs)
component_details.description: Written guidelines that describe duties and rights of personnel, command structures, coordination with other organizations, and reporting requirements, etc. Includes detailed organogram, decision-making flow chart, and defined roles and responsibilities.

component_details.title: Response and recovery planning
component_details.description: A documented set of procedures for the disaster/crisis response and recovery process. Including use of local capacities, transition to recovery, type of activities and serivices provided during response and recovery activities and exit strategies, procedures for DREF & EA, and templates for planning, budgeting and accessing funds.

component_details.title: Pre-disaster meetings and agreements
component_details.description: A commitment to arrange meetings and agreements with Movement stakeholders and external actors to identify, plan for and address gaps for any upcoming disaster season (e.g. monsoon, floods or cyclones, or for any generic disaster/crisis event (e.g Epidemic, pandemic, confilict situations). Pre-disaster agreements should set out each partner's role in the event of a disaster/crisis.

component_details.title: Mapping of NS capacities
component_details.description: A list of the NS capacities including HR (staff, response teams and volunteers) and equipment that are available for disaster/crisis response. Teams could include branch and national response teams. This should be defined by technical speciality where relevant.

component_details.title: Early Action Mechanisms
component_details.description: Designed to translate warnings into anticipatory actions to help reduce the impact of specific disaster or crisis events. They focus on consolidating available forecasting information and putting procedures in place to ensure that a NS can act ahead of any disaster/crisis. Forecast-based financing is included within the scope of this area.

The RCRC Movement provides support to the most vulnerable people in line with the Sphere and CHS standards, Code of Conduct for the RCRC Movement and NGOS in Disaster Relief and the Code for Good Partnership of the RCRC Movement, Gender & Diversity, inclusion and protection, BPI/ Do no harm, context-sensitive analysis, violence prevention, accountability to affected population and disability considerations, Community engagement and accountability (CEA).

component_details.title: RC auxiliary role, Mandate and Law
component_details.description: A constitutional reference to the role of the NS in responding to disasters and crises, which may be legislated or included/ recognized in the National Response System.

component_details.title: Hazard, Context and Risk Analysis, Monitoring and Early Warning
component_details.description: Describes how the NS monitors and maps past, present and potential hazards, disasters and crises (e.g. hazard, vulnerability assessments, gathering information from communities and government authorities) and systematically evaluates the damage that could be caused by a potential disaster/crisis, the frequency, severity of the impact, and the alert the relevant areas to scale the preparedness actions to reduce population vulnerability.

component_details.title: Scenario planning
component_details.description: A set of practical operation plans that closely mirror the generic disaster or crisis response plan but are tailored to a specific hazard type (e.g. earthquake, dengue epidemic, floods, cyclone) and a specific scenario (i.e. number of people affected, their locations and other important factors).

component_details.title: Risk management
component_details.description: A mapping of the potential risks in every area, along with its related mitigation measures. Including financial, reputational, organizational risks etc.

component_details.title: Preparedness plans and budgets
component_details.description: Plans identifying organisational resources, determining roles and responsibilities, and developing policies, procedures and activities in order to reach a level of preparedness to be able to respond effectively to a disaster or crisis. Budgets ensure that the necessary financial support is secured to allow capacities to be built and readiness maintained.

component_details.title: Business continuity
component_details.description: A strategy to counter any potential or anticipated obstacles to effective functioning of the NS, with an eye to ensuring that personnel and assets are protected and able to function in the event of a disaster/crisis.

component_details.title: Emergency Response Procedures (SOPs)
component_details.description: Written guidelines that describe duties and rights of personnel, command structures, coordination with other organizations, and reporting requirements, etc. Includes detailed organogram, decision-making flow chart, and defined roles and responsibilities.

component_details.title: Response and recovery planning
component_details.description: A documented set of procedures for the disaster/crisis response and recovery process. Including use of local capacities, transition to recovery, type of activities and serivices provided during response and recovery activities and exit strategies, procedures for DREF & EA, and templates for planning, budgeting and accessing funds.

component_details.title: Pre-disaster meetings and agreements
component_details.description: A commitment to arrange meetings and agreements with Movement stakeholders and external actors to identify, plan for and address gaps for any upcoming disaster season (e.g. monsoon, floods or cyclones, or for any generic disaster/crisis event (e.g Epidemic, pandemic, confilict situations). Pre-disaster agreements should set out each partner's role in the event of a disaster/crisis.

component_details.title: Mapping of NS capacities
component_details.description: A list of the NS capacities including HR (staff, response teams and volunteers) and equipment that are available for disaster/crisis response. Teams could include branch and national response teams. This should be defined by technical speciality where relevant.

component_details.title: Early Action Mechanisms
component_details.description: Designed to translate warnings into anticipatory actions to help reduce the impact of specific disaster or crisis events. They focus on consolidating available forecasting information and putting procedures in place to ensure that a NS can act ahead of any disaster/crisis. Forecast-based financing is included within the scope of this area.

component_details.title: Cash Based Intervention (CBI)
component_details.description: An effective and flexible way, including all forms of cash and voucher-based assistance, to support people affected by emergencies, maintaining their dignity and choice, while fostering local economies. Cash should also be mainstreamed into other sectors (including Relief, shelter, livelihoods) and services (Logistics, Finance, etc.)

component_details.title: Emergency Needs Assessment
component_details.description: Assess the extent and impact of the damage caused by the disaster/crisis and the degree of vulnerability of the affected population. The first step in any emergency response, such an assessment will identify the needs that require external intervention and the gaps to be filled. It is a vital component of the programme-planning process.

component_details.title: Affected population selection
component_details.description: Identification and selection of target Affected population for interventions, using a pre-defined set of criteria based on need and vulnerability. This includes consideration of specific vulnerabilities such as disability, age and gender.

component_details.title: Emergency Operations Centre (EOC)
component_details.description: A central command and control facility responsible for carrying out disaster/crisis management functions at a strategic level in an emergency situation. The common functions are to collect and analyze data; facilitate decision making that protects life and livelihoods; and disseminate those decisions to all concerned agencies and individuals. Generally located at the headquarter level of an organization.

component_details.title: Information Management (IM)
component_details.description: Ability to manage information including requesting, receiving, analyzing and disseminating as per its procedures and partner requirements (IFRC and public authorities in particular). There should be a clear digital/paper trail that documents what, when and how the NS has acted and provides key information for the development of Emergency Plan of Actions. Includes IM between levels, between departments and Situational Reports, mapping, visualisation of data, GO platform (IFRC).

component_details.title: Testing and Learning
component_details.description: Drills and Simulations allow the organization to test, identify and learn from the results of these type of exercises and incorporate learning into future preparedness and response planning.

component_details.title: Activation of regional and international support
component_details.description: Procedures for requesting and accepting regional and international support in operations, including triggering coordination mechanisms for funding, materials and human resources deployments.

component_details.title: CHEMICAL, BIOLOGICAL, RADIOLOGICAL AND NUCLEAR (CBRN) EMERGENCY PREPAREDNESS
MANAGEMENT OF DEAD BODIES TO FACILITATE THEIR IDENTIFICATION
NS-specific areas of intervention
component_details.description: Sector-specific or services provided by the NS in case of emergencies, it is in line with the NS mandate and legislation in country. It includes Community Based DP/DRR, Evacuation, Health in Emergencies, Epidemic and Pandemic, First aid, WASH, Food security and Livelihoods, Search and rRescue, Shelter, Management of dead bodies, RFL, Transition to recovery, and CBRN preparedness.

component_details.title: Coordination with External Agencies and NGOs
component_details.description: Mechanism that facilitates coordination and collaboration with Non-Governmental Organization (NGO), both local and international NGOs, civil society organizations (CSOs) and United Nations agencies in country.

component_details.title: Civil Military Relations
component_details.description: Dialogue and interaction with military actors, essential to protect and promote humanitarian principles, avoid competition, minimize inconsistency and, when appropriate, pursue common goals.

component_details.title: Coordination with Movement
component_details.description: Mechanisms that facilitate the coordination with ICRC, IFRC, and PNS in-country.

component_details.title: Coordination with authorities
component_details.description: Mechanism that facilitates coordination and cooperation with local and national authorities. It is connected to the NS auxiliary role for humanitarian assistance.

component_details.title: Coordination with local community level responders
component_details.description: Engagement with Community Disaster Response Teams (CDRTs), through training, coordination, and the development of community disaster preparedness and response plans.

component_details.title: Cooperation with private sector
component_details.description: Mechanism that allows cooperation with private sector that often plays a strong role in response, particularly if there is impact on their staff and businesses. There is often a willingness to donate goods and services. Advance agreements help to expedite response actions.

component_details.title: Resource Mobilisation
component_details.description: A documented strategy for raising domestic funds from the government, private sector, general public and other in-country actors to support the national society’s response. This would include allocation of responsibilities, practical mechanisms for accepting funds and for being accountable on funds.

component_details.title: Staff and volunteer management
component_details.description: Well-functioning staff and volunteer management systems and practices allow for effective recruitment, supervision, support and encouragement of staff and volunteers.

component_details.title: Safety and security management
component_details.description: Addresses policy and procedures to ensure the safety of staff and volunteers. This include awareness, effective recruitment, training and management processes in place to ensure that personnel are capable of undertaking the roles demanded of them (from NS operational, management and leaders) according to the Stay Safe (IFRC) and Safer Access (ICRC). Based on safer access framework, including concepts of access, perception, identification and acceptance, and protection and violence prevention.

component_details.title: Communication in emergencies
component_details.description: Incorporates a system of public messaging to enable the NS to share timely, accurate information before, during, and after a disaster or crisis.

component_details.title: Operations Monitoring, Evaluation, Reporting and Learning
component_details.description: The PMERL is designed to implement a results-based planning, monitoring and evaluation system that provides an evidence base of NS performance, including relevance, efficiency, effectiveness, sustainability and impact. A reliable and trusted organization is accountable, providing transparent and timely information and building systems to strengthen data collection and reporting. It is data-driven, analytical and results-based.

component_details.title: Finance and Admin policy and emergency procedures
component_details.description: Overall budgeting, accounting, treasury, assets, financial reporting and financial services operations. it also includes the efficient delivery , cost effective and timely services to the NS. Pre-approved, auditable, expedited procedures that allow for flexibility during a disaster/crisis. These must meet transparency, oversight and accountability standards. Procedures may include faster approval processes, fewer signatures, different authority levels. The Emergency Procedures are activated for a specific period of time.

component_details.title: Information and Communication Technology (ICT)
component_details.description: Refers to technologies that provide access to information through telecommunications. This includes the Internet, wireless networks, mobile phones, radios and other communication mediums.

component_details.title: RC auxiliary role, Mandate and Law
component_details.description: A constitutional reference to the role of the NS in responding to disasters and crises, which may be legislated or included/ recognized in the National Response System.

component_responses.epi_considerations: No

component_details.description: Reflects the NS mission, RCRC principles and mandate.
