Es necesario lograr mayor estandarización y sistematizar el proceso de análisis de contexto desde la Dirección Nacional y las Seccionales. así como la integración de la información comunitaria y multisectorial en el mapeo de riesgos.

Acciones recomendadas: Desarrollar un centro de gestión de la información que permita articular las necesidades de información de las áreas, estandarizar formatos de levantamiento de información así como de sistematización de procesos de intervención en comunidad. Asegurar los recursos para mantener el personal encargado de análisis de datos y manejo de información, con herramientas unificadas para diferentes áreas técnicas.

component_details.title: Scenario planning
component_details.description: A set of practical operation plans that closely mirror the generic disaster or crisis response plan but are tailored to a specific hazard type (e.g. earthquake, dengue epidemic, floods, cyclone) and a specific scenario (i.e. number of people affected, their locations and other important factors).

component_responses.notes:
La SN cuenta con una guía metodológica para la caracterización de escenarios, pero se requiere fortalecer la capacidades para elaborar estos escenarios en las seccionales. Se realizan análisis multisectoriales para identificar los factores determinantes de los riesgos, aunque es necesario mejorar la integración entre los sectores. Existe un formato para el Análisis de Contexto Humanitario en crisis prolongadas y otros escenarios de riesgo, aunque aún no se ha utilizado de manera sistemática.
Los escenarios humanitarios están caracterizados por fenómenos específicos y por territorios de alto riesgo, y se articulan en los planes de contingencia, pero se necesita estandarizar los formatos de los planes para alinearlos con las necesidades de las diferentes áreas misionales.
Es importante mejorar la vinculación de las seccionales en la elaboración de escenarios y planes de contingencias y considerar sus capacidades.
Acciones recomendadas: 
- Se debe incluir en los ejercicios de planificación el componente de Educación en Emergencias. 
- Realizar diagnóstico de necesidades de Seccionales para identificar sus capacidades y necesidades para el análisis y planificación de escenarios, por ejemplo; identificar apoyos técnicos necesarios, conformación de redes de apoyo, entre otros.

component_details.title: Risk management
component_details.description: A mapping of the potential risks in every area, along with its related mitigation measures. Including financial, reputational, organizational risks etc.

component_responses.notes:
La Dirección Nacional cuenta con un equipo especializado en riesgos con diversas áreas como gestión del riesgo de desastres, seguridad operacional, comunicación, jurídica y construcción de paz. Se apoya a las seccionales en la capacitación y asignación de personal calificado. Se dispone de un Sistema Nacional de Seguridad con instrumentos actualizados y una política de administración de riesgos que utiliza matrices para identificar, evaluar y tratar riesgos. Se promueve la colaboración con actores clave y se incorpora el enfoque CEA en los proyectos. La organización tiene políticas y mecanismos para prevenir el fraude y la corrupción, realiza auditorías internas y externas, gestiona incidentes críticos a través de protocolos establecidos y comités de ética y convivencia laboral.
Acciones recomendadas: 
- Estandarizar los mecanismos de rendición de cuentas que permita recoger la percepción de las comunidades sobre los servicios ofertados.
- Mapear y documentar los actores clave por cada una de las áreas misionales para la respectivas rendiciones de cuentas.

component_details.title: Preparedness plans and budgets
component_details.description: Plans identifying organisational resources, determining roles and responsibilities, and developing policies, procedures and activities in order to reach a level of preparedness to be able to respond effectively to a disaster or crisis. Budgets ensure that the necessary financial support is secured to allow capacities to be built and readiness maintained.

component_responses.notes:
El Gestor de Manejo de Desastres y Crisis se coordina con los Directores Seccionales de GR. Se identifican brechas a través de escenarios de riesgo y se registran en PowerBI, y en los talleres de Lecciones Aprendidas. Se cuenta con un fondo de emergencia y estrategias de movilización de recursos. Las acciones de preparación se actualizan y revisan regularmente.

Acciones de mejora: los informes de talleres de lecciones aprendidas deben concretarse con un plan de acción y determinar responsables de seguimiento a estos planes de acción. Así mismo, estos talleres deberían implementarse para todos los proyectos de la institución. 
La SNCRC identifica aumentar el presupuesto del Fondo para priorizar y fortalecer sus líneas de preparación institucional para desastres.
Consolidar una estrategia de preparación para la atención de emergencias y desastres que integre el fortalecimiento a: seccionales, formación continua del voluntariado, procesos innovadores, consecución y gestión de recursos, fortalecimiento al talento humano de la SN y análisis y gestión de datos.
Transferencia de conocimientos (metodologías, herramientas) del orden nacional a las seccionales.

component_details.title: Business continuity
component_details.description: A strategy to counter any potential or anticipated obstacles to effective functioning of the NS, with an eye to ensuring that personnel and assets are protected and able to function in the event of a disaster/crisis.

component_responses.notes:
La SNCRC cuenta con un plan de continuidad de negocio actualizado en octubre del 2023 y acuerdos operativos que incluyen modificadores de crisis.

- A nivel de Seccionales se debe robustecer los procesos que garanticen la continuidad de las actividades esenciales para funcionar en casos de desastre o crisis.

component_details.title: Emergency Response Procedures (SOPs)
component_details.description: Written guidelines that describe duties and rights of personnel, command structures, coordination with other organizations, and reporting requirements, etc. Includes detailed organogram, decision-making flow chart, and defined roles and responsibilities.

component_responses.notes:
La SN cuenta con SOPs actualizados en junio 2024, se debe mejorar su difusión al el personal y voluntariado, así como las herramientas metodológicas y/o procedimientos. Los SOP incorporan procedimientos para todas las fases de la respuesta pero tienen un enfoque para fenómenos de origen natural, incluyen la encala de niveles y organigramas y flujogramas de toma de decisiones.
Acciones de mejora: 
- Se recomienda incorporar a las comunidades desde el enfoque CEA, en la definición de roles y responsabilidades de los SOP.
- Se requieren fortalecer las plantillas para las fases de respuesta con un enfoque para emergencias derivadas del conflicto armado y salud pública y migración.

component_details.title: Response and recovery planning
component_details.description: A documented set of procedures for the disaster/crisis response and recovery process. Including use of local capacities, transition to recovery, type of activities and serivices provided during response and recovery activities and exit strategies, procedures for DREF & EA, and templates for planning, budgeting and accessing funds.

component_responses.notes:
Se cuenta con un Plan de Acción robusto y alineado institucionalmente del que se derivan los Planes de Contingencia e insumos para DREFs y Llamamientos, y que se actualiza con lecciones aprendidas y ejercicios simulados. Existen experiencias positivas sobre la transición hacia la recuperación con apoyos externos o en emergencias recientes para apoyar a comunidades afectadas con transferencias monetarias. Existen procedimientos y Comité de Donaciones para las campañas de movilización de recursos.

Acciones de mejora: En el plan de respuesta es necesario evidenciar la incorporación, visibilización e implementación del enfoque de género y diversidad.
En los planes de recuperación no en todas las áreas se vinculan las partes interesadas. 
Fortalecer las estrategias para involucrar las comunidades en todas las fases de implementación de las intervenciones.

component_details.title: Pre-disaster meetings and agreements
component_details.description: A commitment to arrange meetings and agreements with Movement stakeholders and external actors to identify, plan for and address gaps for any upcoming disaster season (e.g. monsoon, floods or cyclones, or for any generic disaster/crisis event (e.g Epidemic, pandemic, confilict situations). Pre-disaster agreements should set out each partner's role in the event of a disaster/crisis.

component_responses.notes:
Se participa en las reuniones mensuales del Comité Nacional y Municipales de Manejo de Desastres, como se establece en la Ley 1523 de 2012. Participación en el cluster para coordinar y gestionas con actores clave. La firma del Código de Conducta por parte de los contratistas está en proceso de implementación. Existen acuerdos con autoridades para facilitar la importación rápida de ayuda y acuerdos con proveedores estratégicos de bienes y servicios y transferencia en efectivo. En reciente DREF se ha implementado la plataforma Access para transferencias monetarias.
Acción de mejora:
- Los acuerdos con las autoridades para facilitar la importación rápida de suministros, deben actualizarse y fortalecerse para lograr mayor eficiencia.
- Actualizar el Protocolo de Recuperación de la SN, teniendo en cuenta la Estrategia Nacional de Recuperación Resiliente de la UNGRD.

component_details.title: CHEMICAL, BIOLOGICAL, RADIOLOGICAL AND NUCLEAR (CBRN) EMERGENCY PREPAREDNESS

component_responses.notes:
- Realizar capacitación para reconocer e identificar la presencia de materiales peligrosos y las acciones a realizar por la SN.
- Realizar capacitación o actualización periódica en los Protocolos de atención de materiales tecnológicos y biológicos, de manera que se reduzca el riesgo del personal cuando se realice soporte en la atención de este tipo de emergencias.

- Se requiere ampliar a todas las Seccionales la actualización de la hoja de ruta hacia la resiliencia y la metodología AVCA
- Ampliar el conocimiento y aplicación en las Seccionales de la Política de Protección al Abuso y la Explotación Sexual (PEAS) en los procesos de fortalecimiento comunitario en Gestión del Riesgo de Desastres.
- Involucrar la política y el programa de cambio climático en las intervenciones comunitarias en gestión del riesgo.

- Los procedimientos comunitarios de evacuación deben articularse de manera efectiva con los instrumentos de planificación de la respuesta de los Consejos Territoriales de Gestión del Riesgo de Desastres.
- Fortalecer la participación comunitaria en los simulacros de evacuación desarrollados o apoyados por la SN.

- Fortalecer la estructura para la formación de equipos con base comunitaria.
- Seguir capacitando al voluntariado, debido a la alta rotación en las Seccionales.
- Elaborar una guía de manejo de cadáveres con criterios epidemiológicos, técnicos y legales, acorde al mandato de la SN.
- Lograr convenios con empresas para el suministro de elementos e insumos de bioprotección para la Cruz Roja Colombiana.

- La SN continúa en la estructuración de un equipo médico en emergencias tipo 1 fijo (EMT / ERU).
- Incrementar la capacitación de las comunidades en primeros auxilios comunitarios con elementos para primera respuesta.
- Divulgar la "Guía de bolsillo de primeros auxilios psicológicos" 
- Garantiza que en los planes de clase se pueda evaluar a través de simulacros, las competencias de los participantes.
- Intercambio con otras SN para mejorar las metodologías y procesos.

14.21 - Se debe fortalecer actividades en promoción de la higiene, mediante actualizando el material pedagógico e innovar la forma de transmitir los mensajes claves a las comunidades.
14-23- Se sugiere gestionar ser integrantes del WASH HUB, para acceder a los beneficios como pasantías, capacitación y formación, aprendizaje, e intercambio de experiencias 
- Se requiere estandarizar el contenido de los talleres de formación en WASH.
- Se requiere activar la línea de investigación y desarrollo e incorporar nuevas tecnologías, en coordinación el equipo investigador de la SN e intituciones académicas pioneras en innovación relacionada con WASH.

14.25. Se requiere que las seccionales mejoren su capacidad de monitoreo de la seguridad alimentaria en los territorios. (Formatos, guías. check list) que permitan hacer un monitoreo eficiente y continuo.
14.26. Se requiere continuar fortaleciendo capacidad en seccionales para ampliar el equipo técnico que pueda realizar evaluaciones de mercado, y de CASH: (talleres consolidación de redes de apoyo entre Seccionales).

14.32. Se requiere ampliar capacitación en análisis de mercados.
15.36. Se necesita reforzar el rol de la SN en los clústeres (financiación)
14.37. Se necesita ampliar la capacitación en herramientas de recolección de datos y uso de tecnología.

- Se requiere hacer un mapeo de las capacidades de ByR en cada una de las Seccionales a través de un formulario para el registro de la información 
- Se requiere financiamiento para equipos, capacitación entrenamiento, mantenimiento de personal y equipos acorde con la priorización de escenarios de mayor incidencia (Urbano, KSAR y Montaña)
-Analizar y/o explorar las nuevas tecnologías disponibles en el área de búsqueda y rescate.

- La SN cuenta con la Línea de Alojamientos Temporales cuyo enfoque está relacionado principalmente en poder brindar la orientación, la asesoría y acompañamiento en estos procesos y no directamente en la construcción, implementación y coordinación de los mismos.

component_details.title: MANAGEMENT OF DEAD BODIES TO FACILITATE THEIR IDENTIFICATION

component_responses.notes:
- Se requiere la actualización de la Guía de intervención de la Cruz Roja Colombiana en estos escenarios.
- Capacitar al voluntariado y colaboradores en estas guías para fortalecer este proceso.
_ Tener preposicionado Elementos de Protección Personal en caso de que el gobierno requiera nuestro apoyo.

-La SN debe continuar propendiendo por la sostenibilidad del Programa, el cual es fundamental y de alta importancia en el país, ya que las necesidades del contesto lo requieren y es una de las Líneas Misionales establecidas en la respuesta Inmediata de la SN.

-Fortalecer la Estrategia Comunitaria SPAC con la gestión de recursos para la formación de voluntarios y colaboradores.
-Preposicional Kits de Respuesta a nivel comunitario.
-Formación de facilitadores TOT en SPAC teniendo en cuenta la alta rotación de voluntarios.
- Adecuación de la caja de herramientas comunitarias.
-Adecuación de la Metodologia SPAC en Centros Carcelarios y Penitenciarios

component_details.title: Mapping of NS capacities
component_details.description: A list of the NS capacities including HR (staff, response teams and volunteers) and equipment that are available for disaster/crisis response. Teams could include branch and national response teams. This should be defined by technical speciality where relevant.

component_responses.notes:
15.2. - Actualizar la malla curricular y estandarizar los procesos de formación, de los Programas de Gestión del Riesgo de Desastres, Gestión Integral de Salud, Voluntariado.
- Se recomienda que se incluya el componente de Salud Mental y Apoyo Psicosocial, y Genero y Diversidad; teniendo en cuenta la relevancia y acciones que realiza la SN.
- Promover, divulgar y hacer seguimiento a los procesos de formación y retención del voluntariado.
- Desarrollar una hoja de ruta para la mejora de las competencias del voluntariado.
- Aprovechar las nuevas tecnologías para desarrollar programas acorde al contexto y actualidad.
- Diversificar la formación del voluntariado.

15.4. - Realizar un mapeo a las Seccionales para identificar las necesidades de personal, equipos y capacitación; priorizando las Seccionales con mayor necesidad a través de un plan de fortalecimiento.

component_details.title: Early Action Mechanisms
component_details.description: Designed to translate warnings into anticipatory actions to help reduce the impact of specific disaster or crisis events. They focus on consolidating available forecasting information and putting procedures in place to ensure that a NS can act ahead of any disaster/crisis. Forecast-based financing is included within the scope of this area.

component_responses.notes:
16.1. - Validación y aprobación de 3 Planes de Acción Temprana - PAT (Inundación, crisis compleja y dengue), y aprobación del PAT Sequías.
- De acuerdo a posibles eventos que se puedan presentar, formular los DREF Inminente, vinculando en el proceso y de manera participativa a las Seccionales.

16.2. - Se requiere mejorar la forma de acceder oportunamente a la información de las Instituciones Técnicas del Sistema Nacional de Gestión del Riesgo de Desastres - SNGRD y el Instituto Nacional de Salud y el Ministerio de Salud, para la elaboración de los Planes de Acción Temprana PAT. 

16.4. - Se requiere identificar las nuevas tecnologías a implementar de acuerdo a las necesidades, para el envío de mensajes de alerta, que estén relacionadas con la acción temprana, desde el orden nacional y territorial.

16.6.- Hacer un mapeo para identificar las Seccionales que no cuentan con redes locales para informar a las comunidades sobre posibles amenazas, para iniciar un proceso de fortalecimiento (Capacitación, dotación de equipos) en articulación con los Consejos Municipales y Departamentales de Gestión del Riesgo de Desastres.

component_details.title: Cash Based Intervention (CBI)
component_details.description: An effective and flexible way, including all forms of cash and voucher-based assistance, to support people affected by emergencies, maintaining their dignity and choice, while fostering local economies. Cash should also be mainstreamed into other sectors (including Relief, shelter, livelihoods) and services (Logistics, Finance, etc.)

component_responses.notes:
17.1. - Realizar un mapeo de las Seccionales que cuentan con competencias en el Programa de Transferencias Monetarias, para analizar las brechas e implementar un plan de fortalecimiento.
- La SN debe disponer de recursos propios para activar el Programa de Transferencias Monetarias, cuando se requiere; implementando estrategias para la movilización de recursos financieros.

17.9. - Para la SN es importante mantener una participación activa en el Grupo de Transferencias Monetarias.

component_details.title: Emergency Needs Assessment
component_details.description: Assess the extent and impact of the damage caused by the disaster/crisis and the degree of vulnerability of the affected population. The first step in any emergency response, such an assessment will identify the needs that require external intervention and the gaps to be filled. It is a vital component of the programme-planning process.

component_responses.notes:
18.1. Realizar una socialización general a las Seccional para reforzar el conocimiento de los instrumentos de evaluación de emergencia con que cuenta la SN y el SNGRD.
18.2. Fortalecer las capacidades de las Seccionales para el uso de herramientas de tecnologías de la información, para la evaluación de emergencias.
18.7. Tener en cuenta en la formulación de los planes de acción los procesos de autorrecuperación.

component_details.title: Affected population selection
component_details.description: Identification and selection of target Affected population for interventions, using a pre-defined set of criteria based on need and vulnerability. This includes consideration of specific vulnerabilities such as disability, age and gender.

component_responses.notes:
19.2. Socializar en las Seccionales la Política de Género y Diversidad, en las actividades que se desarrollan a través de los proyectos, con participación de los referentes de Gestión y Gobierno; mediante reuniones, Webinar, entre otros.

19.4. Ampliar la cobertura de capacitación y entrenamiento a los voluntarios de las Seccionales, a través de talleres virtuales/presenciales y ejercicios de simulación para la fortalecer el conocimiento de la recopilación de datos.

component_details.title: Emergency Operations Centre (EOC)
component_details.description: A central command and control facility responsible for carrying out disaster/crisis management functions at a strategic level in an emergency situation. The common functions are to collect and analyze data; facilitate decision making that protects life and livelihoods; and disseminate those decisions to all concerned agencies and individuals. Generally located at the headquarter level of an organization.

component_details.title: Information Management (IM)
component_details.description: Ability to manage information including requesting, receiving, analyzing and disseminating as per its procedures and partner requirements (IFRC and public authorities in particular). There should be a clear digital/paper trail that documents what, when and how the NS has acted and provides key information for the development of Emergency Plan of Actions. Includes IM between levels, between departments and Situational Reports, mapping, visualisation of data, GO platform (IFRC).

component_responses.notes: 21.1. Realizar capacitación y entrenamiento a los colaboradores y voluntarios, a través de talleres virtuales/presenciales y ejercicios de simulación en el diligenciamiento de formatos, plantillas y metodologías para la GI.

component_details.title: Testing and Learning
component_details.description: Drills and Simulations allow the organization to test, identify and learn from the results of these type of exercises and incorporate learning into future preparedness and response planning.

component_details.title: Activation of regional and international support
component_details.description: Procedures for requesting and accepting regional and international support in operations, including triggering coordination mechanisms for funding, materials and human resources deployments.

component_responses.notes:
23.1. Fortalecer el conocimiento de las herramientas y los procesos de coordinación a nivel nacional y con las Seccionales.
23.4. Fortalecer el cargue de información al GO, mejorando los procesos de recolección y gestión de la información.

component_details.title: Coordination with External Agencies and NGOs
component_details.description: Mechanism that facilitates coordination and collaboration with Non-Governmental Organization (NGO), both local and international NGOs, civil society organizations (CSOs) and United Nations agencies in country.

component_responses.notes:
La SN posee un dinámico relacionamiento con las agencias de naciones unidas y con algunas ONG del país, permitiendo articulación para intervenciones humanitarias y específicamente con el equipo humanitario país, compartiendo información del contexto humanitario y de seguridad. Adicionalmente, las seccionales a nivel local también interactúan con los equipos regionales de las agencias de naciones unidas y ONG. 
Esto permite aunar esfuerzos para atender las necesidades humanitarias de manera articulada. 

Oportunidad de mejora: 
- Visibilizar el rol de la SN como un aliado estratégico nacional con las agencias de la ONU.
- Se requiere articulación interna para que se fomente la participación en los escenarios en el nivel local, entendiendo el porque de la presencia institucional, para reconocer y atender las necesidades, a partir de la articulación institucional, para potenciar la incidencia.

component_details.title: Civil Military Relations
component_details.description: Dialogue and interaction with military actors, essential to protect and promote humanitarian principles, avoid competition, minimize inconsistency and, when appropriate, pursue common goals.

component_responses.notes:
Respecto a las relaciones cívico militares, la SN establece una articulación con las fuerzas militares para la asistencia humanitaria en su rol de auxiliar del estado, buscando el respeto y aplicabilidad de los principios institucionales y la regulación frente al uso del emblema de la Cruz Roja, respaldados con una normativa internacional y nacional. 

Aspectos de mejora: 
- Mayor difusión frente al alcance del mandato misional y la independencia de la SN en escenarios de situaciones humanitarias.  
- Buscar establecer escenarios para la comprensión sobre el rol auxiliar con las instancias militares.

component_details.title: Coordination with local community level responders
component_details.description: Engagement with Community Disaster Response Teams (CDRTs), through training, coordination, and the development of community disaster preparedness and response plans.

component_responses.notes:
La Cruz Roja cumple un importante rol en la conformación de comités barriales de Emergencia o comités comunitarios de Emergencias, que cumple con las siguientes características:

1. la institución a través de sus seccionales participa en la creación de los equipos de respuesta a nivel comunitario mediante formación, dotación, señalización, documentación, articulación con autoridades locales, etc.
2. Hay mecanismos y procedimientos para la gestión de la información con procesos estructurados y definidos entre las seccionales y la sede mediante reportes, informes mensuales, etc. pero no entre estos comités y las filiales, donde no hay sistematización de este proceso y los procedimientos y mecanismos para la gestión de la información los establece cada seccional.

Aspectos a mejorar:
1. Definir a nivel nacional procedimientos estructuradas para la conformación de comités locales de emergencia haciendo énfasis en establecer mecanismos para la gestión de la información. 
2. Aplicar CEA en emergencias.

component_details.title: Cooperation with private sector
component_details.description: Mechanism that allows cooperation with private sector that often plays a strong role in response, particularly if there is impact on their staff and businesses. There is often a willingness to donate goods and services. Advance agreements help to expedite response actions.

component_responses.notes:
Si, La Sociedad Nacional asegura la debida diligencia al seleccionar socios y aceptar donaciones para mitigar los riesgos de imagen y reputación. adicionalmente hay reglamentación clara respecto al uso del emblema que se refuerza en las diferentes políticas y normatividad institucional, incluyendo manuales de uso del emblema, y reglamentos de personal y voluntariado, acuerdos operativos, etc.
Acciones de mejora:
cuando se contratan servicios de outsourcing mejorar la formación de estas personas para representar a la organización.

component_details.title: Coordination with Movement
component_details.description: Mechanisms that facilitate the coordination with ICRC, IFRC, and PNS in-country.

component_responses.notes:
El acuerdo actual de coordinación y cooperación del movimiento no está actualizado con el acuerdo de Sevilla 2.0, no obstante los mecanismos previstos en la política de cooperación de 2019, crean espacios similares a los propuestos en Sevilla 2.0 permitiendo a los socios del movimiento fortalecer la preparación y respuesta articulada. En el mismo sentido la SN, ha fortalecido los vínculos con las sociedades nacionales vecinas por medio de la cooperación y articulación de acciones humanitarias y fortalecimiento de capacidades.
La SN para formalizar los procesos de cooperación establece documentos formales, tipos, acuerdos o memorandos de entendimiento.

Se describen las acciones para las oportunidad de mejora: 
- Establecer un mecanismos variados y tiempos más ágiles para la formalización de acuerdos o memorandos, específicamente para los proyectos de emergencia. 
- Culminar con la actualización del acuerdo y política de cooperación con base en Sevilla 2.0.
- Asegurar el cumplimiento de lo definido en la política de cooperación.

component_details.title: Coordination with authorities
component_details.description: Mechanism that facilitates coordination and cooperation with local and national authorities. It is connected to the NS auxiliary role for humanitarian assistance.

component_responses.notes:
Hay legislación que propende para el fortalecimiento de los organismos de socorro, no obstante el estado no lo cumple en su totalidad y traslada la responsabilidad a la SN.
Se propone acciones como:
- Socializar el alcance de la SN respecto a su rol auxiliar 
- Socializar la necesidad de fortalecimiento ante las autoridades en los niveles municipal, departamental y nacional  
- Socializar el uso adecuado del emblema con las autoridades 
- Con la entrada en vigencia del Decreto 1314 del 2021, relacionado a la exención de impuestos para los proyectos de cooperación, se requiere mayor agilidad de la agencia presidencial de cooperación para la emisión de certificados de utilidad común, lo cual permitirá reinvertir los costos relacionados a los impuestos en las acciones humanitarias de los proyectos.

component_details.title: DRM Strategy
component_details.description: An outline of the overall goal that the NS seeks to achieve in its disaster and crisis response operations. The goal considers: context analysis, ongoing/regular all-hazards risk assessments: it may define the target proportion of affected population that will be reached, and a definition of the areas/sectors where a NS will usually respond during an emergency.

component_responses.epi_considerations: No
component_responses.notes:
The NS has no DRM strategy that contains a context analysis, trends and success indicators, which includes clear engagement with technical sectors and support services to ensure comprehensive response, and which identifies migration and public health risks, and provides guidance to related interventions. 
There are rather strategic directions that define a general operational objective of responding to 10% of the population. This number was increased to 15% in the DM capacity strengthening plan 2022-2025 (while some branches are not capable yet of meeting the 10%). 
Responses from HQ and branches show that the support brought by LRC to the affected population is based on existing resources.

component_details.title: DRM Policy
component_details.description: Reflects the NS mission, RCRC principles and mandate. It acknowledges other relevant NS policies, and aligns with the government policy (where applicable), incorporating the general rules that the NS will obey in order to achieve something (i.e mandate, strategy, etc.)

component_responses.notes:
There is no DRM policy that sets out guiding principles and values that guide decision-making on the response approach and actions, nor was the IFRC's DRM policy adopted. 
The policy should be inclusive and should involve other relevant sectors and services, especially emphasising on the collaboration between DRM and Health/WASH departments as part of organization-wide approach to response. This is rather found within procedures and the DM enhancement plan. But a more general official documents to which all the others align is needed.

component_details.title: DRM Laws, Advocacy and Dissemination
component_details.description: Designed to support the NS in improving legal preparedness for disasters and crisis and to promote the use of the IDRL Guidelines in order to reduce human vulnerability.

component_responses.epi_considerations: No
component_responses.notes:
The NS has no active IDRL plan nor contributes to national adherence to International Health Regulations.
The RC law does not exempt the NS from customs or taxes on the imported relief items.
The migration department, being the oldest in the NS, coordinates with UNHCR, ICRC and IFRC locally and internationally on IHL. The NS is an implementing partner of UNHCR locally, ensuring activities are done according to UNHCR’s mandate in relation to refugees.

component_details.title: Quality and accountability
component_details.description: Describes the essential elements of principled, accountable, and high-quality humanitarian action. The RCRC Movement provides support to the most vulnerable people in line with the Sphere and CHS standards, Code of Conduct for the RCRC Movement and NGOS in Disaster Relief and the Code for Good Partnership of the RCRC Movement, Gender & Diversity, inclusion and protection, BPI/ Do no harm, context-sensitive analysis, violence prevention, accountability to affected population and disability considerations, Community engagement and accountability (CEA).

component_responses.epi_considerations: No
component_responses.notes:
There is a new CEA focal point at HQ but no counterparts in branches. There is no CEA plan, templates or procedures. 
The response plan is usually prepared by HQ and sent to branches. Therefore, for the last 3 crises, the affected population was not included in the response planning however the plan was based on their needs (needs questionnaire). Nevertheless, longer-term response included meetings to listen to the needs of the refugees in communities. For migration crises, the NS considers the language of migrants. 
There is no safe and accessible feedback and complaints mechanism to record, refer or respond, and monitor communities' concerns and requests regarding the assistance provided or protection issues. Some branches mentioned a review book where people could write things. In some branches, the written information was used, in others it wasn’t. 
The HQ and several branches adhere to protection policies. PGI policies will be widely spread through a program with the CRC. There is no system to adhere to Sphere standards and IASC guidelines on integrating gender-based violence interventions and including persons with disabilities.
During outbreaks, the NS is not prepared to identify communication gaps, communicate risks health promotion messages, track rumours and ensure NS acceptance and access. No clinical quality standards are adhered to (e.g., WHO, IFRC, MoH). 
Implications: 
Risks on the quality of service, the safety of the affected population and the accountability of LRC are high.

component_details.title: RC auxiliary role, Mandate and Law
component_details.description: A constitutional reference to the role of the NS in responding to disasters and crises, which may be legislated or included/ recognized in the National Response System.

component_responses.epi_considerations: No
component_responses.notes:
LRC has defined its role through an LRC Law. 12 activities of the Red Cross are listed, they also include the main function of LRC in responding to migration and displacement crises, however not its role in epidemics. The mandate is reflected in NS formal documents and is known by leadership and directors. 
At the national level, staff might be aware of LRC’s main role, however the authorities don’t understand this function as a mandate from the Government for the LRC to accomplish an auxiliary role in relation to the humanitarian field. 
Locally, branches know part of the mandate. Volunteers seam to focus more on the Registration Centers which they have been involved in. Branches must regularly take contact with municipalities to inform them on the LRC role. Due to the lack of understanding of the auxiliary role nationally, there is no advocacy across authorities’ levels on the collaboration with LRC for humanitarian crises. 
The national and local response plans developed by the LRC can facilitate the involvement of LRC with authorities but don’t cover the understanding of the auxiliary role that the NS has the potential to achieve. 
The LRC law defines the use of the emblem. It gives protection power to the military and religious personnel. This is a breach of the Fundamental Principles and can be a risk to RCRC teams in-country.  
The NS promotes IHL upon need, but not in a systematic way, nor observes compliance.

component_details.title: Hazard, Context and Risk Analysis, Monitoring and Early Warning
component_details.description: Describes how the NS monitors and maps past, present and potential hazards, disasters and crises (e.g. hazard, vulnerability assessments, gathering information from communities and government authorities) and systematically evaluates the damage that could be caused by a potential disaster/crisis, the frequency, severity of the impact, and the alert the relevant areas to scale the preparedness actions to reduce population vulnerability.

component_responses.epi_considerations: No
component_responses.notes: LRC branches don’t have a proper system to monitor risks; they just observe hazards when they happen. Nationally, there is no monitoring system, even for important risks like migration. The LRC doesn't coordinate with neighboring National Societies for migration or displacement, and there's no system for monitoring epidemics with neighboring countries. The lack of collaboration and monitoring means they are not familiar with each other's capabilities and vulnerabilities. While they have a three-year Disaster Management plan, it seems their approach is more reactive, starting data collection and analysis after a disaster has occurred.

component_details.title: Scenario planning
component_details.description: A set of practical operation plans that closely mirror the generic disaster or crisis response plan but are tailored to a specific hazard type (e.g. earthquake, dengue epidemic, floods, cyclone) and a specific scenario (i.e. number of people affected, their locations and other important factors).

component_responses.notes: The LRCs Scenario Planning capacity appears to be limited based on the provided information. Some teams, like the Migration team, have a general understanding of scenario, but the NS has no ready scenarios. Branches rely on instructions from HQ. There are some procedures for local and national responses, but the organization lacks contingency plans and a clear activation plan for responses.

component_details.title: Risk management
component_details.description: A mapping of the potential risks in every area, along with its related mitigation measures. Including financial, reputational, organizational risks etc.

component_responses.epi_considerations: No
component_responses.notes:
"While there is no systematic risk assessment in place, a previous risk analysis identified multiple risks, leading to a net risk rating of ""Major"" due to significant impacts and likelihood. 
The overall risk rating of ""major"" suggests uncertainties in achieving objectives, with the governance framework providing limited assurance. The Lithuania Red Cross faces challenges in advocating for and taking action on migration due to legal complications. Specifically, conflicts between local laws and international standards limits the organization's efforts in this area. The LRCs minimal engagement with host and migrant communities reveals a gap in proactive risk identification. The absence of standardized procedures during risk incidents indicates a need for a more cohesive risk management approach. The 2022 risk assessment underscores the urgency for the LRC to establish clearer board guidance, systematic risk assessment processes, and improved community engagement strategies for effective risk management, especially in the context of migration.

component_details.title: Preparedness plans and budgets
component_details.description: Plans identifying organisational resources, determining roles and responsibilities, and developing policies, procedures and activities in order to reach a level of preparedness to be able to respond effectively to a disaster or crisis. Budgets ensure that the necessary financial support is secured to allow capacities to be built and readiness maintained.

component_responses.epi_considerations: No
component_responses.notes:
No preparedness plans exist. Also little cooperation happens between teams, especially between migration and disaster management.
Specifically for migration, there's no analysis and plans considering entry, exit, or settlement points for migrants, and there are no measures to support host communities and prevent tensions. The decision-making process is centralised at the HQ, with branches having no authority in resource mobilization.

component_details.title: Business continuity
component_details.description: A strategy to counter any potential or anticipated obstacles to effective functioning of the NS, with an eye to ensuring that personnel and assets are protected and able to function in the event of a disaster/crisis.

component_responses.epi_considerations: No
component_responses.notes: Some teams say there is a business continuity plan that takes migration and displacement into account, aligning with the recognition of these factors as major risks. However, there appears to be a lack of concrete evidence or documentation for an approved business continuity plan specifically tailored for major emergency or crisis situations that could impact operations. However, some branches mention the ability to operate from home, and national response SOPs mentions the SG’s house as a meeting point in case of lack of communication, which indicates some level of flexibility and contingency.

component_details.title: Emergency Response Procedures (SOPs)
component_details.description: Written guidelines that describe duties and rights of personnel, command structures, coordination with other organizations, and reporting requirements, etc. Includes detailed organogram, decision-making flow chart, and defined roles and responsibilities.

component_responses.epi_considerations: No
component_responses.notes: During the Ukraine crisis, SOPs were absent, leading branches to rely on instructions from HQ. However, presently, there are SOPs for general local actions with municipalities, but they lack detailed guidance on specific areas of intervention, especially for migration scenarios. While SOPs have been disseminated to branches, the local response SOPs only outline roles for the municipality, branch coordinator, and branch head, with the latter being a member of the EOC. The DM organizational diagram illustrates the involvement in strategic and operational decisions. National response SOPs provide more comprehensive details on roles and responsibilities. Notably, SOPs cover the initiation and conclusion of emergency responses but do not mention early action or a specific plan.

component_details.title: Response and recovery planning
component_details.description: A documented set of procedures for the disaster/crisis response and recovery process. Including use of local capacities, transition to recovery, type of activities and serivices provided during response and recovery activities and exit strategies, procedures for DREF & EA, and templates for planning, budgeting and accessing funds.

component_responses.epi_considerations: No
component_responses.notes: According to their Response SOPs, plans are created after disasters and needs are assessed. However, branches report a lack of an up to date, approved multi-sectoral response plan for efficient resource use. While instructions and training were received for the Ukraine crisis, they came when the disaster occurred, not beforehand. Branches express a need for response plans that consider vulnerabilities and expressed needs of men and women, as current assistance meets commitments but lacks a formal plan. Relief planning lacks a systematic approach based on assessed risks and vulnerabilities, and some branches note a discrepancy between formal plans and actual decision-making processes. The response plans for Ukraine are targeted and prioritize based on vulnerability, but the planning is reported to occur only when a disaster hits and does not adequately include communities and branches in the process.

component_details.title: Pre-disaster meetings and agreements
component_details.description: A commitment to arrange meetings and agreements with Movement stakeholders and external actors to identify, plan for and address gaps for any upcoming disaster season (e.g. monsoon, floods or cyclones, or for any generic disaster/crisis event (e.g Epidemic, pandemic, confilict situations). Pre-disaster agreements should set out each partner's role in the event of a disaster/crisis.

component_responses.notes:
There are no systematic pre-disaster meetings that happen with authorities nationally or locally, nor with disaster response actors. There are agreements with the Government, local authorities, other NGOs and business partners that seam to be well-known by related staff. 
LRC don't have active Movement partners in-country and thus no partners' capacity mapping. 
No information about Movement coordination agreements which are also shared with IFRC. 
Contractors do not sign the code of conduct. There are no agreements with public authorities to facilitate expedited import of humanitarian aid and visas for incoming personnel.

component_details.title: Cash Based Intervention (CBI)
component_details.description: An effective and flexible way, including all forms of cash and voucher-based assistance, to support people affected by emergencies, maintaining their dignity and choice, while fostering local economies. Cash should also be mainstreamed into other sectors (including Relief, shelter, livelihoods) and services (Logistics, Finance, etc.)

component_responses.epi_considerations: No
component_responses.notes:
The LRC Headquarters departments says that the LRC has a CBI preparedness plan, maintains an up-to-date database of trained and experienced staff in CBI, and regularly revises its CBI SOP. 
The unified plan highlights LRC's provision of CVA support to refugees, displaced people from Ukraine, and migrants in irregular situations released from detention. 
There is a CVA focal point and LRC collaborates with Red Rose to provide cash assistance to the most vulnerable Ukrainian population in Lithuania. 
The Multi-year high-level objectives of the National Society include improving the implementation of CVA activities, particularly in supporting migrants and people on the move, through localization and cash preparedness, although specific CBI strategies and plans are not mentioned in other shared documents by the NS.

component_details.title: Emergency Needs Assessment
component_details.description: Assess the extent and impact of the damage caused by the disaster/crisis and the degree of vulnerability of the affected population. The first step in any emergency response, such an assessment will identify the needs that require external intervention and the gaps to be filled. It is a vital component of the programme-planning process.

component_responses.notes:
There is no detailed needs assessment form. The LRC creates one for every emergency. A standard one is being created now (2023).
Migration team says, needs assessment considers language, how migrants can participate, legal status and nationality, yet there is no mention of a PGI component. 
There are different practices and different levels of evaluation processes regarding the presence of trained volunteers for needs assessment among branches.
Emergency plans are formulated after the collection of needs, aligning with the guidelines outlined in the national response SOPs. 
Some branches actively participate in collaborative efforts with other NGOs and access a shared database, leading to referrals based on a common foundation.

component_details.title: Affected population selection
component_details.description: Identification and selection of target Affected population for interventions, using a pre-defined set of criteria based on need and vulnerability. This includes consideration of specific vulnerabilities such as disability, age and gender.

component_responses.notes:
The LRC shows a commitment to clear and inclusive communication during the selection process. However, the responses reveal differences in how selection criteria are put into practice.
In the Ukraine crisis, LRC aimed to help all displaced people without specific criteria. They set clear rules for cash vouchers but found it challenging to reach the right people, so they used different channels. Some branches consider people with disabilities, but it's unclear how they decide. In the Ukraine operation, there were clearer criteria for the CVA program, but branches may lack capacity, relying on HQ criteria. The NS follows national data protection rules.

component_details.title: Emergency Operations Centre (EOC)
component_details.description: A central command and control facility responsible for carrying out disaster/crisis management functions at a strategic level in an emergency situation. The common functions are to collect and analyze data; facilitate decision making that protects life and livelihoods; and disseminate those decisions to all concerned agencies and individuals. Generally located at the headquarter level of an organization.

component_responses.notes:
The LRC has set up an EOC with the DM leading at the national level and the SG at the government's EOC. The EOC team includes heads of various departments and support staff for a comprehensive approach. However, guidelines for responding to specific hazards, like migration, are missing from local and national response plans. 
Communication about EOC activation, volunteer mobilization, and roles is channeled through unit heads, leaving branches waiting for HQ instructions. Local response plans allow collaboration with municipalities during local events. Role of migration teams are not clear. 
There is an equipped EOC at the HQ and alternative EOC and some branches say they have an EOC. EOC organigramme exists. SG is part of the national EOC and branches' managers of the municipalities' EOC. The National response plans offer flexibility in working hours during emergencies.

component_details.title: Information Management (IM)
component_details.description: Ability to manage information including requesting, receiving, analyzing and disseminating as per its procedures and partner requirements (IFRC and public authorities in particular). There should be a clear digital/paper trail that documents what, when and how the NS has acted and provides key information for the development of Emergency Plan of Actions. Includes IM between levels, between departments and Situational Reports, mapping, visualisation of data, GO platform (IFRC).

component_responses.notes:
There are no specific templates or procedures for IM. Some branches experienced equipment shortages during the Ukraine crisis, although most of the branches have basic devices like computers and tablets. 
There is no organized system to store and share files with emergency personnel, relying on informal methods like phones and social media.
It is unclear if the LRC has updated data on high-risk areas categorized by age, gender, and disability. There is no clear format for SitReps, and information from collaborations with other groups lacks a structured framework. The LRC has limited collaboration sharing information with neighboring NSs.

component_details.title: Testing and Learning
component_details.description: Drills and Simulations allow the organization to test, identify and learn from the results of these type of exercises and incorporate learning into future preparedness and response planning.

component_responses.notes:
Some branches acknowledge the existence of simulations and drills, others report their absence.
Notably, there have been multiple simulation exercises (Simex) focusing on evacuation readiness and CBRN scenarios. Scenarios are generally crafted by the Government and local authorities, therefore, the NS does not test critical aspects of its own work like access, acceptance, etc. 
The involvement in a multi-country evacuation project with neighboring NS can lead to a coordinated cross-border evacuation response plan.
Lessons drawn from simulations are mostly known by people who have taken part in them. There is no information on a way to systematically save learnings. There are no plans and procedures that those learning can adapt once collected.

component_details.title: Activation of regional and international support
component_details.description: Procedures for requesting and accepting regional and international support in operations, including triggering coordination mechanisms for funding, materials and human resources deployments.

component_responses.notes: Key staff are familiarized with the support available, but no comprehensive communication schemes are in place to make sure they are truly aware and systematically updated. The contacts with respective IFRC offices are established and communication channels are preserved, but specific SOP’s are absent. IFRC emergency funding mechanisms have been successfully engaged and used. No specific arrangements or plans exist concerning NS response to epidemic or environmental situations.

component_responses.epi_considerations: No
component_responses.notes:
Alytus: first aid, water and sanitation, food security, search and rescue, shelter, restoration of family links 
Elektrenai: Humanitarian aid, first psychological assistance, assistance in things, diversion and escort assistance.
Kaunas: that is based on LRC guidance
Klaipeda: DREF??? Water and sanitation, food security (if we have supplies), pes search and rescue, restoration of family ties – by directing to a targeted specialist, registration centers, transition to restoration, first aid is provided by the community.

component_responses.epi_considerations: No
component_responses.notes:
The provided information does not contain specific details regarding the National Society's performance in terms of evacuation as part of its response strategy. The response ""High Performance"" is too broad and lacks specific details about the NS's preparedness regarding evacuation in different scenarios. For a comprehensive assessment, specific information about the NS's plans, protocols, and capacities related to evacuation would be necessary. Without such details, it is challenging to provide a thorough analysis of the National Society's performance in this specific benchmark.
The National Society has some mechanisms in place for the evacuation of communities in high-risk areas, but there is room for improvement in terms of preparedness. While the acknowledgment of existing mechanisms is positive, the mention that it could be strengthened indicates that there may be areas of vulnerability or gaps in the current evacuation plans. To enhance their preparedness, the National Society should consider identifying and addressing these weaknesses, potentially through training, simulation exercises, and collaboration with relevant stakeholders. Continuous improvement and strengthening of evacuation procedures are essential to ensuring the safety and resilience of communities in high-risk areas.
There is no information about health emergencies, but it is stated that all personnel of LRC branches have protective equipment, vests and t-shirts.

The LRC Statute states that the NS act as an auxiliary of the state in mobilising trained volunteers, citizens and other organisations to provide first aid, psychosocial or other assistance in times of emergencies. It is also mentioned under National Respoonse Plan that,  LRC performs various tasks, including providing first aid, participating in rescue and evacuation operations, humanitarian and logistics activities, etc.
LRC has some WASH related activities (distriubutions of hygine kits) in the past but it is not mentioned in any policy as a  NS roles and responsibilities.

component_responses.epi_considerations: No
component_responses.notes: There is no DRM policy or identified nationaly policy that incorporated livelihoods. However CEA team acknowledges existing plans related to livelihoods, but these have not been reviewed or strengthened. Recognizing and enhancing these plans is crucial for integrating livelihood considerations into comprehensive DRM strategies.

According to the DM plan, the LRC has established national-level relations with the Fire and Rescue Department. Furthermore, the National Response Plan outlines the Emergency Response Coordination Team's duties, which encompass various tasks, including providing first aid and participating in rescue and evacuation operations. However this needs to be elaborated more under DRM policy.

There is currently no established mechanism for consulting the target population on the most suitable shelter response solutions. The Logistics team has highlighted an issue with stock capacity, noting a lack of standardized items. Furthermore, there are no Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) for standard Non-Food Item (NFI) kits, and no identified supplier list is in place. The Shelter team indicates that, considering the country's context, their planning focuses solely on the operation and accommodation of evacuation centers under roofs, neglecting temporary shelter solutions. Volunteers lack training on the utilization of prepositioned shelter materials. Despite having a Community-Based Approach (CVA) tested for foreigners, the Shelter team has yet to utilize it to address the needs of the local population.

component_details.title: MANAGEMENT OF DEAD BODIES TO FACILITATE THEIR IDENTIFICATION

component_responses.notes: The management of dead bodies to facilitate their identification is not part of LRCs response strategy.

The LRC has RFL services, which include a trained coordinator and data manager. However, they have lack of integration into the broader Emergency Preparedness program. Staff and volunteers within the Emergency Preparedness program lack adequate training in RFL processes. In addition, the necessary equipment to be used in RFL systems is also available at LRC. The plan to involve volunteers in providing RFL services has been halted due to access issues. The LRC has entered into an agreement with the ICRC valid from January 2023 to December 2024. This agreement ensures full support, encompassing PSS training and technical assistance, in alignment with the specified terms of the contract.

Key staff members demonstrate familiarity with essential principles, although they understand the key principles, they haven't fully connected them to the recovery aspect. The analysis reveals a need to enhance resilience throughout the response. According to the Recovery team, due to the Lithuanian geographical context, public authorities do not allocate significant attention to the recovery topic. Sectorial or cluster interventions remain uncommon both at the national level and within the LRC.  Additionally, collaboration with institutions to coordinate long-term recovery is part of National Response plan.

component_details.title: CHEMICAL, BIOLOGICAL, RADIOLOGICAL AND NUCLEAR (CBRN) EMERGENCY PREPAREDNESS

component_responses.notes: The existence of a MoUs between the LRC and three Ministries implies that the LRC has a designated role in responding to nuclear emergencies. Nevertheless, it's noteworthy that this role is not explicitly outlined in any documented agreement or official record.

As outlined in the LRC DM plan, all LRC staff and disaster volunteers undergo first aid training. Additionally, community training in health and first aid activities is conducted. Moreover, the LRC Statute specifies that the NS acts as an auxiliary of the state in mobilizing trained volunteers, citizens, and other organizations to deliver first aid, psychosocial support, or other assistance during emergencies. The National Response Plan further details that the LRC is involved in various tasks, encompassing providing first aid, participating in rescue and evacuation operations.

component_details.title: Mapping of NS capacities
component_details.description: A list of the NS capacities including HR (staff, response teams and volunteers) and equipment that are available for disaster/crisis response. Teams could include branch and national response teams. This should be defined by technical speciality where relevant.

component_responses.notes: Some of the LRC branches express concerns about their preparedness, citing challenges such as a lack of trained volunteers at critical locations, resource and capability limitations despite volunteer readiness, and uncertainty dependent on the crisis. Collaboration and communication between departments within the branches appear to vary, with some reporting direct communication and coordination, while others note a lack of documentation reflecting the actual level of interventions. Communication with neighboring National Societies also shows that, with limited information available in some branches, highlighting potential areas for improvement in cross-branch collaboration and information exchange within the National Society.

component_details.title: Early Action Mechanisms
component_details.description: Designed to translate warnings into anticipatory actions to help reduce the impact of specific disaster or crisis events. They focus on consolidating available forecasting information and putting procedures in place to ensure that a NS can act ahead of any disaster/crisis. Forecast-based financing is included within the scope of this area.

component_responses.notes: The LRC doesn't have a system for monitoring and issuing early warnings. Branches report that warnings are only received from headquarters after a disaster or crisis has already occurred. Information on early warnings is also sourced through the civil protection mechanism.

component_details.title: Coordination with External Agencies and NGOs
component_details.description: Mechanism that facilitates coordination and collaboration with Non-Governmental Organization (NGO), both local and international NGOs, civil society organizations (CSOs) and United Nations agencies in country.

component_responses.notes:
The NS is an active member of the humanitarian community nationally. At branch level, coordination happens with other actors upon need, when disasters occur. No specific coordination mechanism with other agencies exists.
Nationally, the NS's role as a cluster member is not clear.

component_details.title: Civil Military Relations
component_details.description: Dialogue and interaction with military actors, essential to protect and promote humanitarian principles, avoid competition, minimize inconsistency and, when appropriate, pursue common goals.

component_responses.notes: No relations with the military.

component_details.title: Coordination with local community level responders
component_details.description: Engagement with Community Disaster Response Teams (CDRTs), through training, coordination, and the development of community disaster preparedness and response plans.

component_responses.notes:
Answers between Branch Network FP and DM FP are very divergent. 
Responses from branches show that there are no procedures to manage information between community and branches, nor branches to HQ. The latter is done through phone calls and emails upon need.
Plans are prepared at HQ so they don't include information from communities. The Ukraine crisis was very different because there was no selection of the population. All refugees were supported, and the needs were reported to HQ. 
There are no CDRTs. The NS does not support a community level response system, including for epidemics.

component_details.title: Cooperation with private sector
component_details.description: Mechanism that allows cooperation with private sector that often plays a strong role in response, particularly if there is impact on their staff and businesses. There is often a willingness to donate goods and services. Advance agreements help to expedite response actions.

component_responses.notes:
NS collaborated with private sector for financial and in-kind donations, including for epidemics. There is no evidence of a screening system that happens to select partners and accepting donations while mitigating image and reputational risks. 
The use of the emblem is very well detailed in the RC law, but no details on who observes compliance. 
There are no mechanisms to retain and activate trained volunteers from corporate partners.

component_details.title: Coordination with Movement
component_details.description: Mechanisms that facilitate the coordination with ICRC, IFRC, and PNS in-country.

component_responses.epi_considerations: No
component_responses.notes:
Partners who want to implement in the country do coordinate with the NS, however this point was marked as insufficient by DM, leadership, Communications and law.
Branches share information with HQ orally, by phone or by mail. There are no regular exchanges with neighboring NSs or coordination mechanisms. This is done upon need. 
When plans are prepared and international assistance is accepted, DM follows a framework to use assistance and report in collaboration with IFRC, except for medical teams.

component_details.title: Coordination with authorities
component_details.description: Mechanism that facilitates coordination and cooperation with local and national authorities. It is connected to the NS auxiliary role for humanitarian assistance.

component_responses.notes:
HQ teams see the collaboration with authorities as a strength whereas branches mention some challenges. 
HQ is formally part of the national humanitarian coordination system however at local level, coordination was difficult during the Ukraine crisis. This might be addressed by the local response SOPs in the future (with no evidence on their efficiency yet). Coordination mechanisms don't exist. 
Most branches have no information on the capacity of authorities, including for epidemics. One branch was able to get a warehouse thanks to the good relation with local authorities. A cooperation agreement was developed with authorities for information sharing and implementing it might facilitate the collaboration. 
RC's assets are the state's and to whether branches were able to ensure independence, some branches answered ""difficult"". 
For epidemics, the NS has clearly defined guidance for the use of the emblem by non-RCRC medical teams in the RC law.
NS is not part of a National Risk Communication and Community Engagement (RCCE) working group.

component_details.title: Safety and security management
component_details.description: Addresses policy and procedures to ensure the safety of staff and volunteers. This include awareness, effective recruitment, training and management processes in place to ensure that personnel are capable of undertaking the roles demanded of them (from NS operational, management and leaders) according to the Stay Safe (IFRC) and Safer Access (ICRC). Based on safer access framework, including concepts of access, perception, identification and acceptance, and protection and violence prevention.

component_responses.epi_considerations: Yes
component_responses.notes:
Safety and security measures are implemented at local and national level for specific hazards and situations: specific briefings, use of PPE’s. However, the security measures don’t appear to be systematically part of planning.
There is no indication the NS is implementing Movement’s security frameworks such as ICRC’s Safer Access or IFRC’s Stay Safe; nor that specific security training are provided.
Volunteer policy indicates volunteers are provided insurance and equipment to work. Documents provided do not provide additional information regarding the monitoring and management of volunteer security in the field such as security and safety issues reporting lines.

component_details.title: Operations Monitoring, Evaluation, Reporting and Learning
component_details.description: The PMERL is designed to implement a results-based planning, monitoring and evaluation system that provides an evidence base of NS performance, including relevance, efficiency, effectiveness, sustainability and impact. A reliable and trusted organization is accountable, providing transparent and timely information and building systems to strengthen data collection and reporting. It is data-driven, analytical and results-based.

component_responses.epi_considerations: No
component_responses.notes:
A PMER focal point exists at HQ level, however it is not visible in the Org. Charts provided. The function is not available in branches. 
Efficiency and timeliness of reporting are highlighted and seem to meet project-based requirements. There is no evidence of the implementation of a systematic M&E framework
Lessons learnt practices are reported as a systematic lessons-learnt capture and learning mechanisms by both HQ and branches.

component_details.title: Finance and Admin policy and emergency procedures
component_details.description: Overall budgeting, accounting, treasury, assets, financial reporting and financial services operations. it also includes the efficient delivery , cost effective and timely services to the NS. Pre-approved, auditable, expedited procedures that allow for flexibility during a disaster/crisis. These must meet transparency, oversight and accountability standards. Procedures may include faster approval processes, fewer signatures, different authority levels. The Emergency Procedures are activated for a specific period of time.

component_responses.epi_considerations: No
component_responses.notes:
Accounting and finance management appear to be centralised in HQ and is not managed at branch level.
The NS counts with a finance/accounting department applying approved and compliant accounting practices. Control and transparency measures are in place. There is no indication these mechanisms are also implemented at branch level.
There are no special and swift procedures or processes aimed at managing finance during emergency operations.

component_details.title: Information and Communication Technology (ICT)
component_details.description: Refers to technologies that provide access to information through telecommunications. This includes the Internet, wireless networks, mobile phones, radios and other communication mediums.

component_responses.notes:
There is a wide use of personal cell phones across the NS for communication; LRC does not provide cell phones. Condition for use in emergency context is not explicit.
Emergency contact lists are available in local procedures and plans for engagement with municipalities.
Internet connection (although sometimes slow) is available in HQ and branches. Wifi on the field is provided by companies as a donation when needed (without written agreement).
There is no official channel for the use of the radio. Hand radios exists, but no radios in cars.

A HQ Logistics position exist under Network Manager. The function doesn’t seem to exist at branch level. Logistics training of volunteer recently started in 2023.
Emergency items are prepositioned across the country for emergency response purpose. Standards of NFI is unknown

There is no evidence of existing procedure for the management of national and international supply chain: import of goods, management of taxes and duties, relationship with broker and transporters, request of equipment from branch to HQ

No procurement procedure provided among documents
Need to be discussed

Vehicles are insured and have the necessary safety and security equipment on board. The use of logbooks and maintenance procedures do not appear to be generalized. Several branches report not having vehicles available locally
There is no evidence of the existence of fleet management procedures, which would include provisions for management of owned fleet, rental and training of drivers

LOGISTICS MANAGEMENT: A HQ Logistics position exist under Network Manager. The function doesn’t seem to exist at branch level. Logistics training of volunteer recently started in 2023.
Emergency items are prepositioned across the country for emergency response purpose. Standards of NFI is unknown.
SUPPLY CHAIN MANAGEMENT: There is no evidence of existing procedure for the management of national and international supply chain: import of goods, management of taxes and duties, relationship with broker and transporters, request of equipment from branch to HQ
PROCUREMENT: No procurement procedure provided among documents. Need to be discussed
FLEET AND TRANSPORTATION MANAGEMENT: Vehicles are insured and have the necessary safety and security equipment on board. The use of logbooks and maintenance procedures do not appear to be generalized. Several branches report not having vehicles available locally. There is no evidence of the existence of fleet management procedures, which would include provisions for management of owned fleet, rental and training of drivers
WAREHOUSE AND STOCK MANAGEMENT: Some volunteers are trained to warehouse and stock management, procedures are not available. Regarding the Warehouses provided on a donation and temporary basis, there is no mention of existing agreement

component_details.title: Staff and volunteer management
component_details.description: Well-functioning staff and volunteer management systems and practices allow for effective recruitment, supervision, support and encouragement of staff and volunteers.

component_responses.notes:
The volunteer policy sets the basis for management of volunteers including principles for training, equipment, insurance and selection of interest. The policy is not implemented and the database is not used. 
Volunteers are provided with necessary ID and equipment. Engagement of volunteers in emergency is not usually framed using ToRs. Basic training is not provided to volunteers systematically. Volunteers can be engaged in areas of interest, not necessarily in areas that require preexisting skills. The management of spontaneous volunteers is done, but procedures don’t exist for all types of volunteers (active, inactive like those of the private sector, spontaneous, etc).
PSS support to staff and volunteers is available.

component_details.title: Communication in emergencies
component_details.description: Incorporates a system of public messaging to enable the NS to share timely, accurate information before, during, and after a disaster or crisis.

component_responses.epi_considerations: No
component_responses.notes:
Focal points and spokespersons are clearly identified at headquarters, and standards and templates are available but branches don’t follow them.
The SN reports a high use of social media in their communication however, action does not look at enhancing accountability to the public and affected populations, and is not bound by a NS-wide policy on the use of social media.
Emergency key messaging and communication doesn’t count with a specific emergency procedure nor SOPs. There is no reported capacity to track negative media and respond accordingly.
Communication in emergencies is not used for advocacy purpose.

component_details.title: Resource Mobilisation
component_details.description: A documented strategy for raising domestic funds from the government, private sector, general public and other in-country actors to support the national society’s response. This would include allocation of responsibilities, practical mechanisms for accepting funds and for being accountable on funds.

component_responses.epi_considerations: No
component_responses.notes:
NS has a resource mobilisation FP and a bank account to receive donations.
It has a list of regular donors from the private sectors however no agreements of collaboration and fundraising that take into consideration the needs of a response at different scales.
There is no resource mobilisation strategy that looks into funding preparedness, local resource mobilisation in highly vulnerable areas and looks into establishing a national emergency fund with criteria for proper use.
There is a guidance on the accepted donations however it doesn't cover the analysis on reputational risks.
Changes in the use of funds is communicated upon need within teams and with partners.

component_details.title: Quality and accountability
component_details.description: Describes the essential elements of principled, accountable, and high-quality humanitarian action. The RCRC Movement provides support to the most vulnerable people in line with the Sphere and CHS standards, Code of Conduct for the RCRC Movement and NGOS in Disaster Relief and the Code for Good Partnership of the RCRC Movement, Gender & Diversity, inclusion and protection, BPI/ Do no harm, context-sensitive analysis, violence prevention, accountability to affected population and disability considerations, Community engagement and accountability (CEA).

component_responses.notes:
La Sociedad Nacional (SN) cuenta con una estrategia, políticas y procedimientos para la implementación del enfoque de Participación Comunitaria y Rendición de Cuentas (CEA) en emergencias. Dispone de 24 puntos focales distribuidos en las juntas provinciales, de los cuales 7 son personal remunerado y el resto voluntarios.

La CRE ha desarrollado un plan de CEA con procedimientos y plantillas estándar que incluyen encuestas de satisfacción, mecanismos de retroalimentación y reclamo mediante buzones físicos, formularios digitales, correo electrónico, código QR, la herramienta Cruz Roja Escúchame y un chatbot. Estas herramientas permiten registrar, remitir, responder y monitorear inquietudes y solicitudes de las comunidades, garantizando respuestas adecuadas y oportunas.

La organización ha capacitado a los puntos focales de CEA en la sede central y en las juntas provinciales, fortaleciendo sus habilidades para asegurar una respuesta humanitaria efectiva, centrada en las personas y construida junto con la comunidad. Este proceso incluye evaluaciones de necesidades (EVIN), planificación conjunta, implementación colaborativa y monitoreo participativo, utilizando espacios de diálogo, grupos focales y encuestas.

En materia de protección, la CRE cuenta con una Política de Integridad, Género y Protección (IGP), aprobada en mayo de 2024, basada en el modelo de la IFRC e incluyendo un apartado de protección infantil. Asimismo, aplica el Plan Nacional de Preparación y Respuesta (PNPR), que integra el enfoque de Protección, Género e Inclusión (PGI) y asegura la protección de grupos vulnerables conforme a las Normas Esfera, la Norma Humanitaria Esencial y las Directrices del IASC.

Actualmente, la CRE trabaja con la Política de Protección contra la Explotación y el Abuso Sexual de la IFRC, mientras avanza en la aprobación de su propia política nacional. Estas normas y políticas fortalecen los servicios especializados, como espacios seguros para la niñez, apoyo a menores no acompañados y separados, prevención de violencia sexual y de género, apoyo psicosocial, restablecimiento del contacto entre familiares y accesibilidad de instalaciones e información.

Además, la CRE promueve las normas mínimas de Dignidad, Acceso y Seguridad (DAF), con cursos e-learning para voluntarios, y aplica las Normas Mínimas de Género y Diversidad en programas motivados por emergencias, garantizando equidad e inclusión. Todos los planes y procedimientos están diseñados bajo el principio de "no hacer daño", mediante evaluaciones de riesgos y medidas preventivas que eviten impactos sociales, económicos y ambientales adversos.

Finalmente, la SN cuenta con herramientas complementarias en proceso de aprobación y un checklist verificable 2025 que respalda la aplicación práctica del enfoque CEA en todas sus actividades y programas.
